Could ‘Rubber Soul’ Be the Best Beatles Album? (Yes)

Tanggal: 14 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.rollingstone.com/music/music-features/rubber-soul-best-beatles-album-1235657869/

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, fall is always rubber soul season. The Beatles’ 1965 masterpiece has always been autumn-coded, with its bristling guitars, wistful vocals, pensive lyrics. Their most emotional album. Their wittiest. Their moodiest. But this fall, Rubber Soul has been in the air even more than usual, because of the phenomenal new Special Edition, which gets you up close with John, Paul, George, and Ringo like never before. Their best.

Sebagaimana diketahui, so what is it that makes rubber soul the beatles’ best album? it’s a loaded question, but for some of us, there’s a correct answer, and it’s simple: it all comes down to the singing. In addition to everything else it is, Rubber Soul is the best place to hear John, Paul, George, and Ringo sing together. It’s four boys telling their stories out loud—you can hear them puzzling out the tales as they sing, bouncing ideas off each other, daring each other to dig a little deeper.

Diungkapkan bahwa over the decades, each era chooses its own beatles album to deify as the ultimate fabs masterpiece. It would be diplomatic and civilized to say that all these albums are equally great…but this will never do, because we all take our own personal Beatles so seriously, and you’d have to be some kind of Mr. In the vinyl era, it was Sgt. Pepper; the CD era chose Revolver; the streaming era has anointed Abbey Road. Mustard to pretend you don’t have a favorite, and for me, that’s always been Rubber Soul.

Berdasarkan laporan, the beatles had to bash out this album in a hurry, in october 1965, to rush some product into the shops in time for christmas. But they had a phenomenal hot streak. They wrote seven of the songs in a week, pushing the deadline right down to the final hours. (Or should we say, it once had them?) Even the quickies have soul — like “Michelle,” a trifle Paul wrote in his teens for the specific purpose of wooing Liverpool art-student girls by pretending to be French.

Sebagaimana diketahui, but the thing that makes rubber soul stand out, head and moptops above the rest, is the singing, with these four boys mingling their voices, each sha-la-la and each na-na-na, each in-my-life and no-i-wouldn’t so charged with raw emotion. Their voices were changing from boys to men — Ringo and John were 25, Paul 23, George 22 — and you can hear their irresistible excitement that they can now emote as the world-weary men they always aspired to be. Because his groovy mod wife Pattie Boyd bought him a thesaurus, hoping it would help him write some eloquent love songs to tell the world about her. Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the lads were cranking around the clock to get rubber soul finished. Martin, who went into the studio early, played his composed solo at half-speed on piano, sped it up to fit the tempo, then played it for the lads’ approval. Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the pace was set right on the first day at abbey road, when john brought in two songs, from opposite sides of the genius spectrum: “norwegian wood,” a candidly introspective tale of getting outmaneuvered by a smarter operator, and “run for your life,” a cheap elvis joke that john somehow turned into one of his saddest, loneliest, most self-loathing vocals. “Run for Your Life” is the kind of song you’d bring to the studio if you scared yourself with how vulnerable you got in “Norwegian Wood. ”.

John was a recluse in his mansion, totally dependent on the Beatles as his only friends. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa but they didn’t laugh. (Rubber Soul is the place to start appreciating Paul’s underrated generosity as a team player; you don’t even notice him in “Norwegian Wood” or “If I Needed Someone,” until you do, but that’s when you realize how selflessly he’s elevating his fellow Beatles’ songs, and how bravely they wrote when they knew they could count on Paul covering their asses. Berdasarkan laporan, there are no happy endings on the album — it’s the first beatles album where none of the songs have “love” in the title, even though there’s a song about the word “love. Diungkapkan bahwa on the final night of the sessions, they still needed two more songs to finish the album. ” You can hear the strain in their throats — you can also hear them revel in it. So they showed up with two of their best: John’s “Girl” and Paul’s “You Won’t See Me. But all over Rubber Soul, you hear the Beatles listen to each other, openly imitating each other. John was eager to claim it for himself, while vacillating on how much Paul contributed. Sebagaimana diketahui, as always, whichever beatles are singing, you can hear their drummer listen to them and support them. “I don’t play all over them. The team behind I Play Rocky found themselves time-traveling 50 years into the past to capture the essence of the story of how an unknown Sylvester Stallone wrote and starred in Rocky, the blockbuster hit of 1976.

Along with fight training and physical conditioning, star Anthony Ippolito immersed himself in studying Stallone’s experience for months until he finally got to hear from the source himself.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “i got to speak to stallone about a month before we started, which was really cool,” ippolito explained during deadline’s contenders film los angeles panel saturday. “But I was, as you can imagine, a little nervous going into that conversation as I had already done a great deal of my own research, but there’s nothing that compares to being able to speak with him directly. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “i felt privileged to be able to hear 50 years later, this crystallized version of him describing his circumstances at the time and him falling in love with writing and just all of these negotiations and how everything panned out for him and how it feels to him, him reflecting on it,” the actor added. “It was really, really awesome. ” Watch on Deadline.

Director Peter Farrelly found that making the crowd-pleasing underdog tale was just as much of an uphill battle as Stallone’s bid to see Rocky make it to the screen.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “every movie’s tough. We shot this in 34 days. “And this one fell apart a bunch getting this made. I’ve never had an easy one, that’s for sure,” Farrelly said. And there was one time, the budget was low too. We had to make it look like the 1970s. And this took us a year and a half and it fell apart three times in the middle of it. They shot Rocky in 28, but they had the advantage of shooting during the 1970s. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “and they kept cutting the budget, cutting the budget,” farrelly added. I’m not getting anything. “And one day I just said, ‘Fuck it. And [Anthony] has been getting his face punched in for a year learning how to box. ’ And then I thought of this guy and that guy. And I thought this is Peter’s masterpiece, Peter Gamble, and I can’t quit on that. But yeah, it’s hard to get a movie made. I don’t need this shit. This is brutal. I’m not getting paid. And it just kept me going. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, writer gamble revealed he found inspiration in the whirlwind three-day marathon in which stallone wrote rocky’s original screenplay. “I said, “Okay, let me just embrace what Stallone did. “And my first draft took about two weeks to write and only working in the mornings got something in the afternoon. Let me see how fast I can write this,” said Gamble. And it changed how I wrote. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “what i found was that so often we’re sitting here trying to make every word on the page great,” gamble explained. And when you get yourself out of the way and you just take these leaps and just dive into something, sometimes you write 15 pages in a day and then you get nine great pages and then you got modeling clay for those bad pages you can work with to make better the next day. “I’d get five great pages just messing with everything. ”.

#685. ‘The Good Daughter’ Stars Rose Byrne and Meghann Fahy on Playing Sisters With Secrets and That Twisty Killer Ending

📅 14 Nov 2026

‘The Good Daughter’ Stars Rose Byrne and Meghann Fahy on Playing Sisters With Secrets and That Twisty Killer Ending

Tanggal: 14 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://variety.com/2026/tv/news/the-good-daughter-spoilers-rose-byrne-meghann-fahy-season-finale-1236945641/

SPOILER ALERT: This interview contains major spoilers from “The Good Daughter,” now streaming on Peacock.

For Sam and Charlie Quinn, the estranged sisters played by Rose Byrne and Meghann Fahy in “The Good Daughter,” the truth was always going to set them free.

Sebagaimana diketahui, adapted by author karin slaughter from her own bestselling novel of the same name, the six-episode peacock series gradually unravels a southern gothic family mystery. More than 20 years earlier, two masked gunmen broke into the Quinns’ rural Georgia home, murdering their mother, Gamma (Olivia Williams), and leaving both sisters with life-altering injuries. Rather than bonding them, the tragedy and a subsequent web of secrets drove the girls apart, culminating in a bitter falling-out a decade ago despite their shared career path. While Sam built a lucrative career in patent law in New York City, Charlie followed in her father Rusty’s (Brendan Gleeson) footsteps to practice criminal defense law in their shady fictional hometown of Pikeville.

Berdasarkan laporan, but when charlie witnesses a tragic school shooting that leaves principal douglas pinkman (kovar mcclure) and a young student dead, sam is pulled back to her old stomping grounds after rusty is badly injured taking the suspect’s case. Forced to step in for her father despite not having very much experience as a defense attorney, Sam reluctantly agrees to represent Kelly Wilson (Shayna Benardo), the pregnant teen who allegedly confessed to killing her principal and a much younger student.

Sebagaimana diketahui, over the course of the season, with the help of charlie and her estranged husband ben (michael dorman), sam discovers that kelly was merely a pawn used by judith (paula malcomson), the kind teacher who looked after charlie following gamma’s death. Upon discovering her husband Douglas had abused and impregnated Kelly — and expected them all to raise the child together — Judith manipulated the unstable teen into bringing a gun to school, planning to kill Douglas and blame Kelly. But when Kelly hesitated to shoot, Judith seized the weapon, executing Douglas and accidentally killing another kid in the ensuing struggle.

Sebagaimana diketahui, at the same time, the shooting resurfaces old memories for both quinn sisters. As Sam digs deeper into the past, the truth of that tragic day finally comes to light: Charlie had been sexually assaulted by Zach Culpepper — one of Rusty’s most dangerous clients who owed him thousands in legal bills — and the brutal home invasion that resulted in Gamma’s murder had been orchestrated by Mason “Huck” Huckabee (Jake McDorman), a man with whom Charlie had a one-night stand right before the school shooting in the first episode.

Sebagaimana diketahui, though charlie had forced rusty to keep her assault a secret for decades, confronting these buried traumas finally breaks down the walls threatening charlie’s relationship with sam — and her marriage to ben. “It’s always really hard when we have things that we don’t like about ourselves, or things that we haven’t confronted about ourselves,” Fahy tells Variety. “That can be a really hard thing to communicate to someone else because when you operate out of a place of hurt, you do close yourself off from the people that you actually want to be closest to. I think that is true for the sisters and the beginning of the series, and then you have the payoff of watching them come through the other side of that and come back together. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, in the conversation below, conducted separately, byrne (also an executive producer) and fahy discuss the “corrosive” nature of family secrets, why they believe sam and charlie are ultimately more alike than different — and whether that cathartic finale is truly the last we’ve seen of the quinn sisters onscreen together. Related Stories 'Hold Onto Me' Director Myrsini Aristidou Kicks Off Historic Oscar Campaign for Sundance Audience Award Winner: 'I Really Feel Like We're Underdogs'.

Diungkapkan bahwa rose byrne: the estrangement and the origin story of sam returning home to face her personal truths was really intriguing. I thought the nature of truth was also really interesting — [with] one person’s perspective then shifting to another and the tension of that, and the great suspenseful nature of the story. She had such fury and anger, which she speaks about in the show and in the book a lot, but [I was interested in] her coming to terms with her anger toward her father and his decisions that led them to this tragedy they find themselves in. That genre has always been really fun to me, and something I hadn’t done for a long time, so it was fun to revisit those tropes.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, meghann fahy: ultimately, the thing that really attracted me to the show is that, when you zoom out, it really is the story of confronting your grief and your trauma and the things that keep us at an arm’s length from the people that we love. It tells a story of coming out on the other side of that stronger and living more of a connected existence, and then drawing the people that you love closer to you as a result of having really faced yourself.

Berdasarkan laporan, byrne: sam’s driven very much by her mother and her mother’s words of, “you have to leave. ” Her sense of really pushing the daughters to leave to a bigger world, to a better place, to more opportunities, particularly as young women — I think that is her drive. She’s extremely bright; she’s very ambitious. This town is corrupt. It’s run by these people and you’ve got to get out. It’s rigged. The voice in her head is her mother’s voice, and she’s very much like her mother. I think the only way through life is to leave and to go somewhere where she can see like-minded people and be less oppressed and repressed in this town, which can be pretty challenging and pretty backward.

Diungkapkan bahwa fahy: i don’t think charlie wanted to leave her dad. I think that she wanted to follow in his footsteps in terms of doing the work that she had seen him do for their whole lives, and there’s something really interesting about that because Charlie and Sam obviously suffered in a big way as a result of what he did for a living and how that affected the family. There was something about Charlie that wanted to stay to rewrite the story or to take control of elements of the story that she didn’t feel that she had. And for her, the path to doing that was staying where it all happened.

Sebagaimana diketahui, fahy: karin did a really good job of weaving that in. A lot of Charlie’s behavior, especially as it applies to her husband, Ben — at the beginning of the show, they’re not really together, but you sort of want them to be. But you understand why he is taking a step back, because the fact that she hasn’t processed any of this trauma that he doesn’t even know about is keeping him from really being with her, and it’s keeping her from really letting him in. That undercurrent is there the whole time, so I didn’t feel like I had to do anything special or extra to lace that in, because Karin did such a good job of building it in the relationships. You see Charlie suffering in her relationships, and you find out why much later, but I think if you watched the show from the beginning and you knew that, you would really be able to see that throughline in her and her behavior throughout the series.

Berdasarkan laporan, byrne: i think it’s her disappointment in her sister after what she sacrificed for her. To your point, this secret is so corrosive to their relationship because Sam doesn’t know the truth. Her sister’s behavior is so triggering for Sam and so disappointing and so crushing when their mother had set this example of leaving and escaping, and I think her lack of compassion for her sister really is a great flaw in the character. Obviously, once she finds out the truth, she understands the whole perspective and also her anger. But that is another very specific trait in Sam that is really roadblocking her ability to have compassion and accept that her sister is not her.

Berdasarkan laporan, fahy: the girls were raised in a house that was very intellectually driven. The scenes where you see Gamma teaching them, the way that she spoke to them — I always think it’s so funny when they’re in the store, and she’s giving Sam a lesson on how to really land saying “Fuck!,” and using her breath and stuff like that. That part of how they were raised is something that they both actually really like.

Sebagaimana diketahui, byrne: sam’s law is patent law, so it’s so dry; it’s so unemotional, and it is so specific. Whereas Charlie’s character, she feels so tied to her father. I think she adores how benign it can be, and she thrives in the specificity of it, in the numbers of it. I think the trauma bond she has with her father and the secret they share — it’s very, very hard for her to leave that, and to leave what they’ve shared together in that sense.

Diungkapkan bahwa fahy: for all of her father’s faults, he protected her when she needed him to. He kept the secret that she asked him to. I think she respected him, and Sam doesn’t in the same way, but then ultimately comes to feel that way about him towards the end.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, byrne: it’s like that great ram dass saying: “if you think you’re enlightened, then go and spend a weekend with your parents. You can think all the things you want about yourself until you’re back in front of whoever consists of your family. There’s just no relationship on Earth like it, and it is so powerful. ” I feel like that speaks really truth to everybody who’s alive and has parents who are alive. I feel like this is a really great examination of that, particularly with Samantha.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, fahy: sam and charlie both wanting to go into the field of law is rooted ultimately in their respect for what they saw their father achieve, regardless of how it ultimately negatively affected everyone in the family and caused their mother to be killed. I know that’s true for Charlie at least. And that’s so awful, but I do think that, ultimately, they really love feeling like they’re helping people. That’s the thing she loves the most about what she does: helping kids that she feels like don’t have anybody else who wants to in the same way that she does.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, fahy: our director, steph green, had found a version of the song that she really, really liked, and she knew that i sang, and she asked if i would be open to covering it. She wanted it to come after Episode 5 because she feels like some of the words, especially in the first verse, could be Charlie singing to Sam. I, of course, was very excited by the idea. I think the way that the episode ends where Charlie’s in the doorway and she’s calling for her sister the way that she did in the first episode — it’s like this callback to her being a child and standing in that same spot right before the worst thing happened. I like that the version that we did is a little bit haunting, a little bit stripped down.

Sebagaimana diketahui, byrne: karin slaughter is so interesting, because she’s so ahead of the reader. She’s so ahead of her audience with her plots, but I do feel like Sam is that role too, and she’s a little bit ahead of the audience in her mind about what’s happening and she’s piecing it all together faster than everybody else. That was something I talked about a lot with Karin, so I tried to remember that in those scenes. I think she intuitively already knows all of this, and it’s catching up in real time as we’re watching it.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, fahy: what’s so interesting about the show is it’s so nuanced in terms of who did what, who is guilty of what, and who was wrong, because charlie did accuse the wrong person [daniel] of assaulting her — and that person was killed. But also, she was a kid, and she was confused, and she only had the information that was in front of her. So in the moment that she realizes that, she feels incredibly guilty for having essentially been responsible for someone losing their life. I think that really speaks to the way that we process trauma. Sometimes, it’s really hard to zoom out and look at things from a different point of view when all you can feel is the trauma that your body is still in fight or flight.

Berdasarkan laporan, she’s unraveling all of that, feeling the guilt of that, feeling the anger of having been intimate with huck, who is now a part of the worst day of her life. Ultimately, I think that Charlie finding out all of this is the thing that breaks her open, that ultimately allows her to come face to face with her truth. That is part of the catalyst to her being able to share that with Ben, which is what she needed to do so that they could really be together in a real way.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, byrne: they say in the birth order, the eldest daughter is such a huge responsibility in a family, especially for a young girl. So to see her sister go through this trauma again and relive it again in front of her is really harrowing and makes her so wildly furious that I feel like that is another very specific thing she’s going through.

Sebagaimana diketahui, fahy: judith was there the day that charlie was assaulted in the woods. For Charlie, feeling safe with anybody is a tall order. Charlie shows up to her door, and Judith takes her in. After that, Judith continues to take care of her in school. She sticks up for Charlie when she’s being bullied. So for her to come to the realization that a person that she really trusted and felt looked after by could have done something so horrible — I think she was a cocktail of emotions, but there was a real, real sadness and heartbreak in there when Charlie realized that Judith really was the one who orchestrated the killings.

Berdasarkan laporan, byrne: that’s so cool. I didn’t know that.

Diungkapkan bahwa fahy: because the novel is so beautifully written, it felt complete to me — and the show felt complete to me, too. I don’t think I ever really pictured it as being ongoing. But that being said, Charlie is one of my most cherished characters that I’ve ever been able to play, so she’ll stay with me for a long time. I would be very curious to know what she would be getting up to and what her life would be like after having gone through everything that she goes through.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, byrne: we felt it was pretty contained within the pages of what we were doing, but i’ve also been around so long that now i don’t know what anywhere will lead to anywhere anymore. So “anything can happen” is really my motto now in this business, because you just never know how things will shake out. I always try to keep an open mind, but it feels like the story we were meant to tell was the one we’ve told.

Diungkapkan bahwa byrne: maybe they go to a private island and have a mojito. They deserve a drink! They should talk about the weather for a few weeks, and keep it really light. Not the news — just the weather, what they’re going to have for dinner. I’m being silly, but I’m kind of not. That’s what I would like: for them to be a little bored, a little quiet, just relaxed.

Sebagaimana diketahui, fahy: i hope that charlie finds real comfort and peace. I think we don’t show a lot of relationships like Charlie and Ben where the person is given space to figure themselves out, and Ben’s not punishing her for it. Another thing that I really, really love about the character of Ben, played by Michael Dorman — we were so lucky to have him because his energy is so unique and loving and understanding. He’s loving her through it while also having his own boundary.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, to see them come back together after having given each other that space, and for him to really hold all of charlie’s truth and say, “i’m still here,” is so hopeful and nice. Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, in 1970, she co-founded disabled in action, a grassroots advocacy organization, and went on to become a leading voice in the independent living movement. Her activism helped pave the way for landmark legislation including the Individuals with Disabilities Education Act and the Americans with Disabilities Act. Audacious, confident, and fiercely determined, Heumann became known as the “mother of the disability rights movement,” helping to transform disability from a matter of charity into a question of civil rights.

I sat by the camera and interviewed them, sometimes as their characters and sometimes as themselves. ”.

Now get in the edit. It was simply the beginning of dismantling the next obstacle.

Sebagaimana diketahui, with the novel being compared most consistently to the reacher franchise, kill current has echoes of the lee child series in its larger story, and has also been compared to john le carré's work, as well. While Hendricks isn't a carbon copy of Jack Reacher, he definitely has many of the same qualities as the wandering hero, but the technological focus of the series provides a different element to the story. With a planned series in the works, Kill Current is just the opening of what will likely be a far longer story, which could be great for the adaptation side of the franchise.

Diungkapkan bahwa as someone who's known to take his work seriously, knowing that reeves is behind the adaptation of kill current is an exciting step in the right direction. As the first major project from Reeves production company, Two Dragonflies, it's clear that Reeves' involvement in the adaptation is more than just a face for the film. While it was only announced in September 2026, Kill Current's adaptation has already been pushed into development, which means there's a great chance it comes to fruition. Instead, being on the development side, Reeves is proving that he's bringing his past experiences to the universe in order to create a franchise.

Sebagaimana diketahui, for readers looking for a new thriller series to dive into on the ground floor, kill current should be a viable option, especially considering that there's already movement on a film adaptation. With Reeves working on the adaptation in a more extensive way and the novel itself receiving praise as the first a hopefully successful series, Kill Current is prepared to be the next action thriller to reach Reacher and John Wick levels of hype.

Sebagaimana diketahui, this was an alteration made to "blade runner" after scott's original cut was not well-received by test audiences. Scott's intended ending involved a weirdly symbolic image of a character examining a piece of origami folded into a unicorn, and Rick Deckard (Harrison Ford) walking into an elevator with the replicant Rachael (Sean Young). The ending was ambiguous and downbeat, in the spirit of film noir.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, scott recalled the experience in a 2015 interview with the hollywood reporter, saying that an unnamed investor wanted him to tack on a happy ending where rick and rachel drive off into the woods together. In the happy ending, Rick talks in voiceover about how Rachel is a special kind of replicant who can live indefinitely. Harrison Ford is on record about how much he hates that voiceover.

There have been many cuts of "Blade Runner" over the years, and Scott has been very frank about how much he dislikes the "happy ending" that was mandated to him.

And he said, 'We have to test this with an uplifting ending, where they will go off into the wilderness together. ' I said, 'Well if they go off into a beautiful wilderness, why do they live in this dystopian environment?'".

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, scott then said he asked stanley kubrick for a little of that lovely woodsy footage he shot for "the shining" and inserted it into "blade runner. " He continued:.

Diungkapkan bahwa "by then i had talked to stanley a few times. I said, 'I know you shot the hell out of 'The Shining,' can I have some of the stuff?' So at the end of the film in 'Blade Runner,' that's Stanley Kubrick's footage. ".

#694. 32 Years Later, Star Trek's Most Important Movie Is Officially Free on Streaming

📅 14 Nov 2026

32 Years Later, Star Trek's Most Important Movie Is Officially Free on Streaming

Tanggal: 14 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.polygon.com/star-trek-generations-streaming-free-november-2026/

Sebagaimana diketahui, there are few things star trek fans love more than a good crossover. Bringing together characters from different eras of the franchise is practically guaranteed to generate excitement, particularly when those characters happen to be two of Starfleet's most legendary captains. But what happens when the movie designed to unite them doesn't quite live up to expectations?.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, released in 1994 and now streaming free on pluto tv, star trek: generations brought captain james t. The result was a movie that divided fans, delivered one of the franchise's most controversial deaths, and destroyed one of television's most beloved starships. Kirk (William Shatner) and Captain Jean-Luc Picard (Patrick Stewart) together on the big screen for the first and only time. Yet more than three decades later, Generations deserves another look, particularly for what it has to say about growing older, accepting loss, and knowing when it's time to move on.

Berdasarkan laporan, the film opens with kirk, montgomery scott (james doohan), and pavel chekov (walter koenig) attending the maiden voyage of the enterprise-b. Kirk is retired, although it's obvious he hasn't entirely adjusted to life outside the captain's chair.

Sebagaimana diketahui, when kirk discovers that the ship's helmsman is demora sulu (jacqueline kim), daughter of his former crewmate hikaru sulu (george takei), he's surprised his old friend found time to start a family. Scotty reminds him of something Kirk himself has always said: If something is important, you make the time.

Sebagaimana diketahui, it's a seemingly insignificant exchange that establishes one of the movie's central themes. Kirk has spent his life exploring the galaxy, but what has he missed along the way? He's saved countless lives and made history, yet he's struggling to find purpose without the Enterprise.

Berdasarkan laporan, decades later, picard faces his own reckoning with mortality after learning that his brother robert and nephew rené have died in a fire. The tragedy leaves him confronting the possibility that his family line will end with him, along with the realization that the life he chose came at the expense of another he might have had.

Sebagaimana diketahui, both captains eventually find themselves inside the nexus, a mysterious energy ribbon that offers its inhabitants a seemingly perfect existence. For Picard, that means experiencing the family life he never had. Kirk finds himself back in a peaceful home, with the opportunity to reconnect with a woman from his past. Perhaps Edith Keeler?.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the temptation is understandable. Who wouldn't want the chance to revisit a happier moment or correct a regret? But Generations makes the case that a meaningful life isn't necessarily a perfect one. Sometimes it's the choices we make, and the sacrifices that come with them, that give our lives purpose.

Diungkapkan bahwa none of this means generations is without problems. Tolian Soran (Malcolm McDowell), wants to return to the Nexus so badly he's willing to destroy entire star systems to make it happen. The movie's villain, Dr. Far from it. While McDowell brings considerable menace to the role, Soran never quite becomes the memorable antagonist the story needs.

Diungkapkan bahwa then there's kirk's death, which remains one of the most debated moments in star trek history. After surviving Klingons, Romulans, Khan, and countless other threats, the legendary captain meets his end beneath a collapsing bridge. For a character who spent decades boldly going where no one had gone before, it's not exactly the grand farewell many fans imagined. And yet there's plenty here to appreciate.

Sebagaimana diketahui, stewart delivers some of his finest work as picard struggles with grief, particularly during a quiet conversation with counselor deanna troi (marina sirtis). The destruction of the Enterprise-D is also genuinely shocking, especially for viewers who spent seven seasons watching the ship become almost as much a character as the people aboard it.

There's also the introduction of Data's (Brent Spiner) emotion chip, which provides some welcome humor, even if the movie occasionally leans a little too heavily into the android's newfound feelings.

Diungkapkan bahwa most importantly, shatner and stewart make the film's long-awaited meeting worthwhile. Instead, they feature two captains reflecting on what it means to make a difference. Their scenes together aren't built around elaborate action sequences or clever one-liners. It's a quieter approach than some viewers might have expected, but one that feels appropriate for these characters.

Berdasarkan laporan, beyond its story, generations occupies a unique place in star trek history. It was the franchise's first theatrical film built around the cast of Star Trek: The Next Generation, arriving just months after the television series concluded its seven-season run.

Sebagaimana diketahui, for years, kirk and his crew had been the faces of star trek on the big screen. Kirk begins the film as a celebrated former captain watching a new Enterprise depart without him. Now it was Picard's turn. The movie makes that transition literal. By the conclusion, he's helping Picard save millions of lives and making one final sacrifice before leaving the future in another captain's hands.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the destruction of the enterprise-d reinforces that transition. The ship that carried Picard and his crew through seven seasons of television adventures is gone, clearing the way for a new chapter. The Next Generation cast would return in three more films, beginning with 1996's Star Trek: First Contact.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, there's something fitting about a movie so concerned with the passage of time serving as the bridge between two eras of star trek. The franchise was changing, just as its characters were learning to accept change in their own lives.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, generations may not be the best star trek movie, but beneath the spectacle, questionable decisions, and collapsing bridges is a thoughtful story about two men who devoted their lives to making a difference. When Kirk gets one last opportunity to do exactly that, he doesn't hesitate. For all the movie's imperfections, it's hard to imagine a more appropriate final choice for the captain of the Enterprise.

Berdasarkan laporan, star trek generations is free to streaming pluto tv. You can also watch it on Paramount Plus.

#696. The 8 Greatest Vampire Books Released Since 'Dracula', Ranked

📅 14 Nov 2026

The 8 Greatest Vampire Books Released Since 'Dracula', Ranked

Tanggal: 14 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://collider.com/best-vampire-books-since-dracula-ranked/

Diungkapkan bahwa the vampire is one of the most enduring monsters in fiction, shifting in step with the times. Supernatural bloodsuckers have existed in folklore for centuries, but they took their core modern form in Bram Stoker's seminal Dracula back in 1897. Since then, countless writers have built on, tweaked, or subverted those ideas over the last 129 years.

Diungkapkan bahwa this list looks at the finest of those books released in the wake of dracula, from the blockbuster dark fantasy of empire of the vampire to the small-town horror of salem's lot. Some of the titles below retain the traditional Gothic atmosphere, while others incorporate sci-fi, psychological horror, historical fiction, or character study.

Berdasarkan laporan, "too much hate will burn a man to cinders. " Empire of the Vampire is a great hybrid of vampire tropes and epic fantasy, courtesy of Jay Kristoff, author of Nevernight and The Lotus War. The story takes place in a high fantasy world decades after a mysterious catastrophe known as Daysdeath obscured the sun, allowing vampires to emerge from the shadows and conquer much of human civilization. Its protagonist, Gabriel de León, is a former member of the Silver Order, an organization of warriors trained to hunt the undead.

Berdasarkan laporan, imprisoned by his enemies, gabriel recounts his extraordinary life to a vampire historian, from his upbringing and military exploits to his desperate quest to recover humanity's last hope. The atmosphere is delectably Gothic the whole way through, and elevated by intricate, lovingly crafted worldbuilding. For instance, the different vampire bloodlines all have distinct powers and belief systems.

Diungkapkan bahwa "do you see? i am a vampire. " This book was an important milestone in the development of vampires in popular fiction, even years before the blockbuster movie adaptation. In particular, it broke ground by treating its bloodsuckers as psychologically complex protagonists capable of guilt, desire, existential despair, and perhaps even growth. The plot focuses on Louis de Pointe du Lac, a vampire who tells his life story to a young journalist in modern-day San Francisco.

Diungkapkan bahwa louis is a compelling protagonist. Lestat, meanwhile, embraces immortality with an enthusiasm that both fascinates and horrifies his companion. He struggles with the moral implications of his existence, repeatedly questioning whether his need to consume human blood makes him fundamentally evil. On top of that, the book throws in a powerful sensual and romantic subtext, which would greatly influence the genre going forward.

Diungkapkan bahwa "innocence ain't all it's cracked up to be. This banger from Joe Hill (the mind behind Horns and King Sorrow) follows Victoria McQueen, a young woman who discovers that she has the power to locate lost objects by riding her bicycle across a mysterious covered bridge. " Layered characters and genuine horror are the name of the game here. This unusual talent eventually brings her into conflict with Charlie Manx, a seemingly immortal predator who abducts children and transports them to a nightmarish supernatural realm.

Diungkapkan bahwa manx travels in a sinister rolls-royce wraith, using his vehicle to drain the life from his victims while maintaining his unnatural longevity. NOS4A2 is a fresh riff on vampire mythology. Just like traditional vampires, Manx grows decrepit and weak when he goes too long without feeding, but he consumes souls directly rather than drinking blood, and behaves more like a serial killer from a thriller than one of the alluring yet dangerous vampires of yore.

Berdasarkan laporan, "dusk is the time when men whisper of matters about which they remain silent in the full light of the sun. " This one is a little more obscure, but it has something of a cult following. The main character is Richard Fountain, a brilliant young Cambridge scholar who travels to Greece and becomes tangled up with a mysterious, mesmerizing, dangerous woman named Chriseis. Soon, he'staking part in twisted, sadistic rituals, and his friends, growing concerned, set out in search of him.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, instead of playing that premise as pulp and relying on conventional gothic imagery, the book distinguishes itself through its unusual combination of intellectual sophistication and provocative subject matter, especially for 1960. Doctors Wear Scarlet explores the psychological dimensions of vampirism, leaning hard into obsession, control, forbidden desires, and the darker impulses concealed beneath respectable social masks.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "the world was gone, and he was alone. " This classic greatly influenced both vampire and zombie fiction. Most notably, it was the first vampire story to strip away the magic and make its bloodsuckers the result of a global pandemic, a conceit that pretty much spawned a new subgenre unto itself. At the center of the plot is survivor Robert Neville, who lives alone in a fortified house, spending his days gathering supplies, researching the disease, and hunting the infected.

Berdasarkan laporan, at night, he barricades himself indoors while the vampires gather outside, attempting to lure him into their clutches. Much of the suspense comes from watching Neville's attempts to understand the biological mechanisms behind the creatures' behavior. In this approach, I Am Legend takes the themes of superstition-versus-science even further than Dracula originally did, culminating in a punchy, unforgettable ending that remains subversive and iconic.

Diungkapkan bahwa "some nights the darkness comes down so thick you can almost taste it. " Set in 1857, Fevre Dream follows Abner Marsh, a struggling steamboat captain whose fortunes change when he is hired by a mysterious gentleman named Joshua York. However, Abner becomes increasingly suspicious of Joshua's peculiar habits, particularly his secretive conversations and aversion to sunlight.

Diungkapkan bahwa long before finding mainstream success with a game of thrones, george r. Martin penned one of the richest and most immersive vampire novels of the late 20th century. While some of the plot mechanics are familiar, the backdrop is unique: the action unfolds on boats navigating the Mississippi River in the antebellum era. R. That setting feels really authentic. Not to mention, Martin also hits hard with the themes. For instance, he presents philosophies concerning the relationship between humanity and its supernatural predators.

Sebagaimana diketahui, "to flee is life. " Most readers will be familiar with the brilliant film adaptation, but many won't be aware that Let the Right One In was originally a book. Set in the Stockholm suburb of Blackeberg during the early 1980s, the novel follows Oskar, a bullied twelve-year-old boy whose miserable existence begins changing when he befriends Eli, a mysterious child who has recently moved into his apartment complex. To linger, death. Needless to say, she turns out to be a vampire.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, in contrast to most vampire fiction in the 2000s, let the right one in does not romanticize the monster. Eli's existence is defined by violence and isolation, becoming a mirror to the ordinary people around her, who also struggle with addiction, exploitation, despair, and inner darkness. The relationship between Oskar and Eli forms the heart of the story, developing into a complicated friendship at once tender and deeply unsettling.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "the town knew about darkness. " This book has been described as "Peyton Place meets Dracula", and that's exactly right. Stephen King's sophomore (published) novel is one of his strongest, fusing vampire mythology with realistic small-town drama. It's an ensemble piece, but the central character is Ben Mears, a novelist who returns to the town of Jerusalem's Lot, Maine, hoping to confront traumatic memories from his childhood. However, his arrival coincides with the appearance of two sinister newcomers, Richard Straker and Kurt Barlow.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, soon afterward, residents begin disappearing or exhibiting strange behavior, slowly becoming an army of the undead. He paints a sprawling, convincing portrait of ordinary people, marked by complicated relationships and private resentments. Again, that could easily have become a schlocky penny dreadful, but King makes it vastly more interesting because the community feels real. This meticulous development makes the town's gradual destruction all the more horrifying.

#697. Why Doctor Strange Abandons The Avengers To Join Doctor Doom Explained

📅 14 Nov 2026

Why Doctor Strange Abandons The Avengers To Join Doctor Doom Explained

Tanggal: 14 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://screenrant.com/doctor-strange-join-doom-secret-wars/

Diungkapkan bahwa there's a sensible reason why doctor strange betrays the avengers and becomes doctor doom's right-hand man during the collapse of the marvel multiverse. In Avengers: Age of Ultron, Ultron builds an endless hive-mind swarm of Ultron Sentries designed to evolve alongside him and enlists Wanda and Pietro Maximoff before the twins defect. In The Avengers, Loki weaponizes the Chitauri to invade the Earth, assisted by the brainwashed Hawkeye and Erik Selvig. Every major Avengers antagonist has led an army and a group of devoted lieutenants. When Thanos finally makes his move in Infinity War and Endgame, he brings the Black Order and hordes of Outriders and Chitauri with him.

Sebagaimana diketahui, one of the biggest questions surrounding avengers: doomsday is the identity of doctor doom's acolytes, who seem to draw inspiration from the black swans and black priests of jonathan hickman’s time runs out storyline. While there's a possibility they're Doombots or alternate Victor von Doom variants, close inspection of their masks and cloaks suggests that Doom is secretly leading corrupted or brainwashed variants of MCU magic users. Doctor Strange, Wanda Maximoff, Clea, and Sylvie are the most likely heroes-turned-villains hiding behind the hoods, potentially manipulated into believing that Doom's authoritarian rule is the only way to save a collapsing multiverse from total destruction.

Sebagaimana diketahui, marvel studios inevitably makes significant changes to every major comic book storyline it adapts into live-action, and the plot of time runs out and secret wars is no exception. Just like the exact location of the Infinity Stones ahead of Avengers: Infinity War and the Avengers' method to undo Thanos' Snap ahead of Avengers: Endgame, the mystery behind Doctor Doom's followers might be one of Avengers: Doomsday's biggest points of speculation and one of its biggest twists as well.

Berdasarkan laporan, as the marvel multiverse collapses in jonathan hickman’s secret wars saga, doctor strange realizes that neither the illuminati nor the avengers can prevent the end of all existence. Throughout the preceding Time Runs Out storyline, Strange watches brilliant minds like Reed Richards and Tony Stark exhaust every scientific and ethical option while incursions erase entire realities. Having already abandoned conventional superhero morality by embracing dark blood magic to save his world, Strange ultimately discovers that the omnipotent Beyonders are orchestrating the multiverse's destruction.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, doctor strange uncovers victor von doom’s secret identity as rabum alal, the great destroyer who spent years killing molecule men across parallel worlds before gathering the survivors into a massive bomb to use against the beyonders. Doom embraced the unthinkable role of cosmic executioner to buy creation a fighting chance. So, joining forces with Doom and Molecule Man for a last stand against the Beyonders before the final universes collide, Strange witnesses Owen Reece channel the Ivory Kings' godlike energy into Victor.

Berdasarkan laporan, following doctor doom's creation of battleworld, doctor strange cements his choice to support doom and accepts the role of sheriff strange, willingly partnering with doom so that at least a sliver of humanity survives. Strange knows deep down that Victor is a tyrant whose rule will eventually crumble under his own pride, but he also understands that without Doom’s iron grip, nothing would exist at all. Although Strange's support of God Emperor Doom is a betrayal of his heroic principles, he has no option but to help a ruthless monarch hold the pieces together until a better world can be reborn.

Diungkapkan bahwa as sheriff of battleworld, doctor strange becomes the supreme enforcer and right-hand magistrate of the realm, bearing the exhausting burden of keeping victor von doom’s patchwork reality from tearing itself apart. Whenever rebellions erupt or forbidden memories of the old multiverse resurface, Sheriff Strange arrives to restore stability. Based in Battleworld's Isle of Agamotto, Strange leads the Thor Corps and mediates violent border disputes between rival barons like Sinister, Apocalypse, and Maestro. Besides, Strange also hides the sealed life raft of surviving Earth-616 heroes he discovered years after Battleworld's creation, keeping the mysterious vessel locked away to prevent it from affecting the peace while he outwardly enforces Doom's every decree.

Sebagaimana diketahui, after eight years of enforcing battleworld’s laws, sheriff strange turns against god emperor doom during the explosive climax of jonathan hickman and esad ribić’s secret wars #4. Strange had secretly kept the mysterious Earth-616 life raft hidden inside his Isle of Agamotto sanctum for five years after discovering it, unsure of what lay inside. When a separate raft belonging to the sinister Cabal led by Thanos and the Maker breaches Battleworld, Strange finally has the Earth-616 vessel opened, awakening Reed Richards, Spider-Man, Black Panther, Captain Marvel, Star-Lord, Cyclops, and the Mighty Thor to join him in the fray.

Berdasarkan laporan, the battleworld conflict draws god emperor doom himself down to the battlefield, where the omnipotent ruler kills cyclops and confronts sheriff strange. Then, Strange performs a powerful teleportation spell that scatters Reed Richards, Black Panther, and the rest of the surviving heroes safely across Battleworld’s various domains where they can ignite a coordinated rebellion. Shockingly, after Strange mocks Doom's lingering fear of Richards, God Emperor Doom obliterates Strange on the spot with a single blast, making Strange a martyr whose final spell ensures the downfall of Doom's empire.

Berdasarkan laporan, the mcu captured the spirit of doctor strange’s pragmatic compromise in avengers: infinity war, when he voluntarily handed the time stone over to thanos on titan. Although Strange's decision is now seen as the wise first step in his successful plan to overturn Thanos' Snap and bring half of the universe back to life, it used to seem like an uncharacteristic move from one of the MCU's brightest minds. Just like his Secret Wars counterpart, Benedict Cumberbatch's MCU Strange recognized that outright victory at that moment was impossible and that temporary defeat was the sole pathway to survival.

Berdasarkan laporan, since the mcu has already shown strange willingly hand victory to a tyrant once, avengers: doomsday will likely adapt sheriff strange with a clever twist so the beat doesn't feel repetitive. Instead of having Earth-616 Strange consciously strike another secret bargain with Doctor Doom, the MCU's adaptation of Time Runs Out and Secret Wars could introduce a brainwashed Strange who may have lost an off-screen battle against Doom following the events of Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness. This scenario is more likely, considering the rest of Doctor Doom's acolytes are also likely to be fellow Avengers.

How do you think Avengers: Doomsday will adapt Doctor Strange's allegiance to Doctor Doom?.

Skip Hinnant, ‘The Electric Company’ Actor and Voice of Ralph Bakshi’s ‘Fritz the Cat’ Movies, Dies at 86

Sebagaimana diketahui, actor skip hinnant, best known for his work on the pbs children’s series “the electric company‘ and as the voice of fritz the cat in ralph bakshi’s racy animated films from the 1970s, has died. He was 86.

Sebagaimana diketahui, hinnant’s death was confirmed by his family in an obituary notice published by the new york times. He died Nov. 8 in Denver.

Sebagaimana diketahui, hinnant was active in theater in the 1960s. He was part of the renowned Julius Monk revue “Struts and Frets” in 1963. Kennedy. ” He appeared at the White House Correspondents’ Association dinner in 1962, performing for President John F. Berdasarkan laporan, hinnant was prolific in voice-over work in animation and tv commercials. He was also known for his active involvement with Actors Equity, AFTRA and SAG (before the latter unions merged) from the 1980s through the early 2000s.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, born joseph howard hinnant in 1940, he grew up in chincoteague island, virginia. He was nicknamed Skip by his older sister Jean. The name stuck as his acting career blossomed.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, hinnant was a charter member in 1971 of the cast of pbs’ “the electric company,” a companion daytime series to “sesame street” that sought to help older kids develop critical thinking skills. Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, during the run of “the electric company,” hinnant was recruited by legendary animator ralph bakshi to voice the title character in 1972’s “fritz the cat,” based on the lascivious stoner cat character created by robert crumb. Hinnant attended Yale University, graduating in 1962.

#702. 5 Times Patrick Stewart's Jean-Luc Picard Proved He Was Star Trek's Greatest Captain

📅 14 Nov 2026

5 Times Patrick Stewart's Jean-Luc Picard Proved He Was Star Trek's Greatest Captain

Tanggal: 14 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.slashfilm.com/2314128/times-patrick-stewart-jean-luc-picard-proved-star-trek-greatest-captain/

Diungkapkan bahwa the late, great patrick stewart brought captain picard to life. The captain of the USS Enterprise-D on "Star Trek: The Next Generation" was, on the page, a resolute and principled character, meant to resemble Horatio Hornblower, a note that show creator Gene Roddenberry gave to Stewart during the show's development. Stewart, however — a classically trained actor – drew on several classical and personal sources to properly create Picard, including Hornblower, Shakespeare's King Henry IV, and one Regimental Sergeant Major Alfred Stewart, Patrick's stern and glowering father.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the character emerged not just as stern and authoritative, but also possessed of deeply held values and very, very high standards. Picard feels like the college professor you hope to never disappoint. He's not fatherly, but he can be kind. He trusts the experts around him, and rarely suffers a crisis of confidence. He may be aloof, but that aids his command style; Picard attracts respect through his almost unshakable competence. He knows how to make good decisions quickly, but is always careful to listen to input from his crew. If you are in any position of authority — from a government official to an assistant manager at a Sephora — you can look to Captain Picard for inspiration.

Berdasarkan laporan, all of the above qualities make picard a great captain of a giant space-faring vehicle. There were, however, several times when the already stalwart captain went above and beyond and proved that his command skills were not merely excellent, but exemplary. Picard would go to bat for his crew, stand up for his principles, and even push himself beyond his comfort zone to ensure he was being the best commander he knew how to be.

Diungkapkan bahwa the five following examples prove that picard is greatest captain in "star trek. ".

Sebagaimana diketahui, the episode "disaster" is essentially the disaster movie "the poseidon adventure" in space. The USS Enterprise is hit by a quantum filament and rendered adrift. g. The crew becomes trapped in various areas of the ship, and communication is not operational. Without communication, each group of characters has to deal with a miniature crisis, e. , a baby is being born in Ten Forward, and radioactive barrels are leaking in the cargo bay.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, when the disaster strikes, captain picard is in the middle of hosting a walking tour for three children, jay (john christian graas), marissa (erika flores), and patterson (max supera), who won the tour as a prize in a recent science fair. The disaster traps Picard and the three kids in a turbolift, and leaves the captain with a broken ankle. Picard is very uncomfortable with children and has no idea how to be a warm and understanding tour guide. This appears to be one of Picard's worst nightmares.

Diungkapkan bahwa what seems like a sitcom scenario, though, eventually proves itself to be an opportunity for him to continue plying his skills as a command officer. He assigns imaginary ranks to the kids, and manages to keep them all calm, even as they have to exit the turbolift and climb a shaft ladder to escape. And he does this while having to face his own discomfort with youngsters. He begins to intuit that the children require a gentler approach than hardened Starfleet officers, and turns their survival into a mission they can all go on together. He doesn't become fatherly, but manages to parlay his captaining into that of an attentive elementary school teacher. It's an inspiring piece of leadership.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "q who" was the first episode of "star trek: the next generation" to feature the borg, a species of soulless, tech-absorbing cyborgs who forcibly and unthinkingly add ship parts and people into their machine collective. The Enterprise encounters the Borg after the trickster god Q (John de Lancie) hurls it many, many lightyears in an instant. Q was inspired to bring the Enterprise to the Borg after Picard, in a perhaps-haughty fashion, declared that humans were quite capable of facing any threat the cosmos had to offer, and didn't require any of Q's magical help in their galactic trekking. Q wanted to show them a threat they couldn't handle.

Berdasarkan laporan, the borg proved to be a formidable threat. The Borg can adapt to any attack. After one invader drone is killed by a phaser, another immediately appears, now immune. They are also capable of self-repair, and possess weapons and technologies the Enterprise cannot repel. The Borg neatly slice a cylindrical piece out of the Enterprise's saucer section.

Diungkapkan bahwa picard tries to remain calm throughout this experience, but the borg are very much unlike anything he has previously encountered. Eventually, Q reappears to Picard to point out that the Borg will pursue the Enterprise relentlessly, behaving like a machine and incapable of being negotiated with. Q asks once again if he truly needs help. Q smugly rescues the Enterprise, returning it to its previous location. Picard, previously so confident, admits that he is scared, and finally confesses that, yes, he needs Q's help. It's one of Q's best moments in the franchise.

Sebagaimana diketahui, picard is a stalwart leader, but it takes true leadership skills to admit when one requires help. The ship was Picard's first priority, and his pride took a back seat. In showing his fear, in this case, Picard became a better commander.

Sebagaimana diketahui, on "star trek," the prime directive dictates that no starfleet officer may interfere with the natural evolution of any world. The Directive was put into place to ensure that Starfleet never takes on a colonialist mindset, merrily enforcing their own values on another world. The Prime Directive also dictates that any society that hasn't yet invented faster-than-light space travel should not be contacted under any circumstances.

Sebagaimana diketahui, that second part was violated by accident in the episode "who watches the watchers. When Liko returns to his people, he declares that "The Picard" is a deity. A Mintakan named Liko (Ray Wise) is electrocuted by the uncovered outpost, and he is taken on board the Enterprise to be treated. Liko seems to remain conscious, and, in a haze, glimpses Picard giving orders. " A low-tech agrarian species called the Mintakans, hovering in its own Bronze Age, was being studied by a hidden Federation lookout when an accident caused its camouflage to drop, revealing everything. A new religion threatens to begin.

Sebagaimana diketahui, of course, accidentally inspiring a religious movement is the worst kind of cultural contamination, and picard is horrified to learn that a mere accident may unwittingly alter the evolution of the mintakans. In order to prove that he is not a deity, Picard resolves to introduce himself to a panicked Liko, who is armed with a bow and arrow. Picard was willing to sacrifice his life in order to preserve the culture and ensure that a religion would not be founded. Picard aims to prove his mortality to Liko, and if he needs to be shot with an arrow to prove that, so be it. That is a deep devotion to Starfleet principles and an impressive adherence to cultural non-contamination.

The episode "The Drumhead" contains what might be Captain Picard's greatest speech, and /Film's Nina Starner has written about how educational the episode is.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the plot of "the drumhead" surrounds an explosion in the enterprise's dilithium chamber, and the ensuing investigation that follows. The explosion appears to be an act of sabotage, perhaps instigated by a visiting Klingon named J'Dan (Henry Woronicz), and may also be connected to a Starfleet medical technician Simon Tarses (Spencer Garrett). The matter is being investigated by a special prosecutor named Norah Satie (Jean Simmons), who is notorious for her hard-line tactics, and who is living up to the legacy of her legal expert father.

Berdasarkan laporan, as the episode grinds on, satie begins seeing enemies everywhere. She is very eager to rout out Starfleet's enemies, and is able to find cracks in every argument. Neither of these things, however, prove who caused the sabotage, and Satie begins probing deeper, questioning Tarses' loyalty. Picard tries to stop her investigation, but that only makes Picard her enemy as well. It's revealed that J'Dan was collaborating with the Romulans, and that Tarses once lied on his Starfleet Academy application about his species; he is secretly half-Romulan himself. It's not long before Picard is also on trial.

Diungkapkan bahwa picard can only point out that satie has gone mad with intolerance and quotes her father: "with the first link," he says, "the chain is forged. The first speech censured, the first thought forbidden, the first freedom denied, chains us all irrevocably. It takes confidence, insight, and moral tenacity to reach that conclusion. " The entire affair reminds Picard that humans are not as enlightened as they thought, and are still prone to prejudice and paranoia. There is still hard work to be done.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the episode "the measure of a man" is one of the five most essential episodes of "star trek: the next generation," displaying the careful consideration of life, right, and humanity that the franchise has become known for. In the episode, the android Data (Brent Spiner) draws the attention of a cyberneticist named Maddox (Brian Brophy) who wishes to dismantle Data to better learn how he ticks. Data refuses, of course, which causes Maddox to declare Data to be the property of Starfleet, and not an autonomous being with a consciousness and free will of his own.

Diungkapkan bahwa picard had worked directly with data closely for about two years at that point, and had come to know data as a person. A hearing is instigated to figure out if Data is actually conscious, and Picard takes on the role of his defender. Picard argues that Data is allowed to determine his own fate, while Maddox, via William Riker (Jonathan Frakes), argues that Data is little more than a glorified machine. In a conversation Picard has with Guinan (Whoopi Goldberg), she points out that there will always be people like Maddox, who long for a class of "disposable people" who can be forced to labor for free. The captain immediately recognizes that she's talking about slavery.

Diungkapkan bahwa picard realizes that the soul of starfleet is at stake, and uses all of his mental acuity and emotional outrage to stand up for data. A captain willing to go to bat for his crew is a great captain indeed, but Picard has to go so far as to argue for Data's very humanity. He is very willing to defend people he cares for, and also what is right.

#705. Zelda: Ocarina of Time Is Actually the Perfect Way to Introduce Kids to Nintendo

Tanggal: 14 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.polygon.com/zelda-ocarina-time-first-nintendo-kids-game/

Diungkapkan bahwa walk into the legend of zelda: ocarina of time’s kokiri forest, and it feels like you’re walking into a picture book. Then you walk into the Great Deku Tree and spiders start falling from the ceiling. Kokiri children are rhythmically attending to their tasks. Fairies flit about. Everyone is friendly, everything is beautiful, and the world both feels safe and makes sense. Especially in the remake, everything is moss-green and dappled with light. My daughter screamed. I jumped, too, and I knew they were coming.

Sebagaimana diketahui, since zelda: ocarina of time returned nov. A few parents are playing with their kids, but skipping whole dungeons in an effort to save their children some nightmares. Some players say the new graphics make the spiders and the ReDeads worse. 5 with its splashy Switch 2 remake, parents on Reddit have argued over how scary (read: appropriate for kids) it is. Others played at age eight and turned out fine. All fair strategies, and they raise the question: Can a game with a screaming zombie in an underground mausoleum be a kid's first Nintendo game? Parents of kids as young as 4 and 5 are asking, despite the game’s official E10+ rating.

Berdasarkan laporan, i’ve played the three child-era dungeons with my 4-year-old. But so are the tools for fighting it. Fear is quite present in this game. Which makes Ocarina of Time — The Legend of Zelda’s fairy tale — the perfect way to introduce kids to Nintendo.

Diungkapkan bahwa the redead’s paralyzing scream, dead hand reaching up through the floor of the well, the long walk through the shadow temple: parents who grew up with the n64 ocarina of time tend to have the same laundry list of nightmares. Most of these live in the later dungeons, though, and there’s a fair chance that nearly three decades of remembering these seminal gaming experiences have amplified the dread.

Parents of kids playing for the first time in 2026 report smaller, easier-to-navigate fears: 4-year-olds who panicked at the first boss and lit up at the second, spiders that terrified them until they learned to hit back.

Diungkapkan bahwa good fairy tales have always been a little scary. K. Chesterton wrote that a baby has known the dragon "intimately ever since he had an imagination," and that what the fairy tale supplies is "a St. George to kill the dragon. G. " Here, we have a tiny Link — a peer to my child — facing something scary and fighting back, with appropriate tools to deal with the fun-sized dangers at hand. The child-era half of the game is there for a reason: It's not not scary, but kids are largely good with it.

Sebagaimana diketahui, eiji aonuma describes hyrule as a world with a bright side and a dark side. " The remake's tools could make something "very, very scary" if the team tried, he said, but the game is "supposed to be for all kinds of players. Link comes from the bright part, Aonuma told one interviewer, and Ganon from the part with "a lot of scary things. ".

Diungkapkan bahwa art director aya shida wanted a hyrule convincing enough to believe in without being literal about it. Her team reached for puppet shows and practical-effects films because both make fantasy characters feel real without reproducing reality exactly. The setting "feels somewhat dark," she said, and the colorful, quirky characters who live in it give the game its "mysterious, almost dreamlike charm. ".

Diungkapkan bahwa in a world built that way, the dark stays a fairy tale's dark: frightening enough to feel real, and charming enough to keep playing. So does Navi. (How did it get in there? My kid wants to know. You’re running away from the spiders, but running toward the opportunity to free a squawking chicken from a wooden box. ).

Berdasarkan laporan, after link pulls the master sword from the stone and ages seven years, the game does get darker. Some are holding the Well and the Shadow Temple back, and commenters in some Reddit threads suggest waiting until kids are 8 or 9 before starting at all. Others report a 4-year-old who lit up when Link grew up and a 15-year-old who cried at the ending. Parents of young children have come up with strategies to match. (I find this deeply relatable; same on both counts. ) Reading comes up constantly, with parents reading the dialogue aloud for the youngest kids and some crediting the game with teaching their kids to read.

Diungkapkan bahwa whether any individual child is ready for this game is, of course, an individual decision, one that every parent will make based on their knowledge of their unique kid. The Great Deku Tree hands Link a mission with stakes he can understand and provides tools he can wield. But, for me, experiencing the remake along with my child made the sense of wonder Child Link feels as he steps out into this world palpable — and it gave me a new appreciation for the honestly very kid-friendly framing of the first half. By the time he meets bigger perils, he’s ready.

Sebagaimana diketahui, that’s all i can hope for my kid when she, too, is ready. We’re still in the first half on our playthrough. She laughed at me when I did a belly-flop into Kokiri Forest’s lake the first time I tried the dedicated jump button. She immediately clocked that the Keaton Mask looks like her beloved Pikachu, which is going to make following this game up with Kirby and the Forgotten Land, Super Mario Bros. I’ve gone on to play the Forest Temple without her, and, yes, it’s scarier, but it’s also longer and has more backtracking than she’d have patience for. Wonder, and Pokémon: Let’s Go! so, so easy. That temple and the grown-up half of the game will be there when she’s ready for it. She cheers “fight, mommy, fight!” when a Skulltula descends, thinks Jabu-Jabu’s Belly is gross — correct — and has fallen for Young Princess Ruto. I can’t wait to watch her grow into it, even if I’ll miss the days when only the child world had her full attention.

#706. An Incredible Hulk Issue Saved Marvel's X-Men Comic From Cancelation

📅 14 Nov 2026

An Incredible Hulk Issue Saved Marvel's X-Men Comic From Cancelation

Tanggal: 14 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.slashfilm.com/2310491/the-incredible-hulk-issue-saved-marvel-x-men-cancelation/

Can you imagine the X-Men without Wolverine? Well, as strange as it seems now that he's the face of the franchise, Logan only joined the X-Men in 1975, over a decade after the team's comic debut.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, in those early years, "x-men" struggled. In fact, most of the defining qualities and characters of "X-Men" came not during that original stretch but during writer Chris Claremont's enormous 16-year-run (1975-1991). Magneto was well over a decade from his reinvention as a traumatized Holocaust survivor. There weren't many strong villains, either. Stan Lee and Jack Kirby's hearts weren't in it, and the character chemistry between the original team wasn't there. Things would get worse for the X-Men before they got better.

Sebagaimana diketahui, "x-men" sales weren't too impressive in the 1960s. The book didn't just face cancellation, it was effectively canceled in 1970. After "X-Men" #66, the comic only reprinted previous "X-Men" stories for five years. Roy Thomas, the former Marvel editor in chief who wrote the last leg of the original "X-Men" run that ended at #66, said that Marvel's publisher Martin Goodman was attempting to get some value out of the book without the cost of producing new stories.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the x-men still showed up as guest stars in other series, like steve englehart's watergate scandal-inspired arc of "captain america," "secret empire," so they hadn't been completely forgotten. Then, in 1975, the Marvel powers that be decided to give the X-Men another shot. Writer Len Wein got the job of writing the relaunch, "Giant-Size X-Men" #1, and used a character he'd debuted in a 1974 "Incredible Hulk" issue as part of the team.

Diungkapkan bahwa in wein and artist herb trimpe's "incredible hulk" #180-181, the hulk stumbles across the canadian border. There, he fights a short, ornery mutant with adamantium claws: Weapon X, aka the Wolverine.

Berdasarkan laporan, the exact creation of wolverine remains a disputed piece of comics history. The general historical consensus is that Roy Thomas came up with the notion for a Canadian superhero and possibly the name "Wolverine," while Len Wein and artist John Romita Sr. (then Marvel's art director) designed Wolverine as we know him. In recent years, Thomas has tried (and succeeded, at least officially) to claim a co-creator credit on Wolverine, which has angered many in the professional comics community, along with Wein's widow, Christine Valada.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, regardless, wein is the one who wrote logan's debut appearance in those "incredible hulk" issues — sparking the enduring hulk and wolverine rivalry — and then added him to the x-men, where he went from team jerk to breakout character. (His first ongoing series lasted only six issues. Perhaps the Hulk left some of his incredible invincibility behind in "X-Men" during that appearance. It's worth noting that the Hulk himself survived a brush with cancellation. ) Incidentally, the Hulk had also guest-starred in "X-Men" #66, the last one before its pseudo-cancellation. In any case, the Hulk was present for both the X-Men's end and the beginning of their resurrection.

Diungkapkan bahwa "x-men" began publishing new stories again with issue #94, starring the "second genesis" team introduced in "giant-size x-men. " Wein soon departed, leaving the team in Chris Claremont's hands alongside artist Dave Cockrum, and together, they made comics history. But while Wolverine's popularity grew, he didn't immediately become the book's star.

Diungkapkan bahwa in fact, it was colossus who was intended to be the new lead. According to Cockrum's successorJohn Byrne, Claremont, and Cockrum even considered dropping Wolverine. That's why, per Claremont, Colossus has the traditional muscular, square-jawed superhero build. Byrne, a Canadian like Logan, pushed to keep him, and that paid off.

Diungkapkan bahwa the first x-man who chris claremont made a star was jean grey, who'd been the token girl and little else in the original run. So, he remade Jean into the team's powerhouse and changed her moniker from "Marvel Girl" to "The Phoenix. Claremont has a thing for powerful women (see: how he wrote Storm). ".

Diungkapkan bahwa jean's transformation culminates in "the dark phoenix saga," which is also when logan solidified his place as the book's star. In "X-Men" #132, the X-Men are captured one-by-one by the Hellfire Club, with Wolverine being dropped into a sewer and written off as dead. The very last page of the comic shows Wolverine, claws brandished, rising out of the water to rescue his friends, then #133 features him tearing through the Hellfire Club.

Diungkapkan bahwa yes, logan was an "obnoxious loudmouth," as dave cockrum put it, but his bad attitude actually made him cooler. So did his mysterious past, which only grew in mystery as the years went on. Plus, let's face it, there's no superpower more badass or metal (literally) than adamantium claws.

Berdasarkan laporan, through the 1980s, the x-men became marvel's premier team. Wolverine, in turn, became the X-Man who got solo stories written/drawn by prestige talent, like Claremont and Frank Miller's 1982 "Wolverine" mini-series or Barry Windsor-Smith's horror-infused origin story "Weapon X. " The "X-Men" movies and cartoons have always made Wolverine a star from the beginning, too.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the "x-men" comics faced marginalization during the 2010s due to marvel studios not owning the "x-men" movie rights. Now that this has changed, Marvel is preparing the X-Men to lead the next Marvel Cinematic Universe saga. Based on its casting choices, it's not messing around.
