#782. 'Virgin River' Star Addresses Cast Changes, Show Future Amid Season 9 Update

📅 14 Nov 2026

'Virgin River' Star Addresses Cast Changes, Show Future Amid Season 9 Update

Tanggal: 14 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.usmagazine.com/entertainment/news/virgin-river-star-addresses-cast-changes-amid-season-9-renewal/

Virgin River has officially been renewed for season 9 but what does that mean for the show’s future after cast changes?.

During an exclusive interview with Us before news broke on Friday, November 13, about the show being renewed for season 9, Ben Hollingsworth hinted how long he could see Virgin River running on Netflix.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “i would like to see it go for a long time. “I think it could go that long. I don’t want to compare it to a show like Grey’s Anatomy but it does have a feeling because Grey’s Anatomy is about that space and that place, where you do see doctors come and go,” Hollingsworth, 42, said. We could be here in 10 years still talking about Virgin River. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa hollingsworth, who plays brady, teased “so much story potential. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “there are so many books in the virgin river series. “And I think the fan base is still fairly hungry for more. We’ll see. There’s a lot of content to be drawn from it,” he noted. ”.

Based on Robyn Carr’s book series, Virgin River follows the lives of residents living in a small town in Northern California, including Mel (Alexandra Breckenridge) and Jack (Martin Henderson).

The hit series, which premiered in 2019, also stars Hollingsworth, Colin Lawrence, Annette O’Toole, Tim Matheson, Sarah Dugdale, Zibby Allen and Kai Bradbury.

Sebagaimana diketahui, after seven seasons, there have been some major departures from the netflix show. Grayson Gurnsey left as Ricky after season 4 in 2022, and Mark Ghanimé, who played Cameron, had a surprising exit once season 6 was released in December 2024.

Diungkapkan bahwa in march, virgin river returned for season 7, and it was later confirmed that marco grazzini will not reprise his role as mike. In another twist, Lauren Hammersley, who has played Charmaine since the show premiered, is also not expected to come back for season 8.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “it’s always bittersweet,” hollingsworth told us. “We never know if and when someone might show back up on the show. One thing we’ve been really great at as a cast is welcoming in when new people do come along. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, he added: “our show very much opens its arms to people. Just like on the show. Everyone’s super kind to everyone. It’s bittersweet to see someone go but also when someone new comes in, they do bring something new to the show and they bring a new texture to the show, which is also important. It’s a great set to be a part of. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, hollingsworth’s insight came as fans remain concerned about his future on the show. The season 7 finale ended with Brady injured in a motorcycle accident and Hollingsworth has remained tight-lipped about whether Brady “will be a part of” Virgin River going forward.

Diungkapkan bahwa “honestly, i wasn’t expecting [the fan reaction] to be so loud. Does he make mistakes all the time? Is he trying to be a better version of himself? Yes and he does have a lot of unfortunate things happen to him. I really take that as a compliment that people are like, ‘This show can’t happen without Brady,'” he added. He’s always trying to do what he thinks is right and he may do the wrong thing but it’s usually for the right reason. And that type of character is really relatable. “I’m right there with them. People have some opinions about it, which is a nice compliment. We’re all trying to be a better version of ourselves and Brady’s been working on that since season 1. It’s special to see people really do gravitate towards Brady and I think some of that is just he is very human. ”.

Virgin River has been renewed for seasons 8 and 9 on Netflix.

Diungkapkan bahwa i know friends is one of the best sitcoms of all time because i’ve returned to it time and time again throughout my life. Like, I couldn’t count on both hands how many times I’ve seen many of the episodes, and I’ve definitely watched it all the way through a few times. It’s been a long time since I went back to the iconic series, but when I got my wisdom teeth out last week, I ended up throwing on the show for some brainless entertainment, and something new came up. Rachel really had me fuming!.

Diungkapkan bahwa now, i know there are rachel haters out there, but in the past i’ve thought of ross as the worst and monica as my second least favorite. I've got to talk about it. This time I found myself practically yelling at my TV screen over what Rachel does more than anyone, and remembering a bunch of other instances where she was super questionable. (But remember, I’m talking about TV characters here, so it’s really not that serious).

Berdasarkan laporan, the first instance that really got my blood boiling was in season 2, episode 4. Rachel gets super jealous about Ross being with her. When they don't end up together in Season 1, Ross meets a nice gal named Julie. At this point, we know that Ross had a long-time crush on Rachel – he even told her earlier as I had recalled. When she hears that Ross and Julie are about to have sex for the first time, she sabotages the whole thing by making Julie talk all night while everyone is hanging out together.

Berdasarkan laporan, sure, it hurts to see someone you like get into a relationship with someone else, but talk about an incredibly passive-aggressive way to deal with it. She’s not only being a horrible friend to Ross, but to all her other friends who she drags down with her. Ross has just gone through a divorce at this point and communicated his interest to her multiple times before he got with Julie, so it feels super unfair. But this is just one of many things Rachel does.

Berdasarkan laporan, a few episodes later, friends has a two-part super bowl episode where they cross paths with jean-claude van damme (yes, the actor as himself). When she protests, she decides to confront him for her (which Monica doesn’t want). Upon seeing the action star, Monica confesses her big crush on him, and Rachel suggests he go up to talk to him. Van Damme starts flirting with Rachel because she’s beautiful, of course. Before she knows it, she’s going on a date with the guy. Rather than shutting it down, she totally goes for it. The nerve of Rachel! I don’t have to tell most of y’all how many girl codes this breaks, but it’s a lot.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, fast forward to the end of season 3, when ross is dating bonnie. To her surprise, she’s got a full head of hair. Phoebe sets them up, but only after asking Rachel if it’d be OK if she does. Rachel only says yes because she believes Bonnie to be bald, and knows Ross won’t like it. So, Rachel decides to convince Bonnie to shave her head because she liked it that way, and she listens. Yes, once again we see Rachel being passive-aggressive toward someone whom she apparently loves, and probably once thought of as the love of her life, AND is actually friends with. This behavior feels more like bullying than friendship to me.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, in the same episode, ross and rachel decide to get back together after her sabotage and manipulation tactics apparently work. Instead, she gives him an 18-page letter that she wrote to read through, and she wants him to read it at 5:30 a. m. We don’t know the exact contents of the letter, but apparently it asks Ross to take all the blame for their failed relationship. But after all that, she doesn’t want to talk things out with her ex before taking him back, for some reason. While I totally agree that Ross made some big mistakes, especially with the cheating, I find this to be a pretty ridiculous way to try to repair a relationship. But, hey, sometimes Friends episodes can be ridiculous.

Berdasarkan laporan, then there’s the season 7 premiere when monica gets engaged. Not too long after Chandler pops the question, Rachel comes on to Ross (who are no longer together, again), and they end up making out in the hallway. Soon all the friends are chatting about what this means for Ross and Rachel rather than focusing on Chandler and Monica’s big milestone.

Sebagaimana diketahui, i think it understandably bothers monica and brings up some past instances where she “stole her thunder. " While you can argue Rachel didn’t know she would cause Monica so much stress, I think Rachel’s actions toward Ross were driven by her own insecurities that came up when she saw her friend engaged. Just be happy for your bestie and don’t kiss your ex and her brother for one day, girl! It’s not that hard.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the last one i’ll bring up is something from the latter part of the show that still breaks my heart. I think it’s super obvious from Season 8 on that Joey has a crush on Rachel, and yet, I feel like she ignores his feelings and manufactures her own in order to feel better about herself. Remember when Rachel decided to date Joey in order to get back at Ross? This is when Ross gets with Charlie, and Rachel essentially decides to get back at him by going out with Joey. Ugh, I'll never unsee all of this.

Berdasarkan laporan, i have one more point to make here. The show just wouldn’t be entertaining if everyone reacted well to every situation. I think one of the reasons why I’m always returning to Friends with my HBO Max subscription is because all the friends feel human and flawed. But, wow I can't believe I did not realize before all the wild choices Rachel made on the show before!.

#785. The Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake Is an Event Even if You’re Not Playing It

📅 14 Nov 2026

The Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake Is an Event Even if You’re Not Playing It

Tanggal: 14 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.polygon.com/switchboard-zelda-ocarina-of-time-reception/

Watching people's personal responses to this classic is beautiful.

Berdasarkan laporan, as i mentioned last week, i'm not playing the switch 2 remake of the legend of zelda: ocarina of time yet. It's been a beautiful and uplifting experience. I'm familiar enough with the game not to be too wary of spoilers, though, so I've been reading around it and watching the responses flood my feeds. Even from this distance, it's clearly the gaming event of the year (until next week, anyway).

Berdasarkan laporan, everyone's enjoying themselves. No tedious discourse has penetrated my feeds, and everyone's initial misgivings about the art style do not seem to have survived first contact with the game itself. The care and joy Nintendo's Zelda team poured into this remake is infectious, and the mood is celebratory. Wild new caricatures of familiar characters delight me as I scroll past them.

What's even more delightful is to see how directly and profoundly Ocarina of Time still connects with people, whether they're revisiting it, experiencing it for the first time, or just being reminded of it because it's in the aether.

Diungkapkan bahwa on saturday nights, i’d take my nintendo 64 cartridge upstairs to mémère’s apartment. She always knew where I needed to go next.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, polygon's corey plante wrote a deeply touching story about his memories playing ocarina with his grandmother this week; at the other end of the scale, jen glennon shared her experience of playing the game for the first time as only a recent zelda convert. "It shouldn't be possible to feel nostalgic for a memory that isn't yours," Jen wrote. It turns out the familiar, emotive connection everyone is feeling with the remake isn't just nostalgia. In Zelda, "you know exactly where you are, even if you've technically never been there before. ".

Sebagaimana diketahui, jen points out that this feeling of knowing the game even if it's new to you stems from the elemental, fairytale simplicity of the storytelling in zelda games. I'd add that Zelda games share a deep humanity, too, more so than most Nintendo games, which tend to be quite abstract. In Zelda, this isn't expressed through strong emotions and high drama so much as it is through humor, caricature, pathos, and telling details. And no Zelda game is more poignant, funny, or scary than Ocarina of Time — not even the complex clockwork soap opera of its sequel, Majora's Mask.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, but maybe it's not out of character for ocarina of time, a game with a time-travel plot that puts the worlds of children and adults in conversation with one another. Small wonder that it made Corey think about his grandmother, and his grandmother think about her child. Maybe the Nintendo developer or translator that slipped the Little Women reference in was instinctively reminded of another classic work of art about childhood. Because that's what Ocarina of Time is.

In a series that’s (almost) all classics, which of Link’s adventures is best?.

The studio was founded by Journey art director Matt Nava, and you can certainly see its influence on this similarly sandy, wordless, and meditative (if also more conventionally exciting) game about surfing around on a sword in a dying world.

Giant Squid's latest asks you to save the world, and chill with some turtles along the way.

Sebagaimana diketahui, once upon a time, shigeru miyamoto was mr. The torch was passed, and now Aonuma is clearly lining up a successor of his own: Hidemaro Fujibayashi, director of Breath of the Wild and Tears of the Kingdom, who has now ascended to a producer credit on Ocarina of Time. Zelda and Eiji Aonuma was his heir apparent. In anticipation of Fujibayashi's future as the king of Zelda games, travel back to the start of his journey with the series: this excellent Game Boy Color diptych, featuring some of the best puzzles in Zelda history.

You'll never believe how much bigger the Switch 2 game is than the Nintendo 64 original.

#790. Brandi Carlile’s All-Requests Tour Isn’t Just a Magnificent Stunt, but an Unusually Moving Transaction Between Performer and Audience: Concert Review

Tanggal: 15 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://variety.com/2026/music/concert-reviews/brandi-carlile-all-request-tour-burn-setlist-concert-review-1236947885/

Senior Music Writer and Chief Music Critic.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, is it possible to plan for magic, serendipity, peak-level proficiency and finally sublimity by… really not planning at all? that is the question. On Brandi Carlile‘s current “Burn the Setlist!” tour, the answer is clear: Sometimes Shangri-La really is best reached with a lost roadmap.

Berdasarkan laporan, the shortish 19-date outing carlile is undertaking at the moment is the first all-requests tour in memory by any artist significant enough to have it show up on our radar. It might even be a historic first, as far as a proven headliner opting to play nothing but spontaneously generated live audience picks. But at the opposite end of the scale from bar bands and tip jars, doing solely requests sounds like as much of a nightmare to most performers as it does a dream to hardcore fans. Which is odd when you think about it, because doesn’t anyone who’s been to a lot of shows over the years have a favorite moment when a star got loose and succumbed to someone shouting out a favorite (though they usually don’t want to encourage that kind of behavior?). There are perfectly good reasons not to throw the song selections completely open to stans for roughly 2 hours and 40 minutes — as Carlile and her two bandmates, Phil and Tim Hanseroth, are doing now — when you have a recorded catalog of close to a hundred original songs, plus a repertoire of proven live cover choices.

Who among even the greats of music has anything close to 100% recall? When the recent and distant pasts are both being dredged up, a good corollary to “Never let ’em see you sweat” might be: Never let ’em see you forget.

Fortunately, Brandi Carlile and the Hanseroth twins are freaking elephants.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, but making a point out of not planning is different from not being prepared. Tim Hanseroth posted an IG video of himself running through their studio albums and strumming along to stir the old juices. Carlile said in a video livestream for fans on the tour’s eve that she would have a monitor for lyrics if she needed it. And Carlile and the brothers are prepared for this, first of all, by having brain chemistry that is clearly a little bit different from mine or probably yours, with the power not just to generate constant creative sparks but to put those sparks in an easily accessible lockbox. You’re either genetically predisposed to that kind of recall or you’re not, and at least a little part of why Carlile and the Hanseroths have been ideal partners since the turn of the millennium is that shared gift. Not that they came into the “Burn the Setlist!” tour relying completely on muscle memory. But at the show I caught, I barely noticed Carlile looking down at it… which I can’t say for most big tours I attend where the show is locked in for months straight.

Berdasarkan laporan, all of this risks making the tour seem like a stunt, which it kind of is. But the bigger reason for why it’s such a rousing success — and a reason why fans may remember these shows almost as well as Carlile and company remember their songs — is how many deeply moving moments are stirred up up in the shows, in the quietest bits that come between the outbreaks of hysterical shouting and sign-waving. Leaving the setlists up to fans, chance or God results in obscure picks and ironic juxtapositions that sometimes aren’t anything more than fun or curious, but are sometimes unexpectedly touching in a way that one of Carlile’s perfectly laid-out arena shows probably couldn’t be. Not just a mere test of skills, these concerts are really a nightly emotional chemistry experiment. On the right night — and the show I saw in Oakland was the right night — it might be transcendent, in a way that’s a little different even from the transcendent gigs we’ve seen before.

Sebagaimana diketahui, carlile had some notes before the show began; rather than restrictions, felt like promissory instructions about how to best proceed through a candy store about to open. ” She noted that they wouldn’t be open to attempting songs they’d never performed even once before, “so we’re not gonna be able to ‘Free Bird’ or ‘Sweet Home Alabama’ this shit. (She later made good on that, picking more people from the rear balcony than any other part of the audience, though the front rows did OK too. ). ”Everything is pretty much fair game,” she instructed — “any song that we’ve ever done. 7 at the Fox Oakland, the second on their tour. “I can see your signs all the way back, and I will call on people all the way in the back,” Carlile declared at the top of the concert Nov. Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, but carlile also wanted it understood that this was not meant to be a tricky pop quiz. You have to be a gay mom that didn’t carry a child to understand this song. So it became ‘I am the mother of Evangeline. ’ And it’s not true — it’s a universal thing — because here I am in Oakland, and this man stood up and wanted me to play the song. And my mantra became, I have to tell myself I’m a mother so that I can believe I deserve to call myself that. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the tour offers an opportunity to witness problem-solving in real time. For Carlile and the twins, perhaps the biggest problem was obliging a request for Alanis Morissette’s “Uninvited. “And no piano? That’s the whole song!” But she and the brothers found their path to make it a pure guitar-and-bass rock ‘n’ roll scorcher, followed by an exultant “We don’t need no stinking strings!” (With implicit apologies, undoubtedly, to SistaStrings. Concert hyperbole is a dangerous thing, but I found myself hard-pressed to recall comparable instances in which I’d seen rock ‘n’ roll performers so throughly committed to the moment, not just for a moment but for close to three hours of them. #801. Inside the First AI Music Awards, a Chaotic Evening Attempting to Normalize Tech-Assisted Tunes

📅 14 Nov 2026

Inside the First AI Music Awards, a Chaotic Evening Attempting to Normalize Tech-Assisted Tunes

Tanggal: 14 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://variety.com/2026/music/features/inside-first-ai-music-awards-sonic-intelligence-academy-1236947847/

I knew things were a little off when the first thing I heard on my walk to the AI Music Awards was “the winner…” followed by the sweet voice of Kelly Clarkson.

Berdasarkan laporan, no, miss american idol did not abandon her feud with the brooklyn bird to capitalize on her newfound appreciation for ai. Alas, not so: It was Clarkson’s Christmas classic “Underneath the Tree,” playing from speakers at a local YWCA event across the street. But as I approached the Mayan Theater in Downtown Los Angeles on a sunny afternoon to check in for Friday’s inaugural “AI Music Awards,” powered by the “Sonic Intelligence Academy” or “SIQA,” I wondered if her voice was so strong as to echo through the nearly century-old theater-turned-nightclub’s walls. Related Stories Tubi Partners With TikTok to Create 10 Original Long-Form Series (EXCLUSIVE).

To qualify for the awards, artists needed to register their tracks to SIQA’s “Verified Registry,” which denotes whether the song was fully AI-generated, made with the assistance of AI or featured a cloned human voice to lead the tune (what the group calls a “human + AI hybrid”).

Diungkapkan bahwa registered artists then nominate their peers in the 25 categories up for consideration — everything from “ai song of the year” to “best ai pop song” to “best ai comedic song” — and then vote on the winners. One of those nominees was Xania Monet, the AI persona of Telisha “Nikki” Jones, who a day earlier won the AI Album of the Year category at SIQA’s inaugural summit and who would eventually go on to win both artist and song of the year, three out of four of the awards’ top categories. (The fourth, producer of the year, went to “DJ Shawn Q. ”).

Berdasarkan laporan, the sonic intelligence academy is the brainchild of software engineer timirah “tj” james and her sister mia james. Since its January launch, it has worked to establish an awards program to counter the mainstream music industry’s aversion to AI. The group believes there needs to be infrastructure that supports those using AI to create music, rather than dismissing its existence, and it hopes to be an AI counterpart to the longstanding Recording Academy that governs the Grammy Awards. It advocates for artists to publicly associate themselves with their AI-powered work, eager to highlight the humans who helped create the product.

Berdasarkan laporan, it’s a noble, if surprising, decision to embrace its role as counterculture when ai artists continue to pursue a billboard charting position. Some of its methods are a little overt, perhaps intentionally: After some in the industry spurned the idea of AI-generated music charting on Billboard’s industry-standard charts, the group used a week in January ahead of the Grammys to launch its own charts exclusively for AI music. The Mayan is a 12-minute walk from the Crypto. com Arena, the Grammys’ longtime home.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the moves are not subtle, but subtlety is not the organization’s goal. The group and awards’ existence alone reflects those in the AI music space trying to move past the thorny legal questions surrounding AI music, which have led to lawsuits by artists and record labels against generators like Suno and Udio over copyright infringement, and into a realm of relevance within the genres they’re trying to embody.

It is, in a word, new, and new things mean kinks to work out.

Berdasarkan laporan, the first kink i noticed was when, as i arrived 30 minutes before the red carpet was set to begin, the doors to the venue were locked. I had to pull on each door before someone opened one, which led me to the check-in stand (bypassing any form of security, which didn’t seem to exist). I entered the foyer and arrived at the makeshift red carpet, where about 12, mostly independent media ventures set up cameras to interview the various nominees, presenters, and VIPs who’d grace the roughly 7-foot-long red carpet in front of one of the two step-and-repeat backdrops. PT. A spokesperson told me 29 media outlets had signed up to cover the event, but that some couldn’t make it because of the sudden flight ground-stop issued by the Federal Aviation Administration around 12:30 p. m. Whether human or AI, aviation afflictions come for us all.

Diungkapkan bahwa the guests gracing the red carpet were not screens rolled out displaying ai avatars, contrary to a reasonable assumption. Sequined dresses and colorful blazers strolled through, stopping to speak with outlets like Reuters to the fiery red mohawk-sporting, sequin-wearing host of “The Iconic Punk Oz” Oz Powers to, tucked against a wall and steps from the red carpet, an effective AI red carpet correspondent housed inside a tall, white faux-stone vessel. Instead, the human creators behind the digital faces strutted the carpet in their Sunday best, treating the night less as music’s biggest night and more as the biggest night for their music. The contraption was developed by the event’s top sponsor, Deepgram, an AI startup specializing in text-to-speech agents.

Berdasarkan laporan, the device, which knew the artists and pressed them about the event, struck in me a slight fear about whether people might opt for robot reporters instead of humans, though that fear subsided when i realized this device could not appear on the red carpet because it could not move. The creators seemed more eager to speak to the physical reporters anyway, with some of them emphasizing the human elements of their AI work. Fredro Starr, one half of the rap group Onyx, spent much of the carpet touting the human vocals that made up his AI-beat-laden record “It All Started in Brooklyn,” which he claimed was the first AI album on vinyl.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “you can’t replace [humans],” starr told me, using the carpet to debut his new moniker, “mad ai. So vocally, you can hear that, but the AI just took it to another level. ” “The feeling that you get was what we bring with the spirit of hip-hop. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, inside the theater, siqa tried to bring a party-like feel to the function. A bar at the back of the venue —at a charge — kept well drinks flowing, and the bar top was littered with copies of a sponsored version of the newspaper “Rolling Out” featuring interviews with many of the nominees and James, the SIQA founder. One of those featured, Xania Monet founder Jones, sparked a wave of controversy last year when some of her Monet songs hit some of Billboard’s genre charts, leading to an interview with CBS’s Gayle King and to Kehlani slamming a $3 million record deal Jones received. As she waited for a drink by the bar ahead of the event’s start, Jones told me she wasn’t worried about the AI of it all overshadowing the pursuit of legitimacy within the greater music industry.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “ai is just a tool,” she said. “It just emphasizes what we do. I just feel like we should all be one. ”.

But despite that lofty goal, the kinks kept rearing their heads.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the event started about 30 minutes past its 6:15 p. m. start time, skipping a planned opening video montage for a dance break performed and choreographed by actor Giovanni Wilson with eight dancers to a seemingly AI-produced song that described — in literal terms — how we were at the inaugural AI music awards. The delay forced the show to skip introducing the nominees for the first half of the awards and instead have presenters just state the winner, robbing some attendees of hearing their names called for what felt like one of their biggest achievements.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the event was hosted by wilson and podcast host lana hout, one half of the podcasting duo the “ai chicks,” with a three-member house band of real people playing guitar, bass, keys and drums, soundtracking much of the night. The two hosts shared the only two microphones apparently available throughout the night, with a teleprompter loaded with the Claude-generated run-of-show, but they often seemed lost about what category, presenter, performance or commercial break was next.

Diungkapkan bahwa at one point, hout and wilson were confused over whether they would cut to commercial or bring out the two presenters for best ai country artist. They then brought out the two country award presenters, only for Hout to walk back out mid-introduction to interrupt and say that, actually, they would go to commercial break. The award was eventually presented 13 minutes later with a different presenter.

Diungkapkan bahwa oftentimes, the use of ai seemed to hover over some of the technical hiccups. Deepgram also had a commercial that played throughout the evening, but it would sometimes play at random moments even when a commercial break wasn’t called. Deepgram was meant to power an AI voice that introduced the night’s presenters and nominees, but it often didn’t work and, when it did, talked over many of the presenters. The Deepgram team sat on the couch to my left, and when I looked over to see their reaction to the madness, one member had her head in her hands.

Berdasarkan laporan, early in the night, wilson tried to introduce a trailer for his latest acting gig, the terrance howard-led film “a good hand wasted” that he said used ai to help finish the project, but none of wilson’s cues seemed to get it to play. Once it finally did, the screen only played a portion of the trailer before Howard’s face even appeared.

“So, ugh,” he said, before raising his hand to summon the audience’s applause.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the teleprompter was not much help, often shifting rapidly as presenters were speaking. The chaos led Wilson, who spent much of the night trying to maintain some decorum throughout the frustration, to joke they were “dealing with a prompter that has Tourette’s. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa the commercials for the event featured deepgram and a new social network called “trinity social,” with the latter’s ai-generated ad featuring a persona wearing a necklace of the rockstar games logo encouraging a stadium full of generated people to sign up for the app. A Rockstar spokesperson did not respond to an immediate request for comment on whether it authorized the logo, though if it did not, the ad would represent the latest in AI content lifting copyrighted material without permission, all at an event celebrating a use of AI that has rankled the music industry over similar concerns.

Some of the greatest energy came from the evening’s nearly 10 performances, all of which made the cut despite the event running nearly 40 minutes behind schedule the entire night.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, there had been some speculation over how, exactly, songs produced with ai and presented by ai avatars would play on stage. Some acts, like country artist Ava Bentley and R&B artist EJ Rogers, lip-synced their entire performance, while others relied on hired performers who did even that for them. For “Chaisen Hale,” a project that features a video of an AI-generated boy with AI-generated vocals, a human lookalike singer named John Victor, 14, was brought out to lip-sync to the track. It turns out, through the power of lip-syncing and acting. Attendees — including one duo, for some reason, dressed as Frankenstein and his bride — were generally riveted.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, nearly all of the performances were backed by the live band and dancers, who were provided to the artists for free by siqa. Many who produce music with AI say they did so because they could not afford the studio musicians and resources required to bring their tracks to life, which made the reliance on the house band feel more like an opportunity to live out their dreams without the cost often paid by traditional artists who hire such musicians to produce their work.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, some of the only actual live vocals came from a rapper named godfellow and grammy-winning singers eric bellinger and candace wakefield, the latter of whom made a point to note the “hiccups” throughout the night and that she was singing live as she performed a song by ai artist “aria blue. ” The performances captured much of what remained in the crowd, which grew smaller and smaller as the night progressed.

James, the SIQA founder, acknowledged the “technical difficulties” ahead of presenting Jones with her awards, but she promised those would be resolved ahead of next year’s ceremony.

Berdasarkan laporan, “because there will be a next year because this is the new music industry,” she told the crowd around 9:45 p. , just as it was hitting its hard end time. ”SIQA has created the infrastructure for that industry and for all the artists coming up in that industry. m. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, and for many of the people in the room, that’s all they wanted. (When I addressed her by her given name, she snapped at me. Another artist named Ramona Höffel, a 56-year-old woman who spends her days helping disabled people, flew in from Switzerland to represent her AI persona “Vireya” on her first-ever red carpet. One artist, Sheena Taylor, accepted her award for best AI gospel song for a track called “I Denounce You, Satan,” by acknowledging the intense traumas she endured that led to a religious discovery. ).

Sebagaimana diketahui, “i have a lot of ideas and wishes, and for a long time i paint, then i write, and that’s not enough,” she said, visibly nervous to be the first person to walk the red carpet. “The music gives me room to all this bring outside of my brain. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, i thought about höffel’s words as i left the venue just after 10 p. , well past the event’s scheduled 9:30 end, and into the downtown rain. m. It’s unclear whether AI music will generate an enduring monoculture in the way the music from the 2010s has, particularly as the larger music industry has mostly ostracized it. To my right was a line forming to get into the venue for “Club 2010s” night, now delayed due to the prolonged awards show. But it’s left people like Höffel feeling stronger, which is all someone like 2011 chart-topper Kelly Clarkson could ask for.

#802. Forget Black Mirror & Severance, This 16-Episode Masterpiece Nails Existential Sci-Fi

📅 15 Nov 2026

Forget Black Mirror & Severance, This 16-Episode Masterpiece Nails Existential Sci-Fi

Tanggal: 15 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://screenrant.com/forget-black-mirror-severance-pantheon-existential-sci-fi/

Sebagaimana diketahui, when it comes to delivering pure existential sci-fi, black mirror and severance would probably be considered the top shows from recent years. Given how both sci-fi series are packed with unsettling explorations of reality, identity, and free will, it is hard not to consider them masterpieces. However, there is one relatively obscure but brilliant sci-fi show that takes existentialism to a whole different level.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, created by craig silverstein and based on a series of short stories by ken liu, pantheon, on the surface, is a cyberpunk conspiracy thriller. Although it is not as well-known as shows like Black Mirror and Severance, it has a solid cult following and boasts a perfect 100% critical score on Rotten Tomatoes. Its acclaim can partly be attributed to its creative animation style and voice acting.

Sebagaimana diketahui, however, the show's true appeal lies in its portrayal of singularity. In its early moments, it sets up a rather simple story where it unfolds in a world where mind-uploading technology is about to be adopted by the masses. With this story setup, though, the show turns into a mind-bending story about the large existential implications of achieving technological singularity and how it challenges our understanding of everything.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, driven by the "ship of theseus" paradox, pantheon initially explores the horrors of uploading one's consciousness. It shows how even after a person awakens in the cloud with the same memories and quirks as their physical self, they are seemingly nothing like their biological original. With this, it prompts one to question whether human evolution is worth it if it strips away one's humanity.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, almost reminiscent of severance's innies and outies, pantheon also explores how a cloned character is completely raised in a simulation to be able to replicate the genius of his original counterpart. This becomes an existential exploration of free will, walking through the character's journey of defining his own moral compass despite being coded to be someone else.

Berdasarkan laporan, similar to one of the most harrowing episodes from black mirror, "be right back," pantheon also walks through the story of a grieving daughter and wife. They struggle to process the demise of David Kim. However, when he returns as uploaded intelligence, they are forced to wonder whether he is merely a digital echo of their inability to process their grief.

Sebagaimana diketahui, pantheon originally premiered on amc+, but it is now available for streaming on netflix in the u. S.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, in its two-season runtime, pantheon also does not shy away from expanding its vision to an international geopolitical scale before going completely cosmic with its stakes. It highlights how Uploaded Intelligence is ultimately weaponized by nations, leading to a chilling Cold War. In its final arc, the show takes an existential look at the Simulation hypothesis by exploring the long-term implications of its central ideas.

Before Pantheon's ending credits start rolling, the sci-fi series leaves viewers with many questions surrounding the importance of having a finite life span and the existence of true meaning in the face of uncertainty.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, pantheon's narrative eventually spirals into wildly fantastical developments focusing on everything from god-like entitites to dyson spheres. Surprisingly, though, even in these moments, the show feels incredibly grounded and relatable. Even when it expands its vision to cosmic scales, it never forgets the sociological and existential roots of its drama.

Diungkapkan bahwa even its portrayal of imaginative and bizarre technology is made to look familiar through recognizable interfaces. Meanwhile, even its 2-D dimensional animation style ensures that when its sci-fi ideas become a little too extreme, its visuals remain tangible. Without explicitly naming certain characters, Pantheon cleverly parallels them with real tech billionaires.

With this, the sci-fi show even becomes a critique of Silicon Valley's transhumanist culture.

Diungkapkan bahwa it also features real-world pop culture references and even features nods to other popular sci-fi works like frank herbert’s dune and william gibson’s neuromancer. It is unfortunate that Pantheon never got to last as long as shows like Severance and Black Mirror. Even with two seasons, however, the sci-fi show is undoubtedly a masterpiece.

#803. 7 Near-Perfect Prime Video Miniseries You Can Binge in One Sitting

📅 15 Nov 2026

7 Near-Perfect Prime Video Miniseries You Can Binge in One Sitting

Tanggal: 15 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://collider.com/prime-video-near-perfect-miniseries-binge/

Diungkapkan bahwa prime video has earned a reputation as the home of massive, multi-season flagship hits like the boys and the lord of the rings: the rings of power, but the platform has also produced several high-profile, critically acclaimed miniseries and limited series. In the last few years, the streaming giant has released several shows in the category, the likes of which are hard to find elsewhere. Though limited in number, these shows have come to be known for their focused narrative, impactful themes, and, for some, stellar visuals.

Sebagaimana diketahui, ranging from internationally acclaimed, award-winning comedies to niche, cult shows, prime video’s library of miniseries and limited shows spans genres, styles, and formats, so there is something for everyone. While not all of these shows have been widely celebrated or lauded by critics, each of them is noted for its resonant storytelling and unique experience, making every minute of their limited runtime worthwhile. So here’s our selection of near-perfect Prime Video miniseries that you can binge in (roughly) one sitting.

Berdasarkan laporan, a psychological thriller created by naomi sheldon and gabbie asher, the girlfriend follows laura sanderson, an elite art gallery owner whose picture-perfect life is disrupted when her son introduces his new girlfriend, cherry, to the family. Robin Wright stars as Laura and also serves as the show’s director (with Andrea Harkin), with Olivia Cooke as Cherry. Laura’s high-society lifestyle and ideologies instantly clash with Cherry’s working-class background, and she begins to suspect the young woman’s motivations. The show also features Laurie Davidson, Waleed Zuaiter, Tanya Moodie, and Leo Suter as other key characters.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, a series adaptation of michelle frances’ novel, the girlfriend is a dark and twisted exploration of love, obsession, greed, power, and a mother’s reactions to and perceptions of her son’s love interest. Even if it is not unique in its themes, it is the depiction of those themes that sets this show apart from its counterparts. The unhinged power struggle between Laura and Cherry is brilliantly depicted through the stellar performances by Robin Wright and Olivia Cooke, with their chilling chemistry driving the show’s narrative.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, one of prime video’s most unique, poetic, and critically praised sci-fi shows, tales from the loop is a stunning series inspired by swedish artist simon stålenhag’s neo-futuristic art book of the same name. Set in a fictional Ohio town, the story revolves around various people living around an underground facility called The Loop, which impacts their perceptions of time, space, memory, and reality. The show stars Jonathan Pryce, Rebecca Hall, Paul Schneider, Duncan Joiner, and Daniel Zolghadri as main characters.

Sebagaimana diketahui, truly out of the ordinary, tales from the loop sets a fantastic example of how a series can be adapted from art. Surreal, sublime, and dreamy, the series brings life to the original artwork and elevates it with a resonant existential narrative about the future of humanity that you would want to watch in one sitting. At the time of its premiere, Tales from the Loop was a critics’ favorite and has remained a sci-fi television gem of the 2020s, even if it has since been overshadowed by bigger, brighter sci-fi contemporaries. The series deserves far more recognition than it has received.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, boots riley’s first television series, i’m a virgo is a surrealist comedy about a 19-year-old, 13-foot-tall boy named cootie, raised by his uncle and aunt, who sheltered him from the harsh realities of the world all his life. But when a group of teenage political activists learns about his existence, Cootie is forced to come out of his protected world, learning about himself and what life truly means. Jharrel Jerome delivers a great performance as Cootie, as does Walton Goggins as the self-proclaimed billionaire vigilante, The Hero.

Berdasarkan laporan, i’m a virgo is a surrealist superhero satire that puts an absurdist spin on the superhero genre, trading power fantasy for social critique. At its heart, the show is essentially a quirky and often darkly funny coming-of-age story that mocks corporate capitalism and systemic racism. I’m a Virgo became a favorite of critics at the time of its release, earning praise for its heart, humor, and satire, as well as Riley’s unique vision, but the series has continued to be one of Prime Video’s most underrated shows.

Sebagaimana diketahui, developed by alice birch, dead ringers is a series remake of david cronenberg’s psychological thriller film, which in turn is an adaptation of the 1977 novel twins by bari wood and jack geasland. Starring Rachel Weisz in the central role that was played by Jeremy Irons in the 1988 film, the series follows obsessively co-dependent twins and fellow gynecologists, Beverly and Elliot Mantle, whose personal relationship, obsession, and ambition push the boundaries of law, ethics, and science. The other key characters are played by Britne Oldford, Poppy Liu, Jennifer Ehle, and Michael Chernus.

Diungkapkan bahwa dead ringers stands out among other gender-swapped reboots with its intelligent writing and dark humor, and is often considered a true homage to cronenberg’s chilling, incisive thriller. Rachel Weisz thrills with her performance, anchoring the show with her contrasting character types, which earned her a Golden Globe nomination and the show a Peabody Award. Widely praised for seamlessly blending high-concept body horror with sharp social satire, Dead Ringers is a psychological thriller that will make genre fans want to watch without breaks.

Diungkapkan bahwa donald glover and janine naber’s dark comedy satire stars dominique fishback as a young woman named andrea "dre" greene, who is obsessed with a world-famous pop star named ni'jah, who remains elusive after a traumatic incident. Swarm focuses on Dre’s extreme, compulsive fandom and how her desperate attempts to follow her desires lead her down a murderous path across the country. Rory Culkin, Paris Jackson, X Mayo, Billie Eilish, Stephen Glover, and more appear as guest stars.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, a heavily underrated and often misunderstood psychological thriller, swarm works both as a depiction of toxic obsession and a cautionary tale, anchored by fishback’s menacing antagonist. The show is a disorienting blend of dark satire, gory slasher, and psychological horror. The series refuses to fit into any genre, shifting from graphic violence to true-crime mockumentary and surreal satire. Critics widely praise the show for being as disturbing as it is nuanced, and Fishback’s outstanding performance earned her multiple accolades, making Swarm one of the best shows about obsessive fandom.

Sebagaimana diketahui, in his first television show as a creator, director, and showrunner, barry jenkins adapts colson whitehead’s pulitzer prize-winning novel of the same name into a thrilling historical fiction story. The Underground Railroad tells the story of Cora and Caesar, two enslaved people on a Georgia plantation who escape their ruthless owners and attempt to take a magical subterranean train to freedom, while being chased by a slave catcher. Thuso Mbedu stars as Cora, Aaron Pierre as Caesar, and Joel Edgerton as the slave catcher.

Sebagaimana diketahui, alternative history and magic realism come together in this haunting and thrilling story of survival and freedom, underscored by a great cast and an incredible visual style that demands uninterrupted attention. Barry Jenkins transports his theatrical storytelling style to the small screen, bringing life to Whitehead’s critically lauded bestseller that reimagines the titular network of abolitionists and their real-life efforts to help enslaved African-Americans escape to freedom. Even though it was well-acclaimed at its release and won several prestigious awards, The Underground Railroad is an underrated miniseries that deserves a lot more attention.

Sebagaimana diketahui, phoebe waller-bridge’s critically acclaimed, multi-award-winning tragicomedy series that catapulted her to global recognition, fleabag is a first-person narrative of the titular narrator’s personal tragedies, identity crisis, and difficult family dynamics. The 30-something single woman in London juggles her struggling café business and the deaths of her loved ones, giving the audience a darkly funny peek into her intimate emotions and challenges as she navigates romance, heartbreak, family drama, and loss. Besides Waller-Bridge, Andrew Scott also gained popularity as The Priest, while Sian Clifford, Brett Gelman, and Olivia Colman are also memorable for their roles.

Berdasarkan laporan, widely considered a television masterpiece of the past decade, fleabag is pure comedic genius. Anchored by Waller-Bridge's pitch-perfect delivery, with a close second by Scott and Clifford, it is a wholesome, honest show that handles delicate themes like suppressed grief and identity crisis with more humor and heart in its limited runtime than multi-season television phenomena. Even though the show is split into two seasons, it is essentially one limited series divided into two chapters, which collectively tells a complete, single-arc story about the protagonist’s healing process that you will want to binge in one sitting.

#804. Kids’ Choice Awards: ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day,’ Zendaya, Tom Holland, BTS Among 2026 Winners

📅 15 Nov 2026

Kids’ Choice Awards: ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day,’ Zendaya, Tom Holland, BTS Among 2026 Winners

Tanggal: 15 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/tv/tv-news/2026-kids-choice-awards-winners-list-1236755415/

The show, hosted by Alex Warren, aired simultaneously on CBS and Nickelodeon for the first time.

Spider-Man: Brand New Day and its stars Tom Holland and Zendaya, along with BTS, were among the big winners Saturday night at the Kids’ Choice Awards.

#806. Richard Sterban, Oak Ridge Boys Bass Singer Who Helped Make ‘Elvira’ a Hit, Dies at 83

📅 15 Nov 2026

Richard Sterban, Oak Ridge Boys Bass Singer Who Helped Make ‘Elvira’ a Hit, Dies at 83

Tanggal: 15 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.billboard.com/music/country/richard-sterban-death-oak-ridge-boys-1236382272/

Diungkapkan bahwa known for his signature "oom poppa, mow mow" bass line on "elvira," sterban had 17 no. 1s on the Hot Country Songs chart with The Oak Ridge Boys, plus two top 40 hits on the all-genre Hot 100.

Sebagaimana diketahui, richard sterban, the bass vocalist behind the “oom poppa, mow mow” hook on one of the oak ridge boys‘ biggest hits, “elvira,” and whose career launched as a backing singer for elvis presley, died on saturday (nov. 14). He was 83.

Berdasarkan laporan, sterban passed away due to complications from bronchitis and pneumonia in hendersonville, tenn. , his family shared. He died after a long battle with cancer, and after retiring from touring last year.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “we appreciate all of your love, support, and prayers,” the sterban family said in a statement released on saturday. “Please continue to lift us up in this difficult time. We find comfort knowing that he is currently face to face with Jesus. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, sterban, a member of the oak ridge boys for more than 50 years with duane allen, william lee golden and the late joe bonsall, revealed a pancreatic cancer diagnosis in september 2025, saying at the time that he was “under the care of the best cancer doctors in the country and, with the help of the good lord above, i believe i will be able to get through this. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa “elvira” — the oak ridge boys’ highest-charting single on the all-genre billboard hot 100, a song that became one of the quartet’s numerous no. 1s on the Hot Country Songs chart, and the winner of a trio of major awards (a Grammy Award, a CMA Award and an ACM Award) put Sterban’s deep vocal front and center in the hit’s chorus.

Diungkapkan bahwa the oak ridge boys had 47 entries on the hot country songs chart, including 17 no. On the all-genre Billboard Hot 100, the group notched four entries, including two top 40-charted hits: “Elvira” (No. 1s that spanned 1978-90. 1s (Fancy Free in 1981, Bobbie Sue in 1982 and Deliver in 1984). They also had 39 entries on the Top Country Albums chart, including three No. 5 in 1981) and “Bobbie Sue” (No. 12 in 1982).

Sebagaimana diketahui, sterban was born in camden, n. , in 1934, and grew up in nearby Collingswood, where he sang at Sunday school and in his seventh grade glee club. J. He went to Trenton State College, now The College of New Jersey, to study music.

Before his professional journey in music led him to The Oak Ridge Boys, Sterban helped found the gospel quartet The Keystones in the Philadelphia area; Bonsall, who would go on to join The Oak Ridge Boys with him, also sang in the group.

In the early 1970s, Sterban found himself singing as a backing vocalist for superstar Elvis Presley.

Berdasarkan laporan, richard sterban, the oak ridge boys’ bass singer who memorably lent his vocals to their beloved “elvira” cover, died saturday. He was 83.

Sterban died in Hendersonville, Tennessee, due to complications from bronchitis and pneumonia after fighting a battle with cancer, his family and the Oak Ridge Boys announced.

Sebagaimana diketahui, born on april 24, 1943, in camden, new jersey, sterban began singing at 6 in sunday school as a soprano. He sang tenor in his seventh-grade glee club, and upon his eighth grade, his voice dropped to bass.

He studied music at Trenton State College (modernly known as the College of New Jersey), and began singing in a gospel quartet where he met Joe Bonsall, his future Oak Ridge Boys bandmate.

Diungkapkan bahwa while singing part-time, sterban joined j. D. Sumner and the Stamps, whom Elvis Presley hired to sing behind him. He then sang and recorded with the King of Rock and Roll, and also appeared in the 1972 concert film Elvis on Tour.

Berdasarkan laporan, sterban was then offered the opportunity to join the oak ridge boys after the departure of noel fox, which he accepted in 1972. Bonsall joined the group one year later, with Duane Allen, William Lee Golden and Sterban already in the group, which carried on as the faces of the band for five decades.

They performed with Johnny Cash, who helped them sign with Columbia Records in 1973, though it was after opening for Roy Clark in 1975 when they met his manger, Jim Halsey, who would later sign with the group.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, they reached success with “y’all come back saloon,” which reached no. 3 on the country chart in 1977, and led to a string of hits. “I’ll Be True to You” became their first No. 1 song, though 1981’s “Elvira” would become one of their largest successes.

Berdasarkan laporan, originally recorded by dallas frazier, the oak ridge boys’ version of the track went to no. 1 on the country chart and No. 5 on the pop chart, sold more than two million copies and won a Grammy. Sterban’s bass refrain was a major touchpoint on the song.

The Oak Ridge Boys went on to also become members of the Grand Ole Opry, the Gospel Music Hall of Fame and the Country Music Hall of Fame.

Sterban released his memoir From Elvis to Elvira: My Life on Stage, written with Steven Robinson, in 2012.

Berdasarkan laporan, sterban is survived by his wife, donna; his daughters, lauren (tyler) and tori (michael); his sons, rich (chele), doug and chris; his grandchildren, mali (zachary), nikolas, tyler (ryann), madelyn, alexandra, rex, owen and charli grace; and his great-grandchildren, salem, asher and theo. Sebagaimana diketahui, gail simone has been one of comic books' most iconic writers for the last couple of decades. Among them are Deadpool, Batgirl, and Wonder Woman. She’s currently on an epic run of Uncanny X-Men that’s produced 39 issues in just over two years. A quick look at her bibliography will show that she’s written many of readers’ favorite characters, and done it brilliantly. That adds up to around two issues a month, which is production that many writers can’t do.

Berdasarkan laporan, there are plenty of reasons to read uncanny x-men, but one of them is the ongoing relationship with gambit and rogue. It’s been everything that a romantic love story should be. They have their disagreements, but it never gets too heavy or angry. On top of that, they’re always showing each other a ton of love. Sometimes the public display of affection is front and center, but never in front of the kids (only that one time in front of Logan in issue #1).

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, because of their amazingly written relationship, it's no wonder that gail simone said there’s no way she’s breaking them up. In fact, she said in a very Gail Simone way.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, anyone who follows gail simone on social media knows that she loves to have fun. Whether she believes it or not is far from the point. For example, one of her consistent jokes is how certain characters can win fights seven times out of ten. It’s why, when she approached the topic of Remy and Rogue breaking up, she said, “I fairly regularly get story suggestions from readers of Anna Marie and Remy separating temporarily or even splitting up entirely. I’d rather throw barbecue sauce on the Mona Lisa. She understands that the internet is a place to have fun. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa relationships in comic books will always have their ups and downs. There are exceptions to the rule, like Superman and Lois Lane, but that’s rare. Sometimes the story ends tragically, like Peter Parker and Mary Jane in Spider-Man: One More Day. So knowing that Gail Simone has no plans to break them up is a refreshing change.

Sebagaimana diketahui, rogue and gambit’s relationship has grown throughout uncanny x-men. In the very first issue, it was clear that it would be a focal point of the series. However, what truly made them one of the best couples in comics is their approach to the former Outliers, who are now the New Mutants.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, they went from being in their honeymoon phase to becoming loving parents. Each of the New Mutants looks at Anna Marie and Remy as their parents, even without the paperwork or being biologically linked. The best part is that they’re amazing at it. Plus, if readers go by context clues, Rogue may be pregnant.

Diungkapkan bahwa one of the storylines in uncanny x-men: wild ride was rogue attempting to purge the demon inside gambit’s soul. They don’t know what you carry inside you. During an exorcism, a demon said to Anna Marie, “They don’t know, do they? Even your worthless husband. ” Of course, demons are known to lie and say all sorts of outlandish things to keep their victim uneasy. In this case, the truth could be what throws a person off more than a lie.

Berdasarkan laporan, rogue will always be overprotective of the people she loves. It felt like Anna Marie was fighting for more than her husband’s soul. She was battling for the future of her family and the father of her unborn child. Nevertheless, Uncanny X-Men: Wild Ride seemed different. If that’s the case, then Gail Simone may have furthered the point that Remy and Rogue should never break up.

#812. This '60s Sketch Show Became One Of The Biggest Flops In TV History

📅 14 Nov 2026

This '60s Sketch Show Became One Of The Biggest Flops In TV History

Tanggal: 14 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.slashfilm.com/2308325/turn-on-60s-sketch-show-biggest-flops-tv-history/

Berdasarkan laporan, networks tried all sorts of wild and outlandish ideas in the 1960s as they attempted to wrestle audiences' attention away from their rivals. This was the decade that gave us "My Mother the Car," the show for which Jerry Van Dyke turned down "Gilligan's Island" and which had him talking to his deceased mother via a car radio. The '60s also gave us Sally Field as a flying nun and sitcoms such as "The Hathaways" which featured a trio of trained chimpanzees who were treated like human children by their suburban "parents. ".

Berdasarkan laporan, it was during this era that abc decided to debut its surreal sketch comedy series "turn-on," and when i say "series," i mean single episode. The show was so poorly received that it was yanked off the air after its debut installment in 1969, and rumors have since emerged that it became the only series in TV history to be canceled while it was airing. That might be a slight exaggeration, but not by much.

Berdasarkan laporan, 1969 was the year the world watched neil armstrong and buzz aldrin land on the moon, "star trek" aired its final episode, and a man who actually did say yes to "gilligan's island," alan hale jr. paid a visit to Sally Field's aforementioned airborne nun. But the year got off to a rocky start for ABC when it debuted one of the most notorious flops in TV history.

Berdasarkan laporan, "turn-on" was created by digby wolfe and george schlatter, with the latter having created the hugely popular nbc series "rowan & martin's laugh-in," aka "laugh in," and the former having written for that same series. Their attempt to recreate the magic at ABC was a more lewd, surreal affair that aired once on Wednesday, February 5, 1969, and was never seen again.

Berdasarkan laporan, forgotten sketch comedy show "weird tv" might be the weirdest series of all time, but "turn-on" isn't far off. For one thing, its concept seemingly had little to do with comedy. Essentially, the whole thing takes place within the Construct from "The Matrix. " What does that mean? Well, in a practical sense, it means every sketch unfolds in a vast all-white vacuum, where the supercomputer supposedly responsible for the show manifests sets and characters. As one of two computer engineers explains during its opening moments, "Turn-On" is "the first computerized TV show. ".

Berdasarkan laporan, the opening sequence is a bewildering and surreal experience, featuring an array of diverse performers who appear within the construct in quick succession, including puppets and a woman who plays a sousaphone before bursting into laughter — all scored by an electronic rhythm and synth hits that apparently have little to do with what's happening on-screen. It's the kind of thing that wouldn't be out of place on Adult Swim in the 2000s. In the late-1960s? Let's just say network affiliates were concerned about their ratings.

Berdasarkan laporan, things get a bit more blue as the debut episode of "turn-on" continues. While "Laugh In" pushed boundaries, its ABC counterpart contained more sexual humor. This mixed media approach sort of calls to mind "Monty Python's Flying Circus," which also debuted in 1969. Meanwhile the show's credits continue to appear throughout the episode as suggestive cartoons pop up from time to time. And by "humor," I mean the word "Sex" flashing on-screen above guest host Tim Conway and Bonnie Boland and a "sketch" in which a woman tries desperately to get a box marked "The Pill" out of a vending machine. Unlike that now legendary series, however, "Turn-On" was cancelled almost immediately.

Sebagaimana diketahui, a stub in the february 7, 1969 edition of the oregonian (via newspapers. com) noted how local ABC affiliate KATU-TV did not air the "Turn-On" premiere at the behest of its management, who were evidently put off by a preview screening. "The station's management decided certain portions of the program 'are not in good taste and that these portions would be objectionable to a substantial and responsible part of the community,'" reads the report, which also noted that the Associated Press critic Cynthia Lowry had highlighted the "frankly blue jokes" that offended the Oregon affiliate management.

Diungkapkan bahwa abc seemed to agree, and it pulled the plug after the first episode went out. ] He convinced them to cancel the show, so by the time it got to California, the show was off the air, and some of it has never been seen. According to co-creator George Schlatter, though, the show's swift cancellation came down to a station manager in Cleveland who wanted to keep "Peyton Place," the show that would have run in the "Turn-On" time-slot, on the air. "[. "He started calling the stations as it came across the country telling them they had to cancel this show," Schlatter stated. " It's this recollection of events that seems to have birthed the "canceled while it was on the air" urban legend.

Berdasarkan laporan, the attempts at transgressive humor and surrealism in "turn-on" feel too try-hard, and the overall experience of sitting through the premiere episode is actually quite unpleasant. That said, it's not impossible to admire Schlatter and Digby Wolfe's attempt to do something different. What's more, we've gotten plenty of awful TV shows with 0% Rotten Tomatoes scores, and I'd much rather watch "Turn-On" than an episode of "Real Rob. ".

The company has since returned to TV and produced shows across different streaming platforms and networks, with its biggest recent hits including "3 Body Problem" and "Adolescence" for Netflix. But it hasn't had success across the board, as the Plan B co-produced Prime Video time travel series "Paper Girls" was canceled after one season in 2022.

Berdasarkan laporan, "paper girls" adapts a 2015-2019 image comic series by writer brian k. Vaughan and artist Cliff Chiang. The comic follows them across different time periods. At first, they're just sent to their immediate future in 2016, where they meet a grown up Erin (Ali Wong in the show). The morning after Halloween 1988 in fictional Cleveland, Ohio, suburb Sony Stream, four preteen paper girls — "new girl" Erin Tieng (Riley Lai Nelet), Tiff Quilkin (Camryn Jones) Mackenzie "Mac" Doyle (Sofia Rosinsky), and KJ Brandman (Fina Strazza) — discover a time machine in an abandoned basement. But later trips swing back and forth from prehistoric times to the far future.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, with its eight episode run, prime video's "paper girls" merely scratched that surface. Its short life sadly mirrors Vaughan's acclaimed comic "Y: The Last Man" being turned into a single-season show as well.

Sebagaimana diketahui, "paper girls" features four kids in 1980s midwest suburbia, riding on bicycles and communicating with walkie-talkies, who stumble onto a science fiction story. There are undeniable similarities to "Stranger Things," and while they're coincidental (the "Paper Girls" comic was already running when the former premiered in 2016), the story's parallels to the Duffer Brothers' Netflix phenomenon probably helped the TV show adaptation get greenlit.

Diungkapkan bahwa but compared to the 1980s nostalgia in "stranger things," "paper girls" takes a harder look at the decade. ) Compare that to "Stranger Things" Season 3, in which one character (Maya Hawke's Robin) admits she's a lesbian to another (Joe Keery's Steve), and he's totally accepting of it. (That bumpy ride is another thing the "Paper Girls" TV series didn't get a chance to realize. The very first time we meet Mac in the comic, she insults some local bullies with homophobic slurs — and she's one of the heroes! But that hatred turns out to be internalized. Across the story, Mac and KJ realize their feelings for each other. It's a nice sentiment about what things should have been like, but it's also completely ahistorical.

Berdasarkan laporan, another story that hits the same mood as "paper girls" is the 2026 time travel amblin throwback "the end of oak street" — for one, both have time-displaced dinosaurs. "Paper Girls" doesn't have as wide a mean streak as "Oak Street," though, making it a happy medium between that and how saccharine "Stranger Things" can get. If you love the "Paper Girls" TV series and crave more, I'd highly recommend the comic as the next best thing. It's a quick read at only 30 issues, and it's got the ending the TV show deserved to adapt.

#828. Forget Ganon, Zelda: Ocarina of Time’s Most Overlooked Boss Finally Gets Its Due

📅 15 Nov 2026

Forget Ganon, Zelda: Ocarina of Time’s Most Overlooked Boss Finally Gets Its Due

Tanggal: 15 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.polygon.com/zelda-ocarina-of-time-remake-twinrova/

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the age of ganon is over. It's Twinrova's turn to rule.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the legend of zelda: ocarina of time is iconic for plenty of reasons, but a big part of that is thanks to its villain. Ganondorf is one of gaming’s great bad guys, a reputation that has only been enhanced by appearances in later games like Wind Waker and Tears of the Kingdom. While Ocarina of Time’s Switch 2 remake does the Demon King justice, it’s also a reminder that the Zelda series has another excellent, and far more underappreciated, foe: Twinrova.

Berdasarkan laporan, first introduced in ocarina of time, twinrova makes for one of the best bosses in zelda history. The character concept is fun enough on its own, but the fight itself is memorable, too. In the Spirit Temple, Link encounters two evil sorceresses who serve Ganondorf, Kotake and Koume. Link has to use his Mirror Shield to absorb their elemental attacks (fire and ice) and reflect them back at the witches. They’re classic witches: a pair of bickering old ladies flying around on brooms. It all culminates with the duo coming together Transformers-style to become Twinrova, an even more powerful witch.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the sisters’ real star-turn moment happens after link vanquishes their twinrova form and they separate once more. Halos appear above both witches’ heads as they begin floating up towards a light. That sets them off into a panic as they realize they are dying, prompting an unexpectedly great sketch comedy routine.

Koume: We’re twins! Don’t try and lie about your age!.

Koume: Who are you calling senile?! Is that how you treat your older sister?.

Kotake: We are twins! How can you be older?.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the remake not only preserves that screwball dynamic, but plays it up tenfold. New animation lets Nintendo go all in on their final argument, as the two taunt and shove each other as they rise into the light. The witches are fully voice acted, and they sound exactly as you probably always imagined, speaking in cartoon squawks. It’s a delightful moment of levity right before Link’s adventure gets serious en route to Ganondorf’s castle.

Sebagaimana diketahui, all of that has left me begging for nintendo to lean on some zelda villains other than ganon in future games. Twinrova got a moment to shine as the big bad of the Oracle games, but they’ve rarely been seen in the 25 years since. There are a lot of villains like that who haven’t been revisited in decades while Nintendo keeps returning to Ganon: Agahnim, Vaati, Demise, Majora, and more. All of them are underexplored in Zelda’s mythos compared to Ganon.

Berdasarkan laporan, there’s a case to be made, of course, that villains like twinrova are so special because they’re not dragged out over and over again. They appear in games where they feel relevant to the story and design, so why force them into games just for the sake of fan service? Maybe Nintendo is better off creating new villains, like Echoes of Wisdom’s Null or A Link Between Worlds’ Yuga.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, i can get behind that, though there is a good opportunity to revisit twinrova if nintendo decides to do so. After all, the witches are 400 years old (give or take) by the time we meet them in Ocarina of Time. You can spot the younger version of Koume and Kotake in Tears of the Kingdom, and they play a role in Hyrule Warriors: Age of Imprisonment. A new game set in that era, with some incarnation of Link facing off against them, could expand the Zelda mythos in a way that feels natural. I’m down to see what hijinks the siblings were getting up to at the young age of 104.

Nintendo’s excellent Switch 2 remake recaptures the soul of a masterpiece.

#830. Naruto’s New Series Is The Perfect Chance To Finally Solve A Decade-Old Mystery

📅 15 Nov 2026

Naruto’s New Series Is The Perfect Chance To Finally Solve A Decade-Old Mystery

Tanggal: 15 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://screenrant.com/naruto-sequel-shadow-rising-rock-lee-mystery/

Sebagaimana diketahui, one of the most gratifying moments to cap off the original naruto story was seeing its protagonist's generation finally able to move forward, build new lives, and even families with one another. For some this was an exercise in celebrating fan-shipping that wound up being canon, and for others, it meant wonderfully unique stories like how Sai and Ino ultimately fell in love. But one particular mystery befuddling fans for over a decade has been that of who Rock Lee gets together with, even momentarily, to have his son, Metal Lee. Rock Lee and his son have hardly been critical in newer Naruto and Boruto stories, but it's still been a burning question.

Berdasarkan laporan, first introduced as one of the most eclectic, and certainly hardest-working young shinobi participating in the chunin exams arc, rock lee gradually began to fade into the background ever since the sasuke retrieval arc. There were certainly still moments in which he could still shine as late as the Fourth Great Ninja War, but it was clear Masashi Kishimoto hadn't seen much more purpose beyond completing his rehabilitation arc, instead giving focus to his mentor, Might Guy, who embodied many of the same principles.

Sebagaimana diketahui, but with naruto: shadow rising evidently visiting naruto's generation as they become parents, it's perhaps the biggest chance to find out who metal lee's mother is. With even the latest Boruto databook utterly snubbing the poor lad, there don't seem to be better opportunities around to explore this, especially as Boruto: Two Blue Vortex has utterly abandoned him.

Berdasarkan laporan, rock lee began his journey in naruto, becoming instantly infatuated with sakura haruno. But with Sakura staying forever loyal to Sasuke, it was clear Rock Lee's feelings would remain unrequited. Even though she never reciprocated his feelings for him, Sakura recognized his bravery and selflessness even as early as in the Forest of Death, and grew to respect him as a reliable ally to Team 7 and an asset to Konoha. At this point, there's been no conclusive proof that any known character wound up marrying him or bearing his child. Naruto: Shadow Rising is the clearest opportunity to at least provide some clarity on the enigma that is Metal Lee's mother, especially since Boruto's dodging it entirely.

Berdasarkan laporan, in the boruto manga series as well as naruto's final chapter, at most, metal lee is only ever seen training with his father or in vanishingly few panels depicting his bouts of nervousness ahead of the chunin exams, or small snippets of him in battle. The anime does as much, too, with episode #94, "A Heaping Helping! The Eating Contest!" showing him mostly with his father prepping for an eating competition. But one scene from episode #18, "A Day in the Life of the Uzumaki Family", shows young Metal and Rock Lee alongside Might Guy and Tenten, attending Naruto's Hokage inauguration day in a flashback.

The mythology of the Tailed Beasts and their Jinchuriki is central to the Naruto story, but you don't need a catchy song to remember them all.

Diungkapkan bahwa metal lee has thus been more of a filler character, appearing less frequently in the manga by comparison, but it doesn't have to be this way for the new naruto sequel. Given Shadow Rising's timeline appears to be leading to this inauguration, it's a solid opportunity to revisit more squarely on Kishimoto's terms.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, with shadow rising likely being about the story leading up to this point, kishimoto could recreate that moment, while definitively ruling out whether tenten is the mother, which at the moment seems unlikely or inconclusive. Much like the trailer showed glimpses of baby Sarada in Sakura's arms, there's also the opportunity for Rock Lee to welcome his baby son into the world. Given his passing resemblance to his father, it's unlikely Metal Lee is adopted or taken under Rock Lee's wing in a surrogate father-son bond like Guy did for him before. Whether Kishimoto reveals who the mother truly is, is up to him at this point, but for what it's worth, it's a question worth answering, even if it begets more questions about Rock Lee in the process.

Diungkapkan bahwa part of the mystique of rock lee is that he's a child utterly born without any remarkable talent or, seemingly, any living parents on record, having to pull himself up by his bootstraps and train harder than everyone around him to reach similar heights. Evidently, Kishimoto never intended to dive into the boy's lineage as it would either be a perfunctory gesture at this point, or actively undermine the core message of his character.

Berdasarkan laporan, just like how fans don't know who rock lee's parents are, naruto readers aren't so much concerned with his son's special lineage. They are simply more interested in seeing Rock Lee happily married, especially after he had to move on from Sakura. For what it's worth, the best possible answer to explain Metal's wildly different temperament, without resorting to fan-shipping his father with Sand ninja Maki or Fourth Tsuchikage Kurotsuchi, is to expect, if anything, for his mother to be a humble Konoha civilian.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, metal lee simply looks just enough like his similarly cartoonish father, with just enough of a layered, anxiety-prone personality and shape to his eyes to suggest a very different mother than the usual company rock lee keeps. Having a more grounded, down-to-earth mother to balance out a father who brings out his intensity would balance out Metal Lee rather nicely. Finally, with more civilians as opposed to ninja emerging after the end of Naruto, it'd feel understated, yet would entirely fit the core of Rock Lee's appeal, to build out a perfectly peaceful, happy ending for a Naruto character.

Berdasarkan laporan, naruto is a franchise spawned from the manga series penned by masashi kishimoto that began in 1999. Generating several tv series, games, movies, and more, Naruto follows the exploits of a young outcast ninja harboring the spirit of a demon fox who seeks to become the Hokage, the leader of his ninja village, to break the stigma against him. Upon the conclusion of the initial series, Naruto expanded into Boruto, following many series protagonists' children and returning faces.
