#881. Listen to the River! ‘Arrow for a Stone Heart’ Is a Poetic Hybrid Experience Told Through an Indigenous Lens

📅 15 Nov 2026

Listen to the River! ‘Arrow for a Stone Heart’ Is a Poetic Hybrid Experience Told Through an Indigenous Lens

Tanggal: 15 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/movies/movie-news/arrow-for-a-stone-heart-film-brazil-indigenous-lens-tallinn-1236753851/

Yes, a peccary in the forest near São Paulo is also talking to us in writer, director and cinematographer Luiza Calagian's debut feature premiering in Tallinn's Rebels With a Cause Competition - find out why.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, a pig-like creature is walking around in the territory of the indigenous guaraní on the outskirts of são paulo, brazil. And it shares what started happening to nature back in the days when the colonizers began to settle. “My name is Rete, I am a peccary,” it tells us. “One day, those who are many started arriving. ” Over time, the stones they brought started swallowing up more and more space, restricting an ancient river, plants and many creatures.

Sebagaimana diketahui, also in the indigenous territory, a woman named jera rete dreams. In her nightmares, the city invades her village. And even the river has a voice – if you are only willing to listen. Related Stories Movies 'Fatherland' Wins Top Camerimage Prize as 'Wild Horse Nine' Nabs Audience Award Lifestyle L. But there is also an old woman who keeps talking to her. A. 's Most Celebrated French Chef Is Staging a Comeback.

Sebagaimana diketahui, in her poetic debut feature, arrow for a stone heart (flecha para um coração de pedra), writer, director and cinematographer luiza calagian, in collaboration with the local guaraní indigenous community, transport us into the heart of the forest near the city. And the documentary-fiction hybrid’s narrative is very different for a reason. The way the indigenous people experience and narrate reality is different. From their perspective, myths, dreams, and relationships with non-humans connect different temporalities and perspectives.

Berdasarkan laporan, the cinematic, maybe even hallucinatory, journey that the movie takes us on elucidates the history of the community’s struggle. Cinema emerges as an opportunity for understanding and, possibly, change.

Berdasarkan laporan, arrow for a stone heart celebrates its world premiere on tuesday, nov. 17, in the Rebels with a Cause Competition of the 30th edition of the Tallinn Black Nights Film Festival (PÖFF) in Estonia.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, calagian co-wrote the film with jera rete. Ahead of the world premiere, Calagian told THR about how the idea for Arrow for a Stone Heart came about and its unique voice, look and feel. Calagian also handled cinematography and shared the editing duties with Caio De. “I kind of grew up with this film. The producers are Vinicius Toro and Sabrina Zimmermann, with Bruno Cucio serving as executive producer. It had to be told from their point of view and from their perspective rather than one that comes from the West. It’s been seven years now,” the creative explains. Utopia Docs is handling distribution and world sales. “The film began to transform as well, and at a certain point, I understood that it wouldn’t make sense for me to try to tell the story, which is the story of the Guaraní. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, so, how do you do that in a comprehensive way? “the mission became how do we bring the guaraní cosmology, the guaraní philosophy, the way that they see, organize, narrate and symbolize reality into the structure of a film, which is by its nature a western thing,” calagian tells thr. “But this also opened up the possibilities of transformation that this art has. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the first thing she started looking at was dreams. “The Guaraní are very, very, very connected to their dreams,” she explains. “They don’t understand dreams just as something that your mind creates or something that your imagination creates, but the dream for them is a form of connecting to other dimensions, other beings, other spirits, to people who are not here anymore, and to gods. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, in the process, jera became a close friend. “She also started organizing who was going to be in the film. “She embraced the project to the point that she became a co-writer,” Calagian shares with THR. She is the leader of this village, and she became not only the co-writer but also the whole heart of the film. So everything kind of revolves around Jera. The main characters other than her are her two daughters. One of the girls, her youngest, plays the river, and the older daughter, who also appears briefly at the end of the film, voiced Rete, the peccary. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa the filmmaker also fell in love with rete, the peccary. “It has a lot to do with the magic of cinema. The Guaraní say it has the capacity of moving and traveling between worlds and entering different dimensions, different perspectives and visiting the gods. And the peccary became the symbol of her production company, Mata Fechada Filmes. “For me, it is a symbol,” Calagian says. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, humans destroying the natural balance and colonization are recurring themes of arrow for a stone heart. Despite all of this destruction, there is still life in the river, which is amazing. The river, for example, is considered one of the wisest and most powerful spirits for the Guaraní. “That’s why I wanted to include this character, the river, to tell her side of the story. She represents an anthropomorphic presence. “Even before colonization, when everything was more in harmony, the Guaraní were very careful and very respectful of those river spirits because they can be dangerous – they are not to be messed with,” the filmmaker highlights. Somehow, nature finds a way to survive, even in such adverse conditions. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, even words and language were chosen with care to properly represent the indigenous people’s view of the world. “Those who are many” is one of the recurring phrases, for example. “That is the common way they call the people who invaded,” Calagian tells THR.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, she has actually worked with the guaraní for more than 10 years now, having in the past also focused on communications efforts to make their voice heard. “We were working on a campaign to make the government recognize the indigenous lands that they had inside the city, one of the biggest metropolises in the world,” the filmmaker notes. “There is a big historical dispute around the history of colonization, especially in São Paulo. There is a regional culture that celebrates the colonizers who were responsible for invading this territory, which has always been Guaraní territory. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, that’s also where the film title, arrow for a stone heart, comes from. It is not only a play on the phrase “heart of stone” for cruel or cold-hearted people but also a reference to the statues and other reminders and colonialism. “There are still a lot of historical monuments, a lot of street names, a lot of public political symbols that celebrate the colonizers, the people who killed and enslaved the indigenous people,” highlights Calagian. “We understood how important this dispute between narratives was, and that’s how this project was born. ”.

Danish actress Mathilde Arcel would be the first to admit she didn’t see this coming.

Berdasarkan laporan, it’s been hardly two months since arcel, in her first-ever leading role in a feature film, was awarded the volpi cup for best actress for her breakout performance in “woman unknown,” may el-toukhy’s riveting, post-world war ii drama that was also feted with the festival’s golden lion. Berdasarkan laporan, now, on the eve of the closing ceremony of the thessaloniki film festival, which wraps nov. 15 with el-Toukhy’s Venice winner, Arcel is taking in the news that she’s among the six nominees for best actress at the European Film Awards, whose nominations were announced Saturday afternoon in Thessaloniki.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, for arcel, whose grandmother comes from the greek island of lesvos, the award ceremony, which will be held in athens in january, feels like “a weird kind of homecoming. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa over coffee at thessaloniki’s mediterranean palace, the 30-year-old still seems awestruck by her meteoric rise. Just over two months ago, Arcel was herself a relative unknown, with a career that had mostly spanned the stage and television. Before her Venice breakout, her only appearances on the big screen were in supporting roles.

After accepting best actress honors on the Lido, Arcel revealed to Danish media that she’d been collecting unemployment benefits ahead of the Italian fest; she was on her way to report to a job center in Copenhagen when she got word that she needed to fly back to Venice for the award ceremony.

Reflecting in Thessaloniki on what she describes with wide eyes as “an adventure,” Arcel says, laughing, “It’s only downhill from here, right?”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “woman unknown” draws on accounts of the many women across europe who in peacetime were publicly shamed for their actions during the nazi occupation — women whose stories have been swept to the margins of the collective memory of world war ii. Accepting the Golden Lion in Venice, el-Touky acknowledged that the film had been “incredibly challenging to make financially, logistically, emotionally,” adding that “what kept me going was the urgent need to illuminate the unknown women of our common history, to make them known. ”.

For Arcel, that history hit close to home.

Berdasarkan laporan, “i remember my danish grandma, when i asked about the war, she told me that she was a kid on the day of the liberation, and she remembered that all of these women, her neighbors, were suddenly being pulled out onto the street. “It really stuck with me, that this was…her most vivid memory from the occupation. Other neighbors spitting at them, calling them names. Their hair was cut off,” Arcel says. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, still, until she began researching the part, the actress says she “didn’t know how vast this phenomenon was, all across europe, how these women were treated. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, in some ways, arcel might have been destined for the part; after graduating from drama school in copenhagen, she says, el-toukhy was “the first person i wrote to. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “i wrote to her that i really loved her movies and i would love to work with her. It was very different from the parts I’d played. I didn’t think it would happen,” she says. “But then she called me in for a casting. It was a new kind of challenge. I definitely didn’t think I would get it, because I felt like the role had a different vibe to it than what I thought at that time was a natural fit for me…. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, her feelings changed once she unexpectedly landed the role, and she began to discuss the part with el-toukhy. “When I read it, I couldn’t get a read on [the character of Marie] immediately,” she says. “It was kind of like detective work when I started working with her to see what kind of person she is and why she does what she does. It was intriguing. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, as with the director’s 2019 drama “queen of hearts,” which stars trine dyrholm as a successful lawyer whose life gets turned upside down by an illicit affair, arcel praises el-toukhy for her ability to craft female characters “that are complex in their morality,” something that she describes as “quite rare. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, working with the danish egyptian filmmaker was a “very collaborative process,” she adds, describing the duo as “a good team. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, “i wanted to know as much as i could about the period. “May is also very hands-on in the research. We both want to do everything we can to know as much as possible. What kind of dreams did they have at that time? What kind of movies did they watch? What kind of music did they hear?” Arcel says. ”.

Next up for Arcel is a trip to the Marrakech Film Festival, where “Woman Unknown” plays in the festival’s Horizons section, while an Oscar campaign in the best international feature category is also underway, after Denmark selected the film as its submission for the 99th Academy Awards.

Berdasarkan laporan, scripts have begun pouring in and the actress — who now has u. S. representation — has cleared her calendar for the next six months as she considers various offers.

Berdasarkan laporan, for now, it’s too soon to say what comes next. “It feels like being on the verge of something that might happen and might not even happen. A lot of dreams and hopes. “It’s very different, very exciting,” she says. Everything is open. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa the thessaloniki film festival runs nov. 5 – 15.

#889. Can You Feel It in the Air Tonight? 11 Best Moments From 2026 Rock & Roll Hall of Fame Induction Ceremony

📅 15 Nov 2026

Can You Feel It in the Air Tonight? 11 Best Moments From 2026 Rock & Roll Hall of Fame Induction Ceremony

Tanggal: 15 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.billboard.com/lists/2026-rock-roll-hall-fame-ceremony-recap-best-moments/

From Cynthia Erivo & Travis Barker doing *the* drum break justice to the Red Hot Chilli Peppers donning Rick Rubin wigs, these were our highlights.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, while many of the headlines leading up to the 2026 rock & roll hall of fame induction ceremony this weekend were about who wouldn’t be there, our highlights from saturday night’s (nov. 14) show at L. A. ’s Peacock Theatre are all about who showed up and showed out.

The night was bookended by two surprise performances, starting with 2005 inductees U2 playing a brand-new song and a classic to kick things off and ending with 2001 inductees Aerosmith joining forces with 2009 inductees Run-DMC to perform their pioneering rock/hip-hop mash-up “Walk This Way,” a top five Billboard Hot 100 smash in 1986.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, in between, a mixture of rising stars and bona fide legends showed up to either introduce or pay musical tribute to the class of 2026 — or, in some cases, the inductees themselves got in on the action. The full Wu-Tang Clan hit the stage for a medley, while Queen Latifah and MC Lyte joined forces for a joint performance celebrating their contributions as women in hip-hop, Billy Idol and his longtime guitarist Steve Stevens did one solo song and one duet with a famous face, and Peter Hook of Joy Division and New Order was surrounded by superfans for a celebration of his dual groups.

Berdasarkan laporan, the through-line of the night was innovation. While the Rock Hall has expanded far beyond the genre of rock & roll, each member of the new class has something vital in common: They changed music for generations to come.

Diungkapkan bahwa below, find billboard‘s best moments from the 2026 rock & roll hall of fame induction ceremony, which will air dec. m. 8 from 8-11 p. ET on ABC and stream on Disney+ the next day.

Diungkapkan bahwa u2 crashed the rock hall ceremony, opening the show with a surprise two-song set a day after releasing their new album, carnaval de luz. The band wasn’t on the bill — they were inducted back in 2005, their first year of eligibility — but they kicked off the night with “Silencio,” the album’s second single, joined by a line of performers dressed as riot police and carrying shields, then closed with 1984’s “Pride (In the Name of Love). ” The twofer from the Hall of Fame vets set the tone for an evening of legends only.

Diungkapkan bahwa trying to match luther vandross’ velvety vocals is a thankless task, but usher was up for the challenge, paying tribute to the late r&b legend with a smooth medley of “so amazing,” “never too much” and “here and now,” a top 10 billboard hot 100 hit in 1990. He nailed the warmth of Luther’s voice, but Usher also made sure to leave in his own signature dance moves for “Never Too Much” to make it his own.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, oprah winfrey, vandross’ friend and fan, nodded to the swag usher channeled for the performance in her induction speech, saying, “the new york times called him the king of the soul ballad. Both are so true, but I think perhaps more accurate was when Luther was named the top artist that people made love to. He was praised by critics as the Pavarotti of Pop. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, neither sade the singer nor her namesake band were in the building for their rock hall induction, but the nigerian-british icon loomed large thanks in part to an intro package that included a very complimentary drake interview, with the canadian rapper praising her “haunting” music and declaring: “there are no bad sade songs. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, case in point: the band’s 1985 top five hot 100 hit “smooth operator,” which rising british star sienna spiro covered after an introduction from fellow sade superfan andra day. “There will only be one Sade,” Day said — but fellow Londoner Spiro brought her own powerhouse vocals to the song to honor the absent superstar.

Berdasarkan laporan, in one of the most striking performances of the night, cynthia erivo covered “in the air tonight” in honor of inductee phil collins — who was previously inducted into the rock hall as part of genesis — and blink-182 drummer travis barker joined her for one of the most iconic drum breaks in all of pop music. It was a perfect illustration of the power of Collins’ career, between the excellent, haunting songwriting and the drum-forward production, and Erivo and Barker were an electric pair.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, barker also gave a speech in tribute to collins, saying of his balancing act between playing in genesis and his solo career: “he wasn’t just successful at both; he was one of the best at both. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, in his own speech, collins also put the drums center stage, noting, “i grew up wanting to play drums. Everything else has been a happy accident. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, chris rock gave a note-perfect introduction to wu-tang clan, declaring: “wu-tang didn’t leave staten island; they took it with them. ” He also added to their many catchphrases when he said, “Wu-Tang is for the children, Wu-Tang is forever, and now Wu-Tang is in the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, all nine living members attended the ceremony, with the group paying tribute to late rapper ol’ dirty bastard throughout. And for everybody that didn’t, you can kiss my inducted a–. RZA had the lengthiest speech of the group, while Method Man kept it light by saying, “I want to thank everybody that believed in us, including the Hall of Fame. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa the group also took the stage for a medley that included “c. E. A. M. R. ” and “Wu‐Tang Clan Ain’t Nuthing ta F’ Wit,” as well as ODB’s son Young Dirty Bastard taking over for his dad on “Shimmy Shimmy Ya. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, a lot of headlines ahead of saturday’s ceremony centered on who wasn’t going to be in attendance, including the previously warring, now-touring-again gallagher brothers. But Better Call Saul star Bob Odenkirk wasn’t too shocked by the news that Oasis had opted out.

Berdasarkan laporan, “anybody surprised they didn’t show up?” odenkirk asked the crowd, immediately adding, “they didn’t want to be here! it would have been out of character if they had. I would’ve worried about them. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, in his intro, odenkirk said he listened to their music to get pumped up before playing breaking bad attorney saul goodman. “I played Oasis songs every day before stepping on set. … If I needed that injection of swagger, energy, moxie, I needed a dose of Viagra for the ego. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, in oasis’ absence, stephen wilson jr. put a country-rock spin on their 1995 smash “Wonderwall. ”.

With Queen Latifah and MC Lyte both being inducted into the Rock Hall in the same year, it only made sense that their paths would overlap, just like they have in the music industry as pioneers of hip-hop.

Berdasarkan laporan, mc lyte was inducted first, with an introduction from fellow female mc remy ma, while megan thee stallion inducted queen later in the night (with a crown fittingly placed atop her head). Both women shouted each other out in their speeches — and they also shouted out their respective sororities, to big whoops from the crowd. And finally, they took the stage together for a medley of their hits (along with Meg and Remy), proving that U-N-I-T-Y always goes a long way in lifting other women up in the historically male-dominated genre.

Berdasarkan laporan, “thank you to my sisters in the name of hip-hop,” queen said during her speech. But when I heard Lyte rap, I was like, ‘Yo, what is that? I want to do that!’ … And then we met, and we just hit it off like sisters. If it wasn’t for Lyte, I don’t know if I would have known this was really possible. “Thank you, MC Lyte. We just had so much fun doing this thing we love. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, just like his unpredictable career, rick rubin also had one of the most unexpected tributes of the night. It all started with a 10-minute-plus monologue/stand-up routine from Neil Young as he led the crowd through Rubin’s winding work history and was book-ended by a speech that made up for the rock legend’s verbosity.

“You can’t kill rock & roll,” Rubin succinctly stated and then quickly left the mic.

Berdasarkan laporan, but it was a pair of musical performances that were the real rubin highlights. Then the show ended with Aerosmith and Run-DMC joining forces for the Rubin brainchild “Walk This Way. First, the Red Hot Chilli Peppers — all hysterically wearing Rubin’s signature long hair-and-beard combo — hit the stage to perform “Give It Away,” from the Rubin-produced 1991 classic album Blood Sugar Sex Magik. ” The pair of musically powerful-yet-slightly offbeat sets set just the right tone for honoring the yogi producer.

You can’t celebrate New Order without first celebrating the band’s origins as Joy Division, which is why the Rock Hall made the unusual move of giving a dual honor to the group fronted by singer Ian Curtis as well as the band that rose after Curtis’ untimely death with the remaining members.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, that twofold honor was on perfect display saturday night thanks to a performance that included bassist peter hook jamming with deftones’ chino moreno and chvrches’ lauren mayberry for joy division’s “love will tear us apart” and new order’s “bizarre love triangle. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, as trent reznor said while introducing them, “there are only two types of people in this world: those who already know just how influential joy division and new order are, and those whose favorite bands — such as u2, radiohead, the cure, the killers, nirvana, depeche mode — how different they would sound if joy division and new order never existed. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa presenter jack black let everyone know early in his speech that iron maiden wouldn’t be in the building for the rock hall ceremony (“they aren’t even here tonight because they’re rocking a world tour as they have been for the last 50 years!” he said proudly), but the metal-loving actor came bearing bad news/good news. Because performing 1983’s “The Trooper” in their stead would be “a supergroup the likes of which have never been seen. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa “i’m talking about guitar god john 5. And on lead vocals, we got St. I’m talking about Brad Wilk from Rage Against the Machine. I’m talking about Kirk Hammett and Robert Trujillo of Metallica. Vincent!”.

Berdasarkan laporan, black then mashed up all their names for this supergroup title: “give it up for the st. Rage-a-tallica 5!”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the hard rock showcase did not disappoint, with st. Vincent taking the lead and superfan Black even chiming in for some harmonies.

As the final inductee of the night, Billy Idol had a robust showcase, between an intro from No Doubt’s Gwen Stefani and Tony Kanal, a solo performance of “Rebel Yell” as well as a Stefani duet on “Eyes Without a Face,” and a 10-minute-plus speech shared with his longtime guitarist and songwriting collaborator Steve Stevens.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, and it was the joy of idol’s speech that ended the evening on a high note, with him imparting wisdom to the next potential honorees. Find out who you are and be it. Go make the impossible possible. “To all the young people out there … now it’s your turn. ”.

Oh, and one last thing: “Now I’m going to party with the Wu-Tang Clan!”.

Berdasarkan laporan, jakarta world cinema has taken its festival outside the indonesian capital for the first time, with the inaugural bandung world cinema and malang world cinema opening simultaneously on nov. 14 in two cities with large student populations and busy creative scenes.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, bandung’s screenings are taking place at cgv paris van java, while malang’s are at cinépolis malang town square, with both editions running through nov. Sebagaimana diketahui, the bandung edition is programming 203 international titles drawn from 69 countries. Cristian Mungiu’s “Fjord,” which won this year’s Palme d’Or at Cannes, opened proceedings.

Berdasarkan laporan, also on the slate are beth de araujo’s “josephine,” which took both the grand jury prize and the audience award in sundance’s u. S. Dramatic Competition in 2026, and Marine Atlan’s “La Gradiva,” winner of the AMI Paris Grand Prize at this year’s Cannes Critics’ Week. Diungkapkan bahwa the festival’s online program, available until nov. 21, includes Ildiko Enyedi’s “Silent Friend,” a Fipresci Prize winner at Venice in 2025, and Ilker Çatak’s “Yellow Letters,” this year’s Golden Bear winner at the Berlinale.

Bandung Mayor Muhammad Farhan attended the opening night at CGV Paris Van Java.

Berdasarkan laporan, “bandung world cinema gives the local audience an unprecedented opportunity to watch alternative cinema outside of the mainstream hollywood films that dominate the theaters. The hope is that this festival will foster a greater local appreciation for film, become a source of inspiration for cinephiles, and encourage aspiring filmmakers to pursue their dreams,” Farhan said.

Diungkapkan bahwa frederica, executive director of bandung world cinema, said organizers had noticed keen interest from cinephiles beyond jakarta for years. “Over the next eight days, audiences in both cities will experience the exact same caliber of bold, thought-provoking, and celebrated global cinema that defines JWC. “Bringing the Jakarta World Cinema experience to Bandung and Malang for the first time has been a long time coming,” she said. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa unlike the jakarta event, bandung will wrap on nov. 21 with a free open-air screening for the general public. Travis Barker inducted the Genesis frontman as a solo artist, while Cynthia Erivo performed "In the Air Tonight" in his place.

Sebagaimana diketahui, phil collins was inducted into the rock & roll hall of fame as a solo artist on saturday (nov. 14), and used his acceptance speech to tell the crowd he isn’t done yet. Explore Cynthia Erivo Genesis Phil Collins See latest videos, charts and news.

Berdasarkan laporan, “you haven’t heard the last of me,” collins said during the ceremony at the peacock theater in los angeles. “I promise you that. ” Related Karol G Surprises Mexico City Fans With Thalía as Special Guest: 'The First Person I Wanted to Be' Simple Plan, Hoobastank & More Take Warped Tour Mid-Flight Amid FAA Ground Stop Journey Drummer Deen Castronovo Exits Mid-Tour to Focus on His Health.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the honor marks collins’ second induction. He entered the Hall in 2010 as a member of Genesis, making him one of a small number of two-time inductees.

Diungkapkan bahwa travis barker inducted collins, highlighting his impact as a drummer. It helped define the sound of drums in the eighties, and you can still hear Phil’s influence today. ” “That sound changed everything. “I remember hearing the drums for the first time and being blown away,” the Blink-182 drummer said of “In the Air Tonight. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, barker also pointed to collins’ success with both genesis and his solo career. “He wasn’t just successful at both,” he said, “he was one of the best at both. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, collins did not perform at the ceremony. He said earlier this year that he had declined an invitation to play because he wasn’t “match-fit” enough to rehearse and sing properly, though he did not rule out returning to the stage. Cynthia Erivo performed “In the Air Tonight” in his place, with Barker on drums.

Diungkapkan bahwa in his speech, collins said he felt unprepared following a night of more polished addresses, and opened by telling the audience he’s “really not as bad as it looks. ” He said his career began with a single goal: “I grew up wanting to play drums. Everything else has been a happy accident. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, collins credited his assistant with saving his life, saying he needed to name her despite her dislike of attention. ” He said she had told him what he was doing was bad for him and what to do about it, adding that he’s “a well man now. “I’d be in a box six feet under. “I’m not joking when I say without her I wouldn’t be here,” he said. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa he also thanked longtime manager tony smith, atlantic records’ ahmet and nesuhi ertegun, and virgin records founder richard branson, who he said “took me under their wing and they saw something that was worth nurturing,” as well as “my three ex-wives, because they’ve loved me through the years and given me five great children. ” His daughter, actress Lily Collins, attended the ceremony with him.

Diungkapkan bahwa collins closed by naming eric clapton and robert plant among the musicians he has played with. “These guys were heroes to me,” he said.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the induction follows years of health issues for the 75-year-old musician. His son Nic played drums on Genesis’ 2021-22 farewell tour, with Collins singing from a seated position. A 2007 spinal injury caused nerve damage that left him unable to grip a drumstick, and he has since undergone knee surgeries and dealt with ongoing mobility problems. Collins told the BBC in January that he now has a 24-hour live-in nurse.

Diungkapkan bahwa as a solo artist, collins scored seven no. 1 hits on the Billboard Hot 100, including “Against All Odds (Take a Look at Me Now),” “Sussudio,” “One More Night” and “Another Day in Paradise. ” His albums No Jacket Required and …But Seriously both topped the Billboard 200.

Berdasarkan laporan, the 2026 rock & roll hall of fame induction ceremony airs dec. m. 8 from 8-11 p. ET on ABC and streams on Disney+ the following day.

#909. I Ain't Got No Body: The Various Non-Corporeal Aliens In Star Trek Explained

📅 15 Nov 2026

I Ain't Got No Body: The Various Non-Corporeal Aliens In Star Trek Explained

Tanggal: 15 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.slashfilm.com/2311655/star-trek-non-corporeal-aliens-explained/

Welcome to Trekspertise, a series where we break down the technology, history, details, and decisions that make the Star Trek universe so complex — and so fun.

Berdasarkan laporan, one of the primary features of "star trek" is theoretical biology. Given the wide panoply of alien species on display throughout the franchise, audiences have been invited to ponder alternate evolutionary paths besides the one that happened to bring us into being on Earth. What kind of planetary conditions would be required to form, say, a hyper-intelligent crystalline being? How did a horta evolve? What will we evolve into in the future? Will our brains adapt to become psychic over time? According to the "Star Trek: Voyager" episode "Threshold" (one of the show's most outraging to fans), it was revealed that humans will eventually evolve into giant salamanders.

Berdasarkan laporan, this leads to a few logical evolutionary extremes, like the fact that some species on "star trek" have evolved into beings of pure energy. To cite a notable example: In the original series episode "Is There In Truth No Beauty?," audiences were introduced to the Medusans, a highly intelligent, telepathic, and empathic species whose light-constructed bodies are so wildly complex that any human looking at them would instantly go mad. "Star Trek" has many examples of non-corporeal aliens who can only be perceived as light, as a psychic presence, as a sound, or as a vision beamed directly into our inferior, corporeal brains. Only a mentally disciplined species like the Vulcans could look at a Medusan, and even then required a special filtered visor (pictured above).

These kinds of aliens expand the audience's mind as to what can be considered life.

Diungkapkan bahwa in looking at fictional non-corporeal species, "star trek" expands our horizons. We're invited to ponder new perspectives about basic concepts like evolution, time, the nature of consciousness, and, perhaps, our own relationship to the cosmos. Non-corporeal entities are one of the coolest ideas "Star Trek" has to offer, and their recurring nature is a constant reminder that life is more complex, and the cosmos more ineffable, than we could ever hope to imagine.

Sebagaimana diketahui, on "star trek," non-corporeal aliens tend to appear as lights or clouds or glowing mists of energy. " That entity had the ability to sort of intuitively communicate with Cochrane (Glenn Corbett), and could also heal diseases and sustain human life beyond its usual biological barriers. Others might immediately think of Zefram Cochrane's glowing, cloud-like "companion" in the episode "Metamorphosis. One might recall the smoke-like alien that made Kirk nervous in the episode "Obsession," one of the more underrated episodes of the show. A common theme of non-corporeal entities on "Star Trek" is that they are godlike and powerful, able to tap into the powers of the universe in ways we don't understand.

Diungkapkan bahwa the medusans may be one of the most popular non-corporeal entities on "star trek," but fans of "deep space nine" would surely want me to acknowledge the wormhole aliens, a. a. k. The Prophets. In that show's pilot episode, "Emissary," Benjamin Sisko (Avery Brooks) travels into a stable wormhole and encounters bodiless creatures who can only communicate with him by appearing as people from his memories.

Berdasarkan laporan, the wormhole aliens from "deep space nine" are so, well, alien, they don't understand concepts like linguistic communication or linear time. They don't see cause leading to effect, but rather a widespread series of events that happen all at once. Sisko has to do the impossible, and explain the human habit of seeing time as a straight line.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, and, of course, there are many species of godlike beings on "star trek" who often take the form of humans, despite not having physical bodies. Those two beings tend to see corporeal humans as lesser species and amuse themselves by taunting and playing with them. Kevin took the form of a human, married, and witnessed his wife killed, leading him to, in a moment of ill-temper, commit instant galaxy-wide genocide of a single species. Less whimsical is Kevin Uxbridge (John Anderson), a member of a powerful energy species called the Douwd. He's the deadliest character in all of "Star Trek. Q (John de Lancie) from "Star Trek: The Next Generation" is one of these beings, as is Trelane (William Campbell) from the original series. ".

Diungkapkan bahwa the list goes on. Q tormented the Calamarain, which exist as ionized gas. There are the Organians, the Lights of Zetar, and the godlike Metrons, the latter of whom oversaw the fight between Kirk (William Shatner) and the Gorn in the episode "Arena," and plenty of other examples. In most cases, non-corporeal entities are so far beyond human experience, it's difficult to communicate with them, much less come to some kind of diplomatic understanding.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, but sometimes non-corporeal entities do become our friends. On "Star Trek: Prodigy," the character of Zero (Angus Imrie) is a Medusan who managed to construct a robot-like vehicle for themselves, allowing them to interact with us flesh-beings without exposing themselves. Sometimes the ineffability of the cosmos works in our favor.

Tanggal: 15 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://collider.com/rivals-season-2-part-2-aidan-turner-victoria-smurfit-emily-atack/

Berdasarkan laporan, greer riddell is a london-based film and television journalist writing about comedy, streaming and the evolving media industry in the uk and usa. She works at Collider, covering the latest in film, television and entertainment through interviews, features, reviews and industry coverage.

Sebagaimana diketahui, her recent brand collaborations include hbo, warner bros. , Netflix, Hulu, Sky, Disney+ and DC Studios. She has covered titles including Saturday Night Live UK, Rivals, Scrubs, Stuart Fails to Save the Universe, Ludwig, Supergirl and Stranger Things.

Her recent interviews include Florence Pugh, Mike Faist and Christopher Abbott for Netflix's East of Eden, Taika Waititi and Jenna Ortega for Klara and the Sun.

Berdasarkan laporan, editor's note: the following contains spoilers for rivals season 2, episodes 7-9. It's been a long wait since June to find out whether Tony Baddingham (David Tennant) and Maud O'Hara (Victoria Smurfit) will get their comeuppance after their affair led to Monica Baddingham (Claire Rushbrook) dying in a car accident during a storm. Rivals is never short of drama, and that's not all for the Baddinghams, as it was revealed earlier in the season that Sarah Stratton's (Emily Atack) baby is also Tony's illegitimate child.

Diungkapkan bahwa to explore these cliffhangers and more, collider joined aidan turner, smurfit, and atack to discuss the first three explosive episodes of rivals season 2, part 2. They break down Declan and Maud's extraordinary argument on Bonfire Night and reveal whether Declan will finally give in to the urges he's been repressing out of fierce loyalty to his wife. Atack shares why she enjoys playing Sarah at her most vulnerable and why the most confident characters are often not what they seem. The trio also reveal what goes on behind the scenes on the Rivals set and whether being part of a series that's so much fun to watch is equally enjoyable to film.

Sebagaimana diketahui, collider: well, i didn't think rivals could get more dramatic, but the last three episodes, they've really blown it out of the water. And I have to ask first: that big showdown between Maud and Declan. Have you recovered from that? In the kitchen?.

SMURFIT: I was just saying my hips are still sore!.

TURNER: [Laughter] I feel really bad about that.

TURNER: Well, I kept on hitting the dirt.

SMURFIT: It's only a hairy second, isn't it?.

Berdasarkan laporan, turner: i kept throwing you down quite hard. It’s one of those ones.

TURNER: It's a year ago now; it still hurts.

Diungkapkan bahwa smurfit: she does. Anyway, so yes, it was great. So, it was like all the emotions, all the justifications, all the failings, all the passion, all. It was weirdly fun to do because it was such a juicy, beautifully written scene. you know, it was just, oh, it was just juicy, wasn't it?.

SMURFIT: You don't get many of those in your career.

Sebagaimana diketahui, turner: you don't. I find when I work, it just all goes a bit weird, and there was a strange energy in the air, and I kind of went wild. Maybe it was a full moon or something, but I felt a bit crazed that night. It's also, not that this should really matter — but it kind of does for me — it was a night shoot, and there's something that happens at nighttime. Did you?.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, smurfit: well, yeah. You kept feckin’ me in a fire!.

Is that something that you do as an actor to get yourself into that sort of big emotional state? Because you're really asked to go from zero to 11 in a really quick space of time.

Sebagaimana diketahui, turner: yeah. Sometimes I think we split the scene where he runs out, but you're in the moment from moment to moment. Yeah. I mean, you just kind of do it, but it's also like, you want to stay present. So you can't play what's ahead of you.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, smurfit: when you know where you're starting and the stuff that's behind you, you don't think about what's coming. You know where you're at, and then you put your foot on the gas, and you're playing with great actors, then it's all just sort of there.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, there's a few moments, actually, in that where declan was stood in the trees and him obviously being incredibly angry there. There were times where it was quite similar to the visuals we got of Tony and him being really angry. So I wondered if that was a conscious decision, or you thought about, actually, is Declan going to get to that Tony level of anger throughout?.

Sebagaimana diketahui, turner: he did get really angry. I think he completely lost control.

Sebagaimana diketahui, turner: i was just saying earlier, i mean, which i sort of forgotten about, but i feel thankful there were other people around. I feel really scared when I think of what he would have done had no one else been there to stop him. It was a kind of blind anger he had.

Sebagaimana diketahui, i'm looking forward to seeing what happens when sarah's secret fully comes out because it's been teased. A few people know. But when Tony actually finds out that has gone around the whole village, that's going to be mad. That's going to be another confrontation, I think! But I wanted to ask you, what's something you enjoy the most? Is it playing somebody who's really confident or at their most exposed? Because there are a lot of scenes in this where you're having some quite emotional moments.

Diungkapkan bahwa atack: yeah, i was really grateful for that. I think she's learned to be a certain way. She has to be a certain way to survive in the world that she's in. And, yeah, women like Sarah are definitely that. And I think what it touches on is the obvious thing that so many outwardly confident people are often inside, kind of, battling something else, battling vulnerability. You know, a male-dominated world, the world of telly.

Berdasarkan laporan, i think that what's so great about the writing is characters like sarah, who would have been so unlikable in other tv shows, but there's something about this. There's something about Rivals where you really root for people that are making all these terrible mistakes and making all these mental decisions.

Diungkapkan bahwa i was really happy when i read the script that we got to expose that vulnerability underneath all the hair and the makeup and the confidence and sexiness. Because that's kind of true to life, really. Not me, just [laughs] confident people; they're often covering something.

The two stars of the Hulu series also break down their characters' toxic relationship.

Berdasarkan laporan, so now that declan has found out that maud and tony have been an item, he has obviously been very loyal to maud before. Does this mean he might have a change of heart? May he explore seeing if Cameron's still interested? Is he going to explore some of those urges?.

Diungkapkan bahwa turner: i don't know what urges he's going to explore, but i think it's going to be difficult for him to come to terms with this. I think it's been really hard on him, and that's going to continue. There's obviously so much love there, and they have this really strong connection, and there's been things in the past — different infidelities and affairs that they've managed to wade through, but this feels different this time. I don't know if he's going to be able to forgive. I think she hurt him in the most fundamental. So, I don't know how it's going to play out. Maybe he will. I don't know.

Is there a behind-the-scenes moment for you that really sums up what it's like to have been a part of that set? Because it looks really fun from where we're watching at home.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, smurfit: i think a lot of the memories, when we do. in a lot of the episodes, we have a set piece, as we call it, which is most of the cast all together at a Hunt Ball, at the polo, you know, all these different set pieces. And it's usually got an incredible story. Everyone's together, so they'll pull this group of people in, and the rest are held in the tent or in a room, and invariably what's happening is games of chess, games of cards, games of— what was that spy game that Brendan Patricks always brings?.

Sebagaimana diketahui, smurfit: codenames, where you're — it's basically like the traitors — all lying. And it's so fun to watch everybody dip into the game; they're called, they go off to work, and then just somebody else will take over the game that they're playing. And, and so there are all these tables full of different, different actors sitting together playing the games. And it's like a big, weird family, dysfunctional children, and absolutely no adults.

You just made me think, actually, that all of the characters in Rivals, they'd be too good at playing The Traitors because they'd all be good at lying, and no one would be able to identify them.

ATACK: It's kind of like they are playing The Traitors!.

Sebagaimana diketahui, turner: i don’t know if declan would be very good at lying. Maybe not him, but, yeah, everyone else, maybe!.

Berdasarkan laporan, it feels impossible to do justice to the late sir patrick stewart with mere words, but we can attempt it. One part of his incredible legacy is voice acting; how could he not try his hand there when he had such a magnificent voice? Stewart's defining voice role is probably the eccentric CIA Deputy Director Avery Bullock on "American Dad. " Casting him against type there is the whole joke. Patrick Stewart, famous for playing dignified, fatherly authority figures like Captain Jean-Luc Picard and Professor Charles Xavier, is the one saying all of Bullock's ridiculous, profane, and unhinged lines, which become even funnier read in his baritone voice.

Berdasarkan laporan, the folks behind the biblical epic "the prince of egypt" also knew the weight stewart's voice carried. Patrick Stewart plays Pharaoh Seti, adoptive father of Moses and the man who ordered the massacre of Hebrew babies that made Moses' mother send him away. At Steven Spielberg's suggestion, DreamWorks Animation adapted the first stretch of the Book of Exodus, or how the prophet Moses (Val Kilmer) — raised as an Egyptian prince — discovered his true heritage and led his people out of bondage. Stewart/Seti has only a few scant scenes in the movie's first act, but he casts a shadow as wide as any pyramid over the rest of the film.

Sebagaimana diketahui, as with later dreamworks pictures, "the prince of egypt" employs celebrity voice casting: kilmer as moses, ralph fiennes as moses' brother/seti's son pharaoh rameses, etc. But here, it mostly works — mostly. Jeff Goldblum as Moses' brother Aaron is a distracting bit of casting where you hear the actor first, not the character. "Prince of Egypt" doesn't disguise Stewart's voice either (you probably couldn't with a voice of such power), but it complements his character to a chilling effect.

Diungkapkan bahwa in "the prince of egypt," seti first appears admonishing his two sons for being reckless in a chariot race. " When Moses asks his father to go easier on Rameses, Seti offers understanding (and pure dramatic irony): "Moses, you will never have to carry a burden like the crown I will pass to Rameses. He's especially harsh on his heir, Rameses, explaining that "one weak link can break the chain of a mighty dynasty. ".

Berdasarkan laporan, pretty typical patrick stewart, right? seti is stern but reasonable, some of the same qualities that made captain picard such a respected leader. His respect-commanding voice is even more effective as a disappointed father, too; would you want to hear "I'm disappointed in you" from that voice?.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, but then moses learns the truth about where he came from, and how. Seeing his son in despair, Seti is gentle but also doesn't deny he had a generation of Hebrew babies murdered as population control. The animation and Stewart's performance work in perfect sync. In Seti's whispered tone, he sounds genuinely pained. Even if his claim "sometimes, for the greater good, sacrifices must be made," rings hollow here, Seti's thousand yard stare tells us that maybe he does feel the weight of what he did and realizes he's damned for it.

Berdasarkan laporan, but then the kicker comes: he tries to "comfort" moses that the babies cast into the nile "were only slaves. " The dissonance of Seti loving his own family and also being a genocidal enslaver is potent, but sadly believable. Fittingly, this is also the last time we see him in the film, because the bond he shared with Moses has been severed.

Sebagaimana diketahui, "the prince of egypt" is one of the most gorgeously animated films ever made, and it's not only the animation that's beautifully crafted. The storytelling is sharp and mature. It sits at the very fine line of being simple enough for kids and complex enough for adults; Moses and Rameses being turned from beloved brothers to enemies by forces much bigger than themselves is painful to watch.

Berdasarkan laporan, right off, "the prince of egypt" is an unconventional title for the exodus story; after all, the whole story is about moses rejecting that life for his people by birth. (Compare it to the 1956 biblical epic titled "The Ten Commandments. ") But the movie paints Moses' deliverance of his people as bittersweet, since it cost him the brother he loved.

Diungkapkan bahwa though not nearly as controversial as nikos kazantzakis's book (and later martin scorsese's film) "the last temptation of christ," "the prince of egypt" similarly invents human drama from scripture. So, then, wouldn't he be afflicted by man's foibles and doubts? The Book of Exodus holds that Moses was raised as an Egyptian in the Pharaoh's own family. "Last Temptation" works from the tenet that Jesus was both fully divine but also fully human. Wouldn't Moses, then, feel pained about having to turn his back on the home where he was raised, even if he recognized the necessity of God's plan for him?.

Diungkapkan bahwa part of the tragedy is that this only flows one way. After Moses learns the truth, he can't look at the enslaved Hebrew workers without thinking their birthright is also his. Conversely, neither Seti nor Rameses clock that the son/brother they love would've been just another of those slaves. It's an excellent use of Patrick Stewart, twisting our relationship to his fatherly presence and providing an undercurrent of darkness to it.

Diungkapkan bahwa there's something of a paradox when it comes to making legitimately good crime action movies. On the one hand, most filmmakers want the action to be as accurate and based in reality as possible, whether it be robbing a bank, taking down a security truck, or whatnot. On the other hand, they don't necessarily wish to inspire criminals who would copycat a crime they happened to see in a movie, especially as that's an instance where all publicity doesn't necessarily equal good publicity. (Remember the brouhaha over a crime allegedly inspired by 1995's "Money Train," a case which only just reached a resolution a few years ago?).

Berdasarkan laporan, the irony of the new crime action film "how to rob a bank" is that it intentionally wishes to exist on the edge separating these two sides. wealth gap, decide to become bank robbers. The film, written by Mark Bianculli and directed by David Leitch, concerns a group of friends who, upon becoming radicalized by the various injustices of the current U. S. Their gimmick is hiding their crimes in plain sight, filming themselves in the act and detailing exactly how they did it for their YouTube channel (all while hiding their identities, naturally).

Berdasarkan laporan, thus, leitch and bianculli have to include a bunch of real-world tactics and hardware without going too far. e. To help accomplish this, they have their bandits (who've dubbed themselves the Wolf Pack) borrow a technique from the sequel to the bonafide action classic that is "Die Hard," i. 1990's "Die Hard 2. " And while the characters never mention the movie on-screen, the inclusion of a trick used by that film's villains works as both an Easter egg homage to that movie as well as a bit of real-world verisimilitude, as this particular tactic does sound like it could actually work.

Berdasarkan laporan, in "die hard 2," the terrorists holding washington dulles international airport hostage around christmas are former u. After Bruce Willis' John McClane their plans while getting a quip or two in, the airport brass call in a military counter-terrorism unit. Then, during the subsequent firefights between the counter-terrorism unit and the terrorists, each group makes a point of switching to clips for their machine guns labeled with blue instead of red stripes. S. Army soldiers who've been corrupted by a military drug lord. Eventually, McClane discovers this code means blue for blank rounds and red for live rounds, revealing that both units are working together.

Diungkapkan bahwa while the terrorists in "die hard 2" have devised a fairly elaborate scheme, the blank-vs-live rounds element seems fairly simple and self-explanatory. The Wolf Pack want to make their robberies feel threatening to the authorities they encounter and only elect to use live rounds to save their own skins. In other words, it has an authenticity about it, which is why its use in "How to Rob a Bank" feels smooth rather than belabored. As such, adopting the blue and red labeled gun clips makes for an easy to understand visual code, so much so that the characters in the film barely have to explain it to the audience.

Berdasarkan laporan, for those who know "die hard 2," this is a cute easter egg calling back to that film's intuitive code system. Who knows if anyone has used it (or will) in real life, but it helps "How to Rob a Bank" exist on that edge.

Berdasarkan laporan, it's a rare thing when two equally well-known artists collaborate behind the camera. That latter director, as it happens, isn't a stranger to blending his creative DNA with another filmmaker. This year alone, we've seen the news that Steven Soderbergh is helping out Matt Reeves with "The Batman Part II," while Quentin Tarantino has handed the "Once Upon a Time in Hollywood" character of Cliff Booth over to David Fincher for the upcoming Netflix spin-off. An auteur director team-up doesn't happen often, but it's certainly not unheard of. Famously, Fincher took over the troubled "Alien 3" after it had been developed for years, and inherited a script structure from director Vincent Ward that he isn't thrilled with to this day.

Diungkapkan bahwa around the same time, the budding film auteur (who was then still primarily known as a music video director) was approached to make a video for the rock star meat loaf's 1993 single "i'd do anything for love (but i won't do that). (That's one version of the story, at least; more on that later. " However, Fincher's price tag caused Meat Loaf to look elsewhere for the video's director, turning to none other than an up-and-coming Michael Bay. " According to Craig Marks and Rob Tannenbaum's 2011 book "I Want My MTV: The Uncensored Story of the Music Video Revolution," Fincher and Meat Loaf's vision was pretty much what the finished video became, a Gothic riff on "Beauty and the Beast. ) Though the two didn't directly work together on it, the final video is, in its own weird way, a collaboration between the pair.

Berdasarkan laporan, although michael bay and david fincher technically worked together at the production company propaganda films, their relationship was definitely more complex than just coworkers or collaborators. As various colleagues and other luminaries who worked at or with Propaganda detail in "I Want My MTV," Fincher was already a star internally given his extensive work on numerous successful music videos, and this was something that the young Bay was all too aware of. Employees told Craig Marks and Rob Tannenbaum that Bay would follow Fincher around the Propaganda offices constantly, with some people already considering him a younger version of Fincher.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, this comparison came to a head when meat loaf approached fincher with the gig for "i'd do anything for love. " According to Meat Loaf, the musician pitched Fincher with a "Beauty and the Beast" premise for the video, which Fincher allegedly loved. However, Fincher supposedly gave Meat Loaf a quote of $2. 3 million, which Loaf balked at. He continued:.

Diungkapkan bahwa "so he came back a few days later and gave me a budget of $1. ' And Fincher said, 'Well then, get Michael Bay. 7 million. ' That's the last time Michael Bay was the cheaper option. I said, 'David, we don't have that kind of money. ".

So, in Meat Loaf's version of the tale, the vision for the music video was the singer's idea, Fincher couldn't make the budget work, and the then-cheaper Bay got a hand-me-down project which he spun into a hit video.

Berdasarkan laporan, in meat loaf's version of what happened with the "i'd do anything for love (but i won't do that)" music video, the video was an idea had by the singer which changed hands from david fincher to michael bay. However, according to Propaganda Films producer Joni Sighvatsson, it was his idea to pass the torch from Fincher to Bay, and as such, the video ended up being the one and only collaboration between the two filmmakers. As he recalled:.

Diungkapkan bahwa "fincher was very expensive. He and the label were at an impasse over the Meat Loaf video, so I said, 'Why don't we just give this to Michael Bay?' Fincher gave it to Bay, we ended up spending $750,000, and it was a seminal video. That was the first and last time Fincher and Bay collaborated. Michael directed, and it was David's concept. ".

Sebagaimana diketahui, it's very possible that sighvatsson is merely aggrandizing the story of the "i'd do anything for love" video, making it sound like it's the result of two now-famous auteurs rather than just one. It's the most perfect visual encapsulation of Meat Loaf's sound, all theatricality and opera. Or it's possible that he and Meat Loaf have hazy memories of what went down and how. It's got Bay's fingerprints all over it, of course, from a fetishization of hardware and sunsets to the way every woman is shot like a supermodel. All we really have to go on is the video itself, which remains one of the most visually rapturous short films of the 1990s. Yet the video's Gothic flavor and trappings feel more Fincheresque. However it happened, the video is a gift, and we should probably thank all three men for it.

#923. Grey's Anatomy's Downfall Can Be Traced Back To One Moment

Diungkapkan bahwa "grey's anatomy" has been on the air since 2005, which is to say that it's experienced a handful of high highs and very low lows. Shonda Rhimes' medical drama, which premiered as a humble mid-season replacement and became one of the longest-running shows in the history of its medium, stars Ellen Pompeo as surgical intern turned award-winning general surgery attending and hospital owner Dr. Meredith Grey, who lives, loves, and learns alongside her colleagues and who has a knack for picking up cases that connect to her personal life in some way (as all of the doctors do, honestly).

Berdasarkan laporan, (i say it "stars" pompeo, but there's a technicality here; pompeo technically left "grey's anatomy" as a series regular in season 19 in 2022, but still provides voiceover and appears on the show often enough that she's still the main character for all intents and purposes. ).

Diungkapkan bahwa there are, if i'm being honest, many parts of "grey's anatomy" that one could identify as a major series downfall, like the time dr. The issue? Many of those lows are followed by highs (as Heigl's Izzie leaves the series, there's a hospital merger followed by a two-part finale in Season 6 that's a legitimate series highlight). Isobel "Izzie" Stevens (Katherine Heigl) has ghostly physical intimacy with her dead fiancé before figuring out it's a brain tumor, the time a plane crash kills most of the show's surgeons, or every time a wedding is interrupted by a dramatic, ridiculous problem. That's why I'm pointing to a true point of no return for "Grey's Anatomy," and I am truly sorry to say that, despite my respect for the show's commitment to "realism" during a terrifying time for the entire world, the 17th season of the medical drama, also known as the "COVID season," is its downfall.

Berdasarkan laporan, at face value, it makes total sense for a show like "grey's anatomy" to address the very real covid-19 pandemic head-on; because the characters also dressed in protective medical gear, there was an air of practicality to the whole thing to boot. Partway through Season 17, Meredith develops a pretty serious case of COVID-19, which sidelines her (and, to an extent, Ellen Pompeo) for the remainder of the season's run, giving her a truly bizarre storyline where she sees dead loved ones in dreams in a random seaside location that fans like me simply refer to as the "coma beach. ".

Sebagaimana diketahui, instead, fans of the series couldn't escape the pandemic surrounding them, and to make things worse, the show's best quality — its genuinely funny and smart dialogue — fell by the wayside in the process. Meredith may have eventually recovered from her severe case of COVID-19 and left the coma beach behind after Season 17, but the show wasn't able to pull off the same feat. and as it continues, you can feel the slip in quality with each passing season.

Berdasarkan laporan, i know better than most people that "grey's anatomy" has its fair share of detractors; i've been watching this damn show since it premiered, and it's one of the longest relationships of my life without comparison. I'll be among the first to admit that a lot of it is heightened and silly — and I got the chance to interview a friend who's a real doctor for this very site, who confirmed that it's the least realistic televised medical drama by a country mile.

Sebagaimana diketahui, still, i'll go to the mat for a lot of seasons and episodes of "grey's anatomy. The chemistry between most of the original actors was undeniably great, its jokes often hit their mark beautifully, and remember that two-part Season 6 finale I mentioned? "Sanctuary" and "Death and All His Friends," which chronicles a devastating mass shooting within the walls of the central hospital, is one of my favorite TV episodes ever. " Shonda Rhimes, while she was still hands-on with the series, was a masterful dialogue writer and gave actors like Sandra Oh (who left the series after the Season 10 finale) unbelievably sharp monologues with regularity. and I'd stack it against plenty of prestige dramas any day.

Diungkapkan bahwa that's what makes the fall of "grey's anatomy" particularly painful for me. Instead of quippy dialogue that feels like a tennis match, characters over-explain everything in the preachiest way possible (like a female doctor explaining to a male counterpart that women get Brazilian butt lifts because society influences them into it). I'm committed to the proverbial bit by still watching it, but it's painful. "Grey's Anatomy" is a pale shadow of what it once was, and it all started in Season 17.

People enter hoping to serve their sentences and eventually leave. Tom Fontana, who created the series, makes the prison's supposedly progressive ambitions feel like a particularly cruel joke. Some barely survive their first week.

Sebagaimana diketahui, but cyril o'reily (scott william winters) is the character whose suffering i find hardest to accept. The institution promises justice but repeatedly manufactures more suffering. And that's the horrible thing about Oz. It doesn't ask us to pretend these prisoners are innocent. Beecher becomes increasingly brutal just to survive. Watching Ryan desperately try to save the one person who loves him unconditionally is devastating, especially knowing how much suffering Ryan himself has caused. Living with a brain injury and dependent on his manipulative brother Ryan (Dean Winters), Cyril is drawn into murder and eventually faces execution. I've watched countless television characters lose everything. Cyril never fully understands the machinery determining his fate. It makes us recognize their humanity even after confronting their worst actions. Few have frightened me like the men of Oz, because even surviving their punishment can mean losing whatever remains of themselves.

#928. 7 Best Things About the Original Xbox That Aren't Halo, Ranked

📅 15 Nov 2026

7 Best Things About the Original Xbox That Aren't Halo, Ranked

Tanggal: 15 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.polygon.com/xbox-retrospective-best-things-besides-halo/

Sebagaimana diketahui, when microsoft entered the console market with its xbox brand, people outside the company didn’t necessarily have high hopes. Throughout the 1990s, the industry was dominated by Japanese hardware companies like Nintendo, Sega, and Sony. But Microsoft meant business, and its first console effort provided some excellent reasons to give the brand a chance.

Diungkapkan bahwa one of the best reasons to own an xbox was undoubtedly halo: combat evolved, with a compelling first-person campaign and a multiplayer mode that kept people busy for dozens or even hundreds of hours. Bungie’s sci-fi epic shifted a lot of hardware units, but it wasn’t the only reason for players to be excited. Here are seven of the best things about the original Xbox that aren’t Halo.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the xbox came out during a difficult time for sega. The company had just ended an unfortunate string of hardware failures that concluded with the death of the Dreamcast, its final console. That platform had offered all sorts of great games, but they didn’t connect with wide audiences because everyone was too focused on the PlayStation 2, which offered a built-in DVD player that made it a particularly attractive prospect.

Berdasarkan laporan, microsoft offered sega a way to present its own vision for a console future without devoting all of its resources to challenging hardware. A string of terrific Sega titles hit the Xbox during its early years, and Microsoft promoted them aggressively, from Jet Set Radio Future to Sega GT 2002 and even more niche affairs like Gun Valkyrie. That support persisted throughout the console’s life, and also produced Panzer Dragoon Orta, one of the very finest games on the system.

Diungkapkan bahwa commercial tie-ins weren’t huge news by the time burger king released a series of three video games near the end of the xbox life-cycle. They had been around for some time, particularly during the Atari 2600 era. In 1983, Chase the Chuck Wagon even built a game around a dog chasing a wagon, which consumers obtained by sending in UPC labels clipped from bags of Purina dog food.

Sebagaimana diketahui, burger king brought that convention back with sneak king, pocketbike racer, and big bumpin’. To get a copy, players paid a small fee while placing an order for a value meal. At the time, Burger King advertised heavily in print and on TV with its creepy “king” character, who featured in each of the games. The games worked on both the original Xbox and the newer 360, a cross-generation wonder that people have largely forgotten.

Sebagaimana diketahui, players naturally associate microsoft with halo, which it published on behalf of bungie. Fable, from Lionhead Studios, kicked off another successful franchise that’s scheduled to return early in 2027 with a reboot from Playground Games. But the giant publisher also took chances on less conventional fare during the era.

Diungkapkan bahwa one such game was kung fu chaos, which offered a parody of ‘70s b-movie chaos. In a slapstick fighting brawler along the lines of Power Stone, players survived perilous environments and talked trash to their opponents until one fighter emerged the victor. The edgy humor doesn’t hold up well today, but plenty of players had fun with it at the time.

Berdasarkan laporan, other unusual releases from the time included phantom dust, a deck builder with 3d arena battles, and voodoo vince. The latter was a platformer featuring a voodoo doll roaming New Orleans. To harm enemies, he had to inflict damage on himself through dangerous maneuvers, like setting himself on fire. Players never knew quite what to expect from Microsoft Game Studios at the time, and it was wonderful.

Diungkapkan bahwa first released on nov. 15, 2001, the original Xbox missed the ‘90s by only a little bit. As it helped define the 2000s gaming scene, it did so with help from one powerful component: the hard drive.

Sebagaimana diketahui, players suddenly had a lot of space to store their game saves. They could install them directly to the device, no longer relying on separate memory cards. If they preferred, they could also rip audio CDs to the drive and then play their favorite titles accompanied by their favorite music. You haven’t lived until you’ve played Dead or Alive Xtreme Beach Volleyball while Creed, Nickelback, and Avril Lavigne croon in the background.

Berdasarkan laporan, unlike today, when a required install for a game like grand theft auto 6 can eat up roughly a third of your available space on a playstation 5, the original xbox supported large libraries without flinching. That made it an especially good time to be an Xbox fan.

Diungkapkan bahwa formerly known as tehkan, the game publisher that became tecmo (and later koei tecmo) published its first original console game on the famicom in 1986. Traditionally a Japanese publisher, the company nevertheless made a name for itself in North America, thanks in large part to the classic Ninja Gaiden series.

Berdasarkan laporan, unexpectedly, tecmo threw considerable support behind the xbox hardware, and with excellent results. Ninja Gaiden (later released in an expanded form as Ninja Gaiden Black) became one of the hardware’s biggest successes. Tecmo also brought over the excellent Dead or Alive fighting game series, which felt like the perfect match for Microsoft’s powerful system. The beautiful environments and the detailed fighters within them provided ample eye candy to remind players that console gaming had come a long way since the 8-bit figures they remembered stomping on turtles only a decade prior.

Graphics were still a huge differentiator, and Tecmo was arguably the era’s developer that did the most to prove the Xbox was a graphical powerhouse.

Diungkapkan bahwa a weekly cheat sheet to what you’ll eventually love to play. No buying, no commitment — just saving for later.

Diungkapkan bahwa console gaming had a certain feel to it by the time the xbox arrived, and microsoft quickly pushed some boundaries. Today, many games release on PC alongside their console counterparts, but that wasn’t the case back in 2001, when Xbox began building bridges across some of the biggest gaps.

Diungkapkan bahwa on xbox, we got to see some games that surprised us, like the elder scrolls 3: morrowind, star wars: knights of the old republic, and even sid meier’s pirates. Microsoft also published versions of the original Fable across the two platforms, and the role-playing epic felt just right on both. And MechAssault made a big splash when Xbox Live launched, proving the power of the hardware to provide compelling online play experiences.

Berdasarkan laporan, the dreamcast deserves credit for making some early efforts in the same arena, but the xbox stuck the landing. In the process, it set Microsoft up to enjoy the even more successful generation that followed with the Xbox 360.

Berdasarkan laporan, by the time the xbox came around, the strong relationship between rare and nintendo had soured enough that the time was ripe for someone else to swoop in and acquire the most storied software developer in twycross, england. Microsoft saw the opportunity and went for it.

Sebagaimana diketahui, although it has failed to capitalize on the rare acquisition the way people once thought it might, microsoft did acquire some early gems in the years before sea of thieves. The latter served as one of the final Microsoft releases on its first console. Grabbed by the Ghoulies and Conker: Live & Reloaded both launched on the original Xbox. A remake of the surprisingly vulgar Nintendo 64 classic, it provided not only a visual overhaul of the single-player campaign, but multiplayer modes that kept players busy fragging each other for hours at a time.

Berdasarkan laporan, most of rare’s post-nintendo triumphs came during the xbox 360 era, but its earliest efforts on the original xbox are solid games that hold up reasonably well today. They didn’t exactly set the world on fire, but they’re fun to revisit even now. You can still acquire them on the Xbox Store today, and they’re well worth a look.

Diungkapkan bahwa disc-to-digital is either a genuine players-first initiative or a swipe at sony. Either way, I'll take it.
