#997. Brand New Day Was Great, But Marvel Still Hasn't Done 1 Thing With Tom Holland's Spider-Man

📅 15 Nov 2026

Brand New Day Was Great, But Marvel Still Hasn't Done 1 Thing With Tom Holland's Spider-Man

Tanggal: 15 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://screenrant.com/spider-man-brand-new-day-mcu-no-standalone-movie/

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, as impeccable as spider-man: brand new day is, there’s still one thing the marvel cinematic universe hasn’t achieved with tom holland’s web-head. Tom Holland's Spider-Man has undergone one of the most interesting journeys in the MCU timeline. Introduced as an enthusiastic teenager desperate to prove himself, Peter Parker has gradually become a more experienced, emotionally complex crime fighter. His story has also been closely connected to some of the MCU's biggest events.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, holland's natural charisma, excellent comedic timing, and ability to convey peter's insecurities have made him one of marvel's most consistently entertaining leads. More importantly, the character has finally reached a point where the consequences of his decisions can meaningfully shape his future, rather than simply serving as another stepping stone towards becoming an Avenger.

Berdasarkan laporan, spider-man: brand new day is an exciting new chapter in that development. It is arguably the strongest installment of Holland's Spider-Man series so far. Director Destin Daniel Cretton’s thrilling blockbuster allows Holland plenty of opportunities to explore a different side of Peter Parker, while maintaining the spectacular action and humor audiences expect. However, despite its success, Marvel still needs to explore one particular direction if it wants to get the absolute best out of its web-slinger.

Diungkapkan bahwa one of the defining characteristics of holland's spider-man has been his relationship with the wider mcu. Unlike Tobey Maguire and Andrew Garfield's interpretations, who largely operated independently of other superheroes, Holland's Peter Parker was introduced as part of an already-established superhero community. His first appearance in Captain America: Civil War established his connection to Tony Stark, with the billionaire becoming Peter's mentor throughout Spider-Man: Homecoming and Avengers: Infinity War.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, tony's influence provided an interesting alternative to the traditional uncle ben relationship, allowing marvel to explore peter's desire for approval from somebody he considered a genuine hero. However, it also meant that Peter's introduction to superhero life was heavily dependent on another character.

Berdasarkan laporan, spider-man: far from home brought nick fury into the story, while spider-man: no way home featured doctor strange and a swathe of legacy spider-man characters. It was an enormously entertaining cinematic event, but it also meant that Holland's third solo movie was arguably his least independent adventure.

Berdasarkan laporan, brand new day continues the tradition, albeit with a different assortment of familiar faces. Frank Castle, AKA the Punisher, is an important part of Peter's latest adventure, while Mark Ruffalo returns as Bruce Banner and Florence Pugh appears as Yelena Belova. These characters certainly have defined narrative purposes beyond simply showing up for the sake of recognition.

Berdasarkan laporan, nevertheless, the pattern is difficult to ignore. Across four solo movies, Holland's Spider-Man has shared significant screen time with numerous established characters. While he's garnered might be an impressive collection of guest appearances, it’s hard not to wonder if Spider-Man will ever get a truly solo adventure.

Diungkapkan bahwa importantly, this isn't necessarily a criticism of brand new day. If anything, Destin Daniel Cretton's movie proves that Marvel can incorporate its wider universe without allowing established characters to overwhelm the story. It certainly makes considerably better use of its supporting superheroes than No Way Home, which occasionally struggled to balance its emotional narrative with the excitement of bringing together so many familiar faces.

Diungkapkan bahwa the difference is that brand new day has a much clearer understanding of what peter's story needs. Following the events of No Way Home, everybody has forgotten Peter Parker exists, leaving him without the relationships that previously defined his life. His isolation is central to the narrative, and Holland gets plenty of opportunities to explore the emotional consequences of sacrificing his personal happiness to protect the people he loves.

Berdasarkan laporan, that makes the inclusion of the punisher particularly effective. Rather than introducing Frank Castle simply because audiences recognize Jon Bernthal's character, the narrative establishes an entertaining dynamic between two fundamentally different approaches to superheroism.

Sebagaimana diketahui, bruce banner's inclusion in brand new day is similarly appropriate, with peter experiencing changes to his physiology. Banner's scientific knowledge and personal experience with an uncontrollable alter ego make him a logical person to consult. Yelena's appearance is comparatively brief, but Florence Pugh brings plenty of personality to her scenes without demanding that the movie divert attention towards the wider MCU.

Diungkapkan bahwa the important distinction is that these characters contribute to peter's development rather than simply reminding audiences that they're watching another installment of a larger franchise. Despite its extensive supporting cast, the most compelling material involves Peter, MJ, and Ned.

Berdasarkan laporan, there's no reason marvel needs to abandon crossovers altogether. The interconnected nature of the MCU is one of its greatest strengths, and Spider-Man's comic-book history is filled with memorable team-ups involving other superheroes. Peter Parker has fought alongside the Avengers, teamed up with Daredevil, and developed friendships with characters occupying completely different corners of the Marvel universe.

Berdasarkan laporan, those relationships are worth exploring, but they shouldn't be an obligatory feature of every solo adventure. The ending of No Way Home created an especially interesting opportunity to change direction with Peter is now completely alone, without Tony Stark's technological resources, the Avengers' support network, or even his closest friends knowing who he is.

Sebagaimana diketahui, that opens the door to a more grounded story built around peter, a compelling villain, and the people closest to him. Rather than another world-threatening crisis, Marvel could explore the pressures of balancing superhero responsibilities with Peter's ordinary life, with several quintessential aspects still missing.

Berdasarkan laporan, the daily bugle, j. His relationships with MJ and Ned, meanwhile, offer a particularly rich source of drama following the events of No Way Home. Jonah Jameson, the citizens of Queens, and the neighborhoods Peter regularly protects are all essential parts of Spider-Man's identity. There's plenty to explore without needing to introduce another superhero to explain the stakes.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, brand new day proves that holland can carry a compelling spider-man story while sharing the screen with other mcu characters. His next challenge should be doing so without them. Marvel has spent four movies establishing Spider-Man's place in its interconnected universe; now it should give him the freedom to occupy his own corner of it.

#1012. Garbage Wraps 2026 Tour With Mariachi-Infused Free Show at Mexico City’s Zócalo: 5 Best Moments

Berdasarkan laporan, shirley manson became the first non-hispanic woman to conquer the iconic venue on nov. 14.

Diungkapkan bahwa garbage wrapped up their 2026 tour on saturday (nov. 14) with a free concert at Mexico City’s Zócalo, paying tribute to a country they have visited for three decades with a nod to its culture.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the scottish-american band performed their song “the world is not enough” from the james bond film of the same name with a mariachi arrangement. They also invited Paulina Villarreal, drummer of the Mexican rock band The Warning, to sing their iconic track “I Think I’m Paranoid. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa garbage frontwoman shirley manson, 60, made history by becoming the first non-hispanic woman to headline the zócalo, drawing a crowd of 90,000 people, according to official figures. Before her, superstars Rosalía and Shakira had packed Mexico’s most important public square in 2023 and 2026, respectively.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “it’s one of the biggest honors of our entire career [to play at the zócalo], and the whole band is very excited,” manson told billboard español before taking the stage. “Really, we’re all really emotional, and we’re so proud to be here tonight, and it’s an extraordinary… It’s a culmination of 30 years of coming to Mexico and playing in this amazing city. ”.

The Scottish-born artist noted that her outfit — featuring a white veil, a floral tricolor headdress and braided hair — paid homage to Mexican culture, particularly the legendary Mexican painter Frida Kahlo, whose life and work have inspired her.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, during their performance, the band — also including drummer butch vig, guitarists duke erikson and steve marker, as well as guest bassist nicole fiorentino — surprised fans with their own rendition of the cure’s classic “lovesong. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the setlist kicked off with “no future,” followed by “hold,” “have we met (the void),” “vow,” “the men who rule the world,” “chinese fire horse” and “run baby run. ” The group also performed “The Day That I Met God,” “Control,” “Fix Me Now,” “Special” and “Stupid Girl,” taking fans on a journey through 30 years of their career and eight studio albums, including Garbage (1995), Version 2. 0 (1998), Beautiful Garbage (2001) and Let All That We Imagine Be the Light (2025).

Diungkapkan bahwa garbage joins an exclusive list of acts who have performed at mexico’s zócalo, the second-largest public square in the world after tiananmen square in beijing. This iconic venue has hosted legendary artists and bands, such as Paul McCartney, Roger Waters, Justin Bieber, Manu Chao, Shakira, Rosalía, Café Tacvba and the late icon of Mexican regional music Vicente Fernández. The concert was organized by Mexico City’s government through its local Department of Culture.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the record for attendance at free zócalo concerts is held by colombian superstar shakira, who drew over 400,000 people in march 2026, according to city authorities. She is followed by the Argentine rock band Los Fabulosos Cadillacs, who brought in 300,000 attendees in June 2023, and Grupo Firme, who gathered 280,000 fans in September 2022.

Here are the five standout moments from Garbage’s show at Mexico City’s Zócalo.

Diungkapkan bahwa the traditional mexican shout to express brotherhood also reached manson, who went down into the crowd twice to make the encounter more intimate. With the Mexican flag tied around her neck, the performer sang “Chinese Fire Horse” while greeting and hugging some fans. The chant “¡Shirley, hermana, ya eres mexicana!” (“Shirley, sister, you’re already Mexican!”) echoed through the city’s iconic plaza also known as the First Square, moving her to tears.

Sebagaimana diketahui, one of the most anticipated moments of the night came with the appearance of paulina villarreal, a member of the warning, whom manson had already announced as a guest. The Mexican rocker joined the band during “I Think I’m Paranoid,” a song that has become one of Garbage’s signature tracks. The performance sealed a moment between two female rockers from different generations who have made history.

Diungkapkan bahwa a surprise the group prepared for this special night was a heartfelt rendition of “lovesong” by the iconic british band the cure. The opening chords sparked euphoria among the audience, who joined Manson in singing at the top of their lungs, creating a unique and deeply moving moment.

Manson, who has stood out for her activism in favor of women’s rights and the LGBT community, took a moment during the concert to express her support for Palestine upon noticing some flags waving in the Zócalo square.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “it makes me happy that people are fighting for those who don’t have very much in life and who are in need of protection and who are struggling against a power that is threatening to completely destroy them,” the artist said. Doesn’t matter if you come from f—ing Palestine, whether you come from Mexico City, whether you come from Edinburgh, Scotland, or Madison, Wisconsin, or from Boston, Massachusetts. “The important thing I think to remember is that we’re all absolutely exactly the same. We’re all the f—ing same”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, garbage took the iconic theme song “the world is not enough,” which they originally recorded in 1999 for the james bond film of the same name, to another level by transforming the symphonic orchestra sound into traditional mexican music, accompanied by the mariachi fiesta de méxico. The arrangements for the piece were crafted by sound sculptor Héctor Ruiz, who elevated it to a dramatic and festive level. The performance served as the finale to a concert by a band that helped define the sound of rock in the 1990s.

#1017. Black Clover Won’t Get A Season 3, But Season 2 Might Not Be The End

📅 15 Nov 2026

Black Clover Won’t Get A Season 3, But Season 2 Might Not Be The End

Tanggal: 15 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://screenrant.com/black-clover-season-3-season-2-not-end/

Diungkapkan bahwa black clover is having the time of its life with its long-awaited season 2 comeback. Nine years after its October 2017 debut, and five years after episode #170 went off the air in March 2021, Studio Pierrot’s seasonal overhaul is finally giving Yuki Tabata’s shonen epic the universal acclaim it always deserved.

Berdasarkan laporan, that newfound respect is showing up across every major metric. On top of dominating viewership on Crunchyroll, season 2 also delivered the highest-rated anime episode of 2026 after episode #5, “The Highest vs. the Lowest,” scored a near-perfect 9. Black Clover currently sits at #6 on IMDb’s global Most Popular TV Shows chart, standing completely alone near the top while the next closest anime, Attack on Titan, trails way back at #50. 9/10 on IMDb.

Berdasarkan laporan, however, the anime is burning through the manga so quickly that a traditional season 3 might not make sense. Tabata’s eleven-year manga run officially ended in May 2026 in Jump GIGA with chapter #392, leaving just 122 chapters between the end of season 1 (chapter #270) and the finale.

Berdasarkan laporan, with season 2 reportedly planned for 24 to 26 episodes across two cours, the first cour is already adapting the 61-chapter spade kingdom raid arc. By its end, the anime will be ready to enter the final 61-chapter Ultimate Wizard King saga. Whether Cour 2 covers the Land of the Sun and Judgment Day battles in 2027 or reaches the showdown against its next major threat, Asta's journey may wrap up in a completely different format rather than a traditional season 3.

Diungkapkan bahwa on paper, black clover season 2 adapting four to five manga chapters per episode makes it look like studio pierrot is racing through the remaining story. However, that breakneck pace has more to do with how Yuki Tabata structured the Spade Kingdom Raid arc. Most of those chapters are packed with massive double-page spreads, fast fights, sparse dialogue, and shorter 13-to-15-page counts. Five chapters of nonstop action might sound like a lot, but they don't necessarily translate into five times the usual amount of animation.

Diungkapkan bahwa that should change as the anime moves into the final ultimate wizard king saga, which begins with chapter #332. The story shifts towards heavier lore, character development, and longer conversations, especially during the Land of the Sun training arc with Ryuya Ryudo and the Ryuzen Seven.

Berdasarkan laporan, black clover also moved to jump giga in late 2023, where chapters became longer, often reaching 20 to 25 pages. With all that in mind, the adaptation rate could naturally drop to two or three chapters per episode. If Cour 2 follows that pattern, season 2 could end around the peak of the Judgment Day invasion, leaving the final stretch for a separate finale.

Sebagaimana diketahui, even then, there won't be enough chapters left to fill a traditional 12- or 24-episode season 3. A canon theatrical movie could be one way to finish Asta's story. With Demon Slayer: Infinity Castle, Jujutsu Kaisen 0, and Chainsaw Man – The Movie: Reze Arc showing the box-office potential of anime films, Studio Pierrot has plenty of reason to consider it.

Berdasarkan laporan, the studio also has experience with the format. Its 2023 film, Black Clover: Sword of the Wizard King, was directed by current season 2 director Ayataka Tanemura and became a hit on Netflix. A theatrical finale could give the series the grand send-off its long-awaited return deserves.

Berdasarkan laporan, a theatrical movie isn't the only way studio pierrot could wrap up asta's story. If the studio wants to keep the finale on television, it already has the perfect blueprint in Bleach: Thousand-Year Blood War. Pierrot worked with Tite Kubo to expand the manga's rushed final arc with new fights, extended backstories, and never-before-seen Bankai reveals. Yuki Tabata could take a similar approach with an expanded final cour for Black Clover.

With the manga officially ending, the final war against Lucius has finally revealed the absolute strongest mages.

Sebagaimana diketahui, tabata struggled with health issues towards the end of his weekly shonen jump run and had to condense several side battles during the judgment day war. An anime adaptation could finally give those moments the time they deserve, whether by extending the Magic Knight Captains' fights against upcoming threats or adding more material after chapter #392. So, while Black Clover might not get a traditional season 3, that doesn't mean Asta's story is ending with season 2. Between a theatrical finale and an expanded final television event, the series still has plenty of ways to give its fans the ending they've waited years for.

Asta and Yuno, orphans with a shared dream of becoming the Wizard King, follow distinct paths: Yuno with natural magic abilities, and Asta through determination despite his lack of powers.

Berdasarkan laporan, leitch: being a director is awesome. You get to have all these great artists working for you and you get to take their ideas and curate something great. You have a vision for something, and it's like a bag of marbles that you hold at the beginning of the day, and they just dump them on the table, and then the rest of the day, you're trying to keep all the marbles. It totally is. That's directing really, essentially.

Diungkapkan bahwa kelly, i am a huge weezer fan, and you are producing something called the weezer movie. What the f is The Weezer Movie?.

Berdasarkan laporan, mccormick: i cannot speak about the weezer movie! [laughs] not really. If you know Weezer, you know the movie is going to be very “Weezer-y. ”.

McCORMICK: I hope it's aiming for next year, Steven.

What's been the most difficult sequence of your career, and how close did it come to being like, “we can't do this?”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, leitch: there were a lot of those on the fall guy. We were challenging ourselves to do them for real. We took a lot of time and a lot of prep to get it right. The car jump was scary in the sense that you were making that land on the ground. There were just a lot of practical stunts in that film. We were landing it ramp to ramp, but then when you actually put it up two stories in the air and do the same jump, you're just kind of like, “oh. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa mccormick: they were testing it near where we were shooting. I made them do that survey that they do on the streets all the time. It needed to be exact. It was very programmed exactly how fast he had to go in order to make sure he got to the other side ,and it was wrong, and he was slow, and he felt it, and he punched it, and he got over. Every day, I was like, “Do the survey; just tell me that it's not eroding leading up to it. It tripped up and stopped working while he was taking the ramp. There was this ramp to ramp, and they kept getting the ramps higher and farther apart as they succeeded every day, basically. " The crazy part with that stunt was that it was really the speedometer that ended up being problematic. The set was actually manmade, but it was also filled with dirt and stuff, and I was just really worried that the wind, the rain, or even the sun would be pushing one side or the other differently than we were expecting. In the movie, you can see it.

LEITCH: He clipped the front of it and he hit more of the set than the ramp.

Sebagaimana diketahui, mccormick: you can see the set just flying in the movie. The needs were still really high. That one was really intense. That's him barely making the ramp. If you saw the shot where John is racing and trying to get to Nick, that's like the way that they shot it, made it look like there were tons of people. Honestly, some of How to Rob a Bank was stuff that I was like, “Are we going to be able to get it done?” David puts 800 pounds of genius and a 2 pound bag, like no matter what size he's doing. There were not tons of people! Some of the scariest parts to me is not being able to have the resources. It was all of our guys who worked on, three times, four times the size budget that this was. That one's one where, if it goes sideways, it's not a good thing. The film is shot on 35 millimeter, and then on Prosumer, and at the end, it's on digital. There are only 230 extras, which is for the riot, which is like not a lot considering what we're doing. And in this case, it was a modest budget. They came up with the most genius ways of stacking the extras. Weirdly, that's scarier than a stunt to me.

Sebagaimana diketahui, i actually have a question about that. You mentioned you have a limited amount of extras. With the way technology is now, how much do you think about [not using AI], but using technology like CGI to add more people in or do you want real people?.

McCORMICK: I mean, it depends on the movie, probably.

Berdasarkan laporan, lietch: cgi wouldn't have looked great, you know. The top shot, at the end, where we crane up, it's the drone shot where Nick is laying out on the pavement. I'll be honest, I added a few people in CGI because we had less extras, and so we made it look like there was more of a group, and CGI worked great there.

McCORMICK: By the way, this movie couldn't afford much CGI either.

Diungkapkan bahwa you guys are offered a whole bunch of stuff at this point. What was it about this one that said, “We have to do this”?.

Sebagaimana diketahui, leitch: the script really spoke to us. Could I tell that story and be part of the conversation using sort of the 87 North Engin–the David Leitch engine–of action and comedy, and be a little bit more message forward than I normally am, but also make it an entertaining ride and have people enjoy it, but then at the end of it, feel something and maybe there's a call to action for you in your own life to do something for your neighbor or go out and vote and hold your politicians accountable. This originally was going to come out on Labor Day, and I think Amazon had wished for it to go out on Labor Day, and I think the timing wasn't right for marketing, and we found a great slot at the end of the year or so. Actually, we passed on it, because of the size, and we were going to look and go into some bigger things, and we just couldn't let it go. Every week it gets more timely. It's not like the movie's lost its timeliness. We have this massive disparity of wealth with young and old. What's been going on in the last couple of years and reading this script, it just felt really timely and really relevant. A couple weeks later, we reengaged and said, “you know, we really want to do that. That was the goal with this film. ” Again, I really wanted to just address the elephant in the room. After Tuesday, it’s even more timely. It was to do something provocative and dangerous, but also entertaining.

Berdasarkan laporan, mccormick: it's a subject we're really passionate about, and we wanted to use our platform to join the conversation and to be part of it like a [time] capsule film. Everybody’s watching. They do it for longer than they probably even think, but it's worth it for the message because they're that devoted to what they want people to hear. To try to make change, which was what was cool about it. These creators have such connectivity to their followers. The message is so forward in this movie in the coolest way that’s almost done with this bravado that they're going to get away with it. They're not trying to hide in plain sight. There were two other aspects that were really exciting to us. I think David always bends genres or at least adds to the conversation of the genre, and heist movies aren't like this movie, right? The robbers are hiding. What's the difference? How can you play in both formats? How do they meet? Where do they meet? How do they connect? How do they answer and question each other? We thought that that would be a really fun opportunity for David to play in that space. It's so Gen Z in that way. The second part was to try to find a way to connect with social media and creator storytelling in an authentic way. I haven't really seen a movie that does it in the same way, and I think it's one of the achievements of the film.

Sebagaimana diketahui, i really love the way you did the youtube stuff with nick talking to the camera. Talk a little bit about putting together those YouTube clips, because they're very effective and they're dropping truth bombs on the audience. You’re not lying with these numbers.

Sebagaimana diketahui, leitch: no, not at all. I mean, the things that I watch are really entertaining and they're engaging and they're crazy. Nick is breaking the fourth wall on film, and we're using graphics over film and there's a song playing like you would [hear] if you were watching a YouTube thing, but it's like carrying you through the whole piece. It’s a real motivation to want to rob a bank. I think that was one of the fascinating things about the script initially. The first video was scripted, and there were other videos along the way, but they were really more like The Anarchist Handbook. We created the gang wearing these colorful masks. That was an intentional thing. You read those first numbers. The whole social media thing became its own life in the pre-production process. I started to write those edutainment videos so I could drop them in at different places in the scripts to carry the story forward, but also keep the energy going and, again, combine these two storytelling styles. You see in the middle of the second act when they get caught and there's the interrogation scene, those two styles come together, and that's where life really meets social media. Then you do a little research and you're like, “wow, really?” I think people will be shocked by it. It was very grounded. Social media doesn't feel like that to me. I started to rework those sequences and created the persona of The Wolf that wasn't in the script. How can we, like Kelly said, bring these to make a modern piece about social media and its power? It’s still grounded in these people's real traumas that have led them to wanting to rob banks.

I know you guys made this on a budget, so how the f did you get Radiohead and Billie Eilish? You have some real needle drops in this movie, and they're big songs.

Diungkapkan bahwa leitch: kelly is always good with me at the beginning when there's a budget and we're looking at line items and you look at your spreadsheet. I know for me, as a storyteller, that's an emotional cheat code. It’s shot to the music and we know how we're going to edit it. And then I formulate my shot sequences around that music. That was Lewis Capaldi for the longest time. It used to be “Someone You Loved,” which is also beautiful. At the end of the movie, with the Billie Eilish song, that did change. I go through the script and there are needle drops that come to mind, and 99% of them stick. That sequence in the interrogation scene, I knew we were going to use Lily Allen and we were going to use “Fuck You. It's shameless, but it's premeditated. ” I'm shooting it in that way. You realize, “How much am I going to need for Dave’s musical appetite?” We usually set that aside, and it's like, “Wait, that's two days of shooting?!” But we do it because I know it's going to make the film. We changed it at the last minute, but I still shot that section like a musical piece intentionally.

Sebagaimana diketahui, mccormick: we loved it so much, and then it was exactly what happened with the playability of that song. Young women actually were testing really high in the film, and they would literally write like, “is there any way to change out that Lewis Capaldi [song]?” They're our biggest lovers of the movie. Everybody overplayed it, and so did we. We got to take care of the ladies!.

Diungkapkan bahwa billie eilish works pretty well. Radiohead is pretty selective with what they allow. How tough was it to actually get “Karma Police”?.

Berdasarkan laporan, mccormick: we work with this music supervisor named susan kent, and she's really awesome. I think you wrote something to [Radiohead] as well. David wrote a love letter to Billie Eilish. I just say, “is there any way to get it lower?” And then she says, “yes!” There are times where we write love letters. I don't know how she gets the deals that she gets. We show them clips of the movie sometimes to show them where it's going to play, which works really well for our films because it's usually a pretty good use, and that sometimes brings the budgets down, but it also just gets you the song sometimes, too.

Sebagaimana diketahui, leitch: you know, people believe in it. I think this was a special piece where they knew the material. This movie has a little bit of a message.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, mccormick: the billie eilish [song] i learned is a toxic breakup song. I thought there was something so cool about it in the sense that it's kind of a toxic breakup from the system. We added that component to it, even though it is kind of their love story. At the same time, there's such sorrow to it that I think it kind of works for everything you need to feel.

Berdasarkan laporan, this isn't really a question. I just want to make sure I say out loud that the health insurance industry in America is out to fuck you, and anything that we can do, especially in your movie to get more people talking about this, is very important. It's more like a statement. I give credit to Amazon for being behind it. That's all I got. It's a huge corporation pointing out some of the bullshit.

Sebagaimana diketahui, mccormick: everybody inside of amazon is really passionate about the movie. If you've ever shot with extras, you know that they barely stick around for lunch, let alone stick around for the full day, let alone if you're shooting nights. One of my favorite stories [was] when we were shooting in the streets of Pittsburgh. They were so incredibly supportive. You've seen the work that they're doing on social media, especially. They made their own signs. It was just so cool and it made us feel like this is what we want people to feel coming out of the movie, too. You don't have to riot, per se, or rob a bank, but together you're stronger. They all came to party. It was like a rave. We shot two weeks of nights in downtown Pittsburgh, and every night there were five more people! They came, and then they brought five friends, and we ran out of masks, costumes, and everything, because it just became this movement in Pittsburgh while we were shooting it. They don’t stay all night or come back the next night, forget about that. These trailers are out of this world, and you could just feel that this is hitting us all, even when you're working there too, you know? It’s pretty interesting to see how much everybody who's been a part of it galvanized around it. Find your communities, say your truth, let's make a change.

I need to talk about editing, because you guys know I'm fascinated by editing.

McCORMICK: Elisabet Ronaldsdottir crushed this.

Sebagaimana diketahui, leitch: the icelandic genius. She edited the first John Wick and all of our films. She's amazing.

Berdasarkan laporan, everyone in this audience knows that i love john wick. A lot of people don't remember that it was possibly going straight to DVD or straight to Blu-ray. I could be wrong about this, but then Lionsgate picked it up and then it became a thing.

McCORMICK: It’s more complicated, but we should talk about the editing on How to Rob a Bank.

Sebagaimana diketahui, what is it like when you guys are in the editing room and you're putting together the assembly cut, because you've worked on a number of movies. When you're making your assembly cut, which is where you take all the footage and put it together, have you ever wanted to, like, jump out the window when you have an assembly cut? Or do you always have something?.

Sebagaimana diketahui, leitch: that's a great question, steve. ” If she looks at me like, “we got some stuff to figure out,” and then I’m like, “oh shit, now we really got to go to work. We got to play with those video sequences that were edited in a different house, but then [they were] brought in and we re-edited them. During the first Wick, I didn’t love it. Wow. You got to go out. We were meticulous about the editing in this film. Elisabet has seen a lot of material over the years, and she's really brutally honest, and she pulls no punches. I've become really comfortable with letting things go to make for the greater good. Getting the timing just right, playing with the music, adjusting the sound, having a scene in, having a scene out, watching it again. I didn’t understand that letting go amplifies another scene, and as I’ve grown as a filmmaker, post has become one of my favorite places to play. I love that process. You should do this for a living! Sometimes, you see it, and you're like, “what have I done?” I hide it really well! I do try to walk in with positivity, but there are times where I'm like, “oh, my God!” I trust Elisabet, who's amazing, and I trust Kelly. ” Post[-production] has become a passion for me. I would be bad on an island where you have to pick somebody to go and be like, “it's the greater good. She can look at you and go, “we have a great movie. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, for people that don't realize how, how long does it typically take for you guys to edit a film? i don't think people realize that it’s a battle. You are working long hours for many months to put something together.

Diungkapkan bahwa mccormick: we have a pretty short editing schedule. I think it's 27 or 28 weeks.

Tell the people, is that like a Monday through Friday? Is it 9 to 5?.

Berdasarkan laporan, leitch: yeah. I might be watching a reel doing notes, Elisabet might be working on a second reel. There’s a lot of things going on. It's more like a 9 to 7. You have your editor who's working on scenes you may be watching, you divide the movie into different reels so you can actually digest it in a way so that you're not rewatching everything all the time. We may have an assistant editor looking for sound or a different take.

Diungkapkan bahwa mccormick: you’re working with your composer, you're working with your visual effects team, you're having meetings all the time on iterations of either music or effects. It’s a lot.

Berdasarkan laporan, leitch: it’s kind of endless. There's so much to do that the day just gets consumed.

Sebagaimana diketahui, mccormick: there’s a 10-week period that’s contractual with the dga. I think people really think that that's a ton of time, and then they run out of time. That happens so often that they didn't have the discipline in those ten weeks, and things go off the rails because it feels like you've got all the time in the world, and then you are out of time so fast.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, leitch: what i like to do now is to get my first six weeks. I'm super intense and I try to get to the strongest version of the movie that I'm feeling at the moment. I bring Kelly in for fresh eyes and then it's like dropping a hand grenade on it! “Damn it, it was good for a second!” Then I have another four weeks to take those ideas and shape them. I try to get a really strong assembly cut, reduce it down. The movie ultimately becomes better the more you put it under pressure.

Berdasarkan laporan, mccormick: david's director's cuts are really mature, so it's nice, because then the studio can see what the movie is. It's the slowest process in our high-tech world to have AI taking over our jobs. It takes forever. Then it’s testing it again and really listening to the audience for confusion, for pacing, for jokes, for songs, and then finishing it, which takes forever, too, because it's like three weeks of mixing. It's not like a split where it's like it's his cut versus theirs. He's pretty accepting of notes, if they’re really good, at the director’s cut phase, to do his first preview so that, again, we're making the same movie with the studio. We've never really done that. You're basically testing that cut. They have to mix a reel and then match the reel to the edit, and the conforming. I go, “Isn’t there a way to do this faster?!”.

LEITCH: You're sliding things around frame by frame to get the sound back to where it was when you make an edit.

McCORMICK: It’s like three weeks of that, going back and forth and then listening again and going back and forth, then it's color.

LEITCH: You can see how much Kelly loves post!.

McCORMICK: I actually do! I like it more than production!.

Sebagaimana diketahui, every time i hear from people about what goes on behind the scenes, in terms of making some of these movies, and the bigger the film, the longer it can take and the more meticulous, it's crazy. What was the last thing you cut out before you picture-locked [on How to Rob a Bank]?.

Diungkapkan bahwa leitch: let me say this, because i would be more like the last thing i put in because we were toying with the ending. If you were having the real feels when he's laying on the ground and the camera's moving up, we could have gone to black. That was my first ending of the movie, but I shot all the other endings.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, leitch: it leaves a very, very different feel. I wanted this to be a call to action, and I wanted this to be about hope. At the end of the day, I thought it was better to go with the original ending that we shot. I kept watching the film, and I was really moved by that moment.

How did you decide on how to escape prison? When you do something like that, are you in the back of your mind, like, “well, we might want to continue the story”? Or is it like, “we're just going to have fun with this”?.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, mccormick: it actually stemmed from just wrapping, and the hope. Wrapping up Renzi, it worked so well that you knew that he was still doing stuff and like going to hack his way into some more fun videos, and it wrapped up Anna Sawai’s character so well, and then it gave you hope. It wasn't about a franchise play at all. It was just about hope in this case.

Berdasarkan laporan, leitch: exactly. It was really more of just wrapping up this movie, because I think it was really a one-off about this message.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the best movie title of 2027 is you guys. You own the best title of next year. They made another movie and the title is….

McCORMICK: It’s definitely a palate cleanser from tonight.

Diungkapkan bahwa you've done a lot of second unit [directing]. How much do you lose your mind having a second unit director on your movie? Because I would imagine you want to shoot absolutely everything, or maybe I'm wrong about this.

Diungkapkan bahwa leitch: i don’t have a lot of second units on my set. I don't push a lot off to the second unit. On this film, Greg Rementer directed all the heist stuff, and that was the stunt team dressed as the actors, because we're using masks. When I do, I generally have great people that I trust that have been with me for years. I just let them go wild.

McCORMICK: There were like a thousand cameras on everyone, prosumer cameras, the drones, and he shot them like they were a play.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, leitch: we shot it like it was just real life. You're capturing it like a content creator would, right? There's just cameras everywhere, and you're seeing the cameras. There’s a lot of trust with me and the stunt teams, because we go way back, and I've been in that world for so long.

Diungkapkan bahwa i could ask you guys a million other things, but i'm going to get killed. I've already gone way too far and so on. I'm just going to stop there and say, congrats on the movie.

LEITCH: You’re already going to get killed by the health insurance industry!.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, fuck the health insurance industry! i hate them so much. No one should go bankrupt in America for having to go to the doctors.

A Man Has Just Retired, But the Government Insists He Is Dead. Welcome to ‘When I Existed’! (Exclusive Trailer, Plus Chat With the Directors)

Sebagaimana diketahui, uruguayan writers-directors alejandro damiani and martin avdolov discuss their feature debut, premiering at tallinn, full of black humor. Plus, watch the exclusive trailer. Kafka sends his regards!.

Diungkapkan bahwa silvio bertolini lives in montevideo, uruguay, and has just retired after 40 years of work. His reward? A pregnant daughter in Barcelona, a wife hoping for a family trip, and a government that insists he is – well, there is no way to put it kindly – dead. Sebagaimana diketahui, when i existed (cuando yo existía) is the title of the social satire that is the feature debut by writers-directors alejandro damiani and martin avdolov, a uruguay and spain co-production fueled by black humor – and frustration. Diungkapkan bahwa the cinematographer is manuel branaa, with editing handled by dan avram, martí rocca, damiani and avdolov. The producer of When I Existed is Federico Cetta for El Cielo Cine. The film was made with the support of ACAU, FONA, MVD Filma, MVD Socio, FIC and Ibermedia. Berdasarkan laporan, presenting to the bands generally, and to hook specifically, was trent reznor, who said that in the punk era joy division differed by “level(ing) their gaze at the physical and emotional scars caused by the worst events of the 20th century, reflected in the industrial landscape they called home and posed the question: what chance does love have of surviving in a place like this?” the nine inch nails auteur spoke of curtis as “one of popular music’s all-time great baritone singers. #1028. 7 Pointless Sci-Fi Movie Remakes That Were Worse Than The Original

📅 15 Nov 2026

7 Pointless Sci-Fi Movie Remakes That Were Worse Than The Original

Tanggal: 15 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://screenrant.com/sci-fi-movie-remakes-worse-than-original/

Diungkapkan bahwa the science fiction genre has been particularly afflicted with movie remakes that couldn’t hold a candle to the original. Sci-fi's greatest stories are often remarkably adaptable, with ideas that remain relevant across generations. Sci-fi has always been one of cinema's most imaginative genres, exploring technological breakthroughs, alien civilizations, dystopian futures, and the potential extinction of humanity. Naturally, Hollywood has repeatedly returned to successful science-fiction movies, hoping to introduce familiar stories to new audiences with bigger budgets, modern special effects, and contemporary interpretations.

Diungkapkan bahwa unfortunately, updating a classic doesn't necessarily improve it. Some older science-fiction movies were products of particularly inventive film-making, using practical effects, intelligent writing, and ambitious social commentary to create worlds that audiences hadn't experienced before. Reproducing their basic premises with more sophisticated technology can leave remakes looking considerably less impressive, especially when the original's most interesting ideas are diluted in favor of generic action and spectacle.

Diungkapkan bahwa hollywood has produced plenty of successful sci-fi reimaginings, but there are also several examples that struggle to justify their existence. Whether they misunderstand the original's central themes, replace distinctive characters with forgettable alternatives, or simply fail to capture the same imaginative spirit, these remakes demonstrate that some classics really are better left alone.

Berdasarkan laporan, the day the earth stood still (1951) is one of science fiction's greatest films, using an extraterrestrial visitor's warning to dissect cold war paranoia, nuclear proliferation, and humanity's capacity for self-destruction. Scott Derrickson's 2008 remake, starring Keanu Reeves as the alien Klaatu, attempts to modernize that message by replacing the original's anxieties about nuclear warfare with environmental destruction.

Diungkapkan bahwa unfortunately, the updated version sacrifices much of the intelligence that made its predecessor so effective. The remake certainly has impressive visual effects, particularly when Gort unleashes a swarm of microscopic machines capable of consuming everything in their path.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, however, its environmental message is surprisingly muddled, with the remake struggling to reconcile its ecological concerns with conventional disaster-movie spectacle. The original’s memorable philosophical exchanges and restrained tension are replaced by an overreliance on destruction and spectacle. As a result, it lost all its charm and was left feeling notably hollow.

Sebagaimana diketahui, paul verhoeven's total recall (1990) is gloriously excessive science fiction. It combines Arnold Schwarzenegger's unmistakable action-hero charisma with grotesque practical effects, absurd humour, and an increasingly complicated mystery surrounding Douglas Quaid's identity. Len Wiseman's 2012 Total Recall, starring Colin Farrell, is considerably more interested in looking futuristic than recreating the original's wonderfully strange personality.

Diungkapkan bahwa both films follow an ordinary construction worker who visits rekall, a company promising to implant artificial memories of an exciting adventure. However, the remake abandons Mars entirely, relocating the action to a dystopian Earth divided between the wealthy United Federation of Britain and the impoverished Colony.

Diungkapkan bahwa the production design is undeniably impressive, particularly the enormous futuristic cities and the fall, an underground transportation system connecting the two territories. Unfortunately, Total Recall's visual similarities to Blade Runner are distracting, and its elaborate action sequences lack the personality of Verhoeven's original. There's also no equivalent to Schwarzenegger's outrageous one-liners, the bizarre Martian mutants, or the unforgettable practical effects that made the 1990 film so distinctive.

Berdasarkan laporan, h. G. Wells' The Time Machine has inspired numerous adaptations, but George Pal's 1960 film is particularly memorable for its imaginative depiction of a distant future divided between the peaceful Eloi and the subterranean Morlocks. Simon Wells, the author's great-grandson, directed a new adaptation in 2002, starring Guy Pearce as Alexander Hartdegen.

Sebagaimana diketahui, despite its impressive production design, the remake struggles to recreate the sense of wonder that made its predecessor so effective. After his fiancée Emma (Sienna Guillory) is killed during a robbery, the scientist becomes obsessed with traveling backwards through time to prevent her death. The biggest change is the addition of a romantic motivation for Hartdegen's time-traveling adventures. His repeated failures eventually lead him 800,000 years into the future.

Berdasarkan laporan, the revised motivation makes the story considerably more personal, but it also reduces the intellectual curiosity that drives wells' original novel. Instead of exploring the consequences of humanity's social and evolutionary divisions, The Time Machine resembles a conventional adventure about a man attempting to rescue a romantic interest. Jeremy Irons' sinister Uber-Morlock provides an entertaining antagonist, but the character feels more like a generic blockbuster villain than an interesting development of Wells' ideas. It lost all sense of wonder and replaced it with bland action.

Berdasarkan laporan, frank oz remake of the stepford wives transformed an unsettling satire on technology and social conformity into an underwhelming comedy vehicle. Bryan Forbes' 1975 adaptation of Ira Levin's novel follows Joanna Eberhart (Katharine Ross), a photographer who moves with her family to a seemingly idyllic Connecticut suburb. She gradually discovers that the town's husbands are replacing their wives with obedient robotic duplicates, creating a nightmare vision of patriarchal control.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the 2004 remake, starring nicole kidman and matthew broderick, retains the basic premise but dramatically changes its tone. The light-hearted interpretation certainly features some funny jokes but completely undermines the message of the original. The critique of patriarchal control becomes a star-studded farce – cheapening its central message.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, it feels a lot like the original movie itself has been replaced by a compliant robotic duplicate designed to perpetuate the status quo. The 1975 Stepford Wives presented the idea of men literally engineering their ideal wives as frightening, the modern remake decided it was funny.

Diungkapkan bahwa rollerball (1975) imagined a future in which multinational corporations controlled society and maintained public order through a violent spectator sport. Starring James Caan as Jonathan E, the original used its fictional competition as an allegory for corporate power, consumerism, and the suppression of individual freedom. The 2002 Rollerball remake, starring Chris Klein, largely abandons that political sophistication in favor of chaotic sporting violence.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the new version relocates the action to central asia, where rollerball has become a hugely popular extreme sport. Jonathan and his friend Marcus (LL Cool J) become involved in the competition, only to discover that promoter Alexi Petrovich (Jean Reno) deliberately engineers increasingly dangerous matches to improve television ratings.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, there is certainly potential in updating the original's criticism of corporate entertainment for an era dominated by reality television and sensationalist broadcasting. However, the is much more interested in showing people crashing into one another than examining why audiences enjoy watching them suffer. Furthermore, Rollerball's heavily edited matches are frequently difficult to follow, while Klein lacks the commanding presence Caan brought to the original.

Diungkapkan bahwa paul verhoeven's robocop (1987) is a particularly effective fusion of science-fiction action, political satire, and grotesque violence. Peter Weller plays Alex Murphy, a Detroit police officer murdered by a gang of criminals before being resurrected as a technologically enhanced law-enforcement machine. His gradual rediscovery of his humanity provides the emotional foundation for a film that simultaneously ridicules corporate greed, privatized policing, and sensationalist television.

Sebagaimana diketahui, josé padilha's 2014 remake updates that premise for an era of military drones, surveillance technology, and sophisticated robotics. Consequently, it should have had so much more to play with. Dennett Norton, who becomes uncomfortable with the corporation's manipulation of Murphy's memories and emotions. Indeed, there are interesting ideas here, particularly through Gary Oldman's Dr. However, the remake's more restrained approach to violence removes an essential ingredient of Verhoeven's satire.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the original robocop's exaggerated corporate advertisements, grotesque news broadcasts, and outrageous action sequences made its criticism of 1980s capitalism considerably more effective. Padilha's version is slicker and more technologically sophisticated, but its conventional action-movie structure simply cannot match the original's personality.

Berdasarkan laporan, the original death race, directed by paul bartel and produced by roger corman, starred david carradine as frankenstein, a masked driver competing in a cross-country race where contestants earned points for running down pedestrians. Its deliberately outrageous premise provided the foundation for a gleefully tasteless satire of authoritarian entertainment and America's obsession with violence.

Berdasarkan laporan, paul w. S. Generic muscle man Jason Statham plays Jensen Ames, a former racing driver framed for murder and imprisoned in a privately operated facility run by the calculating Warden Hennessey (Joan Allen). Anderson's version replaces the original's bizarre road-racing competition with a prison-based televised spectacle. She offers him a chance to regain his freedom by taking the place of the masked racer Frankenstein, competing in heavily armed vehicles against other prisoners.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the remake delivers plenty of entertaining automotive carnage, with its armored cars, mounted machine guns, and elaborate stunt driving providing some impressive action. However, Death Race loses much of the original's darkly comic premise. The 1975 film's scoring system, which rewarded drivers for killing pedestrians, was an absurd extension of its dystopian satire; Anderson instead turns the concept into a fairly conventional prison-break adventure. It’s not a remake in the conventional sense, but a reimagining based on the least important parts of the iconic sci-fi original.

#1036. 8 Hard Sci-Fi Shows Even Better Than The Expanse

📅 15 Nov 2026

8 Hard Sci-Fi Shows Even Better Than The Expanse

Tanggal: 15 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://screenrant.com/hard-sci-fi-shows-better-than-the-expanse/

Berdasarkan laporan, when it comes to hard sci-fi shows for the true genre aficionado, the expanse is hard to beat. Its attention to scientific principles like gravity, acceleration, and the practical difficulties of interstellar society gives its futuristic setting a remarkably grounded foundation. However, while it’s difficult to argue against The Expanse being the definitive modern space opera series, its position as TV’s best hard sci-fi show isn’t so clear-cut.

Berdasarkan laporan, several hard sci-fi tv shows bring their fiction with just as much science, if not more, than the expanse. True, they don’t all focus on life among the stars or deliver storytelling as consistently compelling as the Rocinante crew’s saga, but they definitely match and even beat Prime Video’s series when it comes to their sci-fi being cerebral, complex, and rooted in real scientific principals.

Berdasarkan laporan, the expanse makes space travel much more interesting because it remembers that the challenges of traversing the void last long after liftoff. The show focuses on an international crew on an extended expedition through the solar system, with the central drama and tension all stemming from the day-to-day difficulties of simply continuing the mission. The short-lived 2009 hard sci-fi series Defying Gravity leads into this even harder, making the daily struggles of its eight astronauts the central attraction. Their spacecraft, the Antares, feels genuinely claustrophobic and fraught with danger even when things are going smoothly.

Sebagaimana diketahui, for viewers who appreciated when the expanse focused on the rocinante as a home and shared workplace and the interpersonal difficulties this caused, defying gravity is ideal. As far as hard sci-fi goes, it does a fantastic job at bringing to light the practical problems of making a spacecraft habitable. That approach makes real-life engineering dramatically meaningful, because keeping people alive requires several things to keep working simultaneously. Power, temperature regulation, and the crew’s ability to function belong to the same fragile system. It’s a much more intimate account of life aboard a spacecraft than The Expanse usually has room for, accurately portraying interplanetary travel as difficult, exhausting daily work.

Sebagaimana diketahui, dangers to humanity after first contact is the focus of many great action-heavy sci-fi tv shows, but in both the expanse and another life it creates problems that firepower can’t solve. In the two-season Netflix show, Niko Breckinridge (Katee Sackhoff) commands the Salvare on a mission to investigate a civilization responsible for an alien artifact discovered on Earth. That premise already gives both series a connected scientific challenge: reaching an unknown intelligence and understanding what humanity has encountered. Just like in The Expanse, exploration in Another Life is an exercise in interpreting incomplete evidence while keeping the expedition alive.

Sebagaimana diketahui, where another life beats the expanse is that it explores concepts like extraterrestrial biology and technology with much more depth. Where The Expanse left its protomolecule and Ring Gates a mystery, Another Life explores the science behind understanding unfamiliar organisms in great detail. It takes The Expanse’s alien intrigue and turns it into a central drip-feed of discoveries that undermine the Salvare crew and the audience's existing assumptions. As a bonus, the Netflix show also handles existential questions around AI incredibly well through the ship’s on-board intelligence, William (Samuel Anderson), and his emergent emotional capabilities.

Sebagaimana diketahui, orphan black doesn’t look to space for its hard sci-fi, but to human cloning and the age-old debate around how much genetics and circumstances shape who we are. The mystery begins when Sarah Manning discovers another woman who looks exactly like her. Thanks to Tatiana Maslany’s incredible performance as over a dozen different clones, the relationship between inherited biology and lived experience become apparent long before the show dives into scenes that discuss it in a laboratory. From there, the series turns cutting-edge genetic science into something personal, raising fascinating debates around scientific ownership when “experiments” have been in the real world long enough to start families, have ambitions, and, most importantly, forge their own identities.

Berdasarkan laporan, the hard sci-fi dive into biology in orphan black explores contemporary concerns around genetic manipulation and the ethics of the institutions controlling these areas of research. Fans of The Expanse who are drawn to the exploitation surrounding protomolecule research specifically will find similar material in Orphan Black. It’s this foundation that gives the central conspiracy significant weight and makes it feel much more grounded than many other TV shows and movies about cloning. However, this show focuses much more on the human consequences of biotechnological research than The Expanse ever did, especially when it comes to treating people as experiments.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, a continued presence after death is something the expanse explores through the protomolecule reconstruction of miller (thomas jane), but in netflix’s hard sci-fi cyberpunk series altered carbon it’s treated as a society-wide economic issue. Former soldier Takeshi Kovacs (Joel Kinnaman, Anthony Mackie, and Will Yun Lee) enters this world’s privileged superhumanly-long-lived circles through a murder investigation. Human consciousness can be stored in devices called cortical stacks and transferred into replacement bodies, creating a civilization where wealth can literally buy immortality. The detective story is incredibly gripping, but it’s the worldbuilding surrounding it that makes Altered Carbon so great when it comes to hard sci-fi specifically.

Sebagaimana diketahui, altered carbon explores the natural ramifications of technologies that allow new bodies to be purchased, identities to outlast their original appearance, and the wealthy being able to protect themselves against consequences that remain permanent for everyone else. Backups introduce gaps between a person’s remembered experience and what happened to their body, while replacement bodies complicate intimacy, punishment, and recognition. This becomes especially harrowing and fascinating when it comes to the implications of the human mind as transferable information. These consequences create an authentic-feeling picture of everyday life where the show’s speculative neuroscience technology is real.

Sebagaimana diketahui, artificial intelligence exists in the world of the expanse, but it’s not a central focus. Another hard sci-fi show also focuses on this specific idea only with man-made AI instead of alien-created space portals. The implications of civilization-changing technologies, however, is. That show is Person of Interest, which starts as a straightforward crime procedural but ends over a struggle to reclaim humankind control of its own destiny from the grasp of unplanned rapid technological progress.

Diungkapkan bahwa in the show, scientist harold finch (michael emerson) builds a system capable of identifying potential violence through surveillance data, then recruits john reese (jim caviezel) to investigate the people it flags. Of course, over time this system becomes so advanced that it’s dangerous, especially when rival equally powerful artificial intelligences begin to emerge. For The Expanse fans, Person of Interest’s escalating struggle over a technology powerful enough to reorder society is incredibly satisfying, despite the specifics of both plots being worlds apart.

Berdasarkan laporan, a huge part of the hard sci-fi appeal of the expanse is its grounded depiction of the space technologies of the future and the political frictions facing a humanity spread out across multiple planets. Any fans who want a story that focuses more on this than it does on mysteries like the ring gates and protomolecule will find Apple TV’s For All Mankind much more satisfying. The show begins with the USSR beating NASA to the Moon Landing, then explores how this impacts technological and social progress. It especially focuses on space travel, which takes a drastically different turn. The result resembles a history that could conceivably lead to the 24th century solar system of The Expanse.

Sebagaimana diketahui, for all mankind’s attention to spacecraft operations and the demands of maintaining distant settlements gives its ideas an intellectual weight that makes it one of the 21st century’s best hard sci-fi shows. As the series reaches humanity's attempts to colonize Mars, it moves from practical concerns to societal disputes over political authority. This should feel instantly familiar to fans of The Expanse, and it’s hard to recommend a show that feels like a better companion piece.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, interplanetary politics are complicated and detailed enough in the expanse, but apple tv’s foundation expands that challenge across an entire galaxy to make it the core of one of television’s most ambitious space operas. Mathematician Hari Seldon (Jared Harris) approaches this society through psychohistory, a predictive science combining mathematics with the statistical behavior of vast populations. Its hard sci-fi focuses on how a civilization spread across hundreds of stars would function, particularly when its worlds all have different priorities and relationships with the central authority of humanity’s galactic empire. His forecast of total societal collapse across the galaxy forms the center of a narrative exploring what the forces that shape civilizations truly are, and whether humankind really will ever have control over them.

Berdasarkan laporan, essentially, foundation is a much more focused dive into one of the most satisfying themes of the expanse. Foundation also stretches this exploration problems across generations too, examining how knowledge survives, political power fades, and long-term plans are never immune to chaos. Both shows understand that humanity’s expansion into space creates political problems that a unified central government alone can’t seem to solve. Its scale makes the difficulties of governing an interplanetary society in The Expanse feel like the earliest stage of a much greater challenge.

Berdasarkan laporan, keeping thousands of people alive in space requires more than winning the next battle, which battlestar galactica understands with brutal clarity. The Expanse understands this too, but it’s Battlestar’s commitment to making problems like exhaustion, water, food, and fuel central to its survival story make it much more satisfying in this arena. After the Cylons devastate human civilization, a surviving fleet must keep moving while preserving the systems that sustain its remaining population. This fascination with realism even extends into the fleet’s technology. Computer networks create vulnerabilities and maintenance becomes harder as equipment deteriorates.

Diungkapkan bahwa at the same time, battlestar galactica also focuses on its wilder elements through an incredibly hard sci-fi perspective. Not only that, but it also manages to have an incredibly plausible depiction of the complex political intricacies of a humanity spread out across multiple starships too. Through the Cylons, the series rigorously examines ideas like artificial consciousness and the relationship between memory and identity. While both shows are brilliant, Battlestar Galactica feels like it surpasses many of the hard sci-fi strengths of The Expanse, even when it veers into more fantastical or conceptual territory like Cylon prophecies or cyclical time loops.

#1043. Pitch Perfect: The 20 Best Music Schools in the World

📅 15 Nov 2026

Pitch Perfect: The 20 Best Music Schools in the World

Tanggal: 15 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/music/music-features/best-music-schools-world-1236752338/

From Juilliard and USC to Berklee and Eastman, these are the programs and conservatories training the next generation of Hollywood composers.

Diungkapkan bahwa conservatories, typically built around intensive studio training in performance and composition rather than the broad general education requirements of a traditional college, made a strong showing in thr‘s annual look at the world’s best music schools. But schools with well-regarded media scoring programs, which teach composing for film, TV, video and gaming — USC Thornton, Eastman, Berklee and Columbia Chicago — retain their influence in Hollywood and beyond.

Sebagaimana diketahui, david serkin ludwig, dean and director of the music division at juilliard, which continues to expand its opportunities for media scoring, says that the grounding conservatories give their students is important in a world where ai is encroaching even on creative disciplines like music. “So I’m happy with the direction we’re going, and we just have to keep staying current. “A great hedge against the replacement aspect of AI is having a very deep and thorough training, because you want depth of knowledge and experience for people using the tools,” he says. ” Related Stories Music Richard Sterban, Oak Ridge Boys' Bass Singer, Dies at 83 Music Meet Plave, the Very Real Virtual K-pop Boy Group.

Berdasarkan laporan, to see where that type of training is happening, we turned to the people working in the field. Contributing to this year’s ranked list via survey: the Society of Composers and Lyricists, the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences’ music branch, the Alliance for Women Film Composers and the Composers Diversity Collective. Thanks go to Ray Costa and Costa Communications for their help in distributing THR‘s survey.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, long a holdout on media scoring instruction, juilliard now offers several courses, including composing for visual media, which gives students the fundamental skills they need to compose for film and tv, as well as commercials and video games, with focuses on both traditional and more diverse contemporary approaches. Scoring to Picture is a two-credit course offered through the school’s extension division that covers spotting, or placement of music and sound in a project, scoring brief media excerpts and enhancing drama in film with music.

Berdasarkan laporan, the school also has renovated and upgraded its film scoring labs and classrooms. “So looking into motion sensors, other kinds of digital response tools but also just the software itself, and making platforms available for our students: laptops, cameras, all the devices and tools they need to create their own media. “We’re aspiring to stay on the cutting edge of available technologies for them, so we’re doing a lot in interactive music technology as well,” says Serkin Ludwig, the dean and director of the music division. ”.

NOTABLE ALUMNI John Williams (Star Wars); Philip Glass (The Hours).

Berdasarkan laporan, usc thornton continues to thrive at the center of the hollywood music community and offers a two-semester master’s degree program in screen scoring that recruits about 20 students a year for a deep dive into composition, orchestration, programming, conducting, producing and editing music for screen-based media. The program has been chaired by Jeanine Cowen since 2022. The filmmakers are amazed because most of them have no idea what a live ensemble can do for their picture. “In September, we did a massive mock scoring session with 25 Thornton musicians and our composers, and we were just doing it so everybody could get a sense of what a scoring session is. “We’re really trying to take advantage of our relationship with the cinema school,” Cowen says. So we’ll probably keep doing that because it was such a huge success. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, while los angeles has faced challenges in employment and keeping jobs in town, cowen says hollywood’s creative culture is still vital: “every session we’ve had so far, the pro studio players are all busy, so we’re not able to get our first call all the time, and it’s because there’s a lot going on in town that’s keeping musicians busy. ”.

NOTABLE ALUMNI Bear McCreary (The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power); James Newton Howard (The Hunger Games: The Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes).

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, university of rochester’s eastman school of music continues to offer students both intensive conservatory training in performance and composition, as well as a renowned program for film and media scoring with funding and participation from prolific composer jeff beal (house of cards, monk) for the school’s beal institute for film music and contemporary media. With this program, we invite technologically curious musicians to explore new ways of creating and experiencing music, keeping Eastman’s world-class curriculum at the forefront of musical innovation. Next year will see the school broaden the institute’s approach, as associate professor of music and technology Dennis DeSantis explains: “In an ever-evolving technological world, Eastman’s Beal Institute for Film Music and Contemporary Media is excited to reach beyond the traditional methods of composition by launching a new major in music creation and technology in fall 2027. ”.

NOTABLE ALUMNI Maria Schneider (Grammy-winning composer); Lew Soloff (jazz trumpeter).

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, sean mcmahon continues in his role as chair of screen scoring at berklee, which includes two programs, film and media scoring and game and interactive media scoring, both of which are four-year bachelor of music degrees. The school’s Next Gen Composer Lab is an immersive, five-day collaboration among Berklee Screen Scoring, the Boston Conservatory and the Vienna Symphonic Library. “Nine composers each get to conduct and record their original music with the 84-piece Vienna Synchron Orchestra, while two elite conservatory instrumentalists sit inside the orchestra itself, recording shoulder to shoulder with Europe’s finest session players,” McMahon says.

Berklee now also offers a Master of Arts in music supervision, the first of its kind in the world: a one-year, fully online graduate program covering the art of selecting, licensing and integrating music into TV, games and advertising and taught by music supervisor pros like Julia Michels (The Devil Wears Prada).

NOTABLE ALUMNI Alex Lacamoire (Tony winner for Hamilton); Howard Shore (The Lord of the Rings).

Berdasarkan laporan, the herb alpert school offers media scoring training through its composition and theory program, in which student composers receive instruction in studio recording, counterpoint, global musicianship and orchestration. Students are encouraged to take advantage of interdisciplinary crossovers to collaborate with live performers, student film and media directors, and cross-cultural ensembles inspired by ethnomusicology and world jazz styles. New students must complete a music theory assessment examination to achieve placement in global musicianship and formal music theory classes.

NOTABLE ALUMNI Joseph Trapanese (The Greatest Showman); Quincy Jones (Thriller).

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, if you’re extremely talented, looking for premier conservatory training in the los angeles area and hard up for cash, colburn offers elite undergraduate, graduate and postgraduate programs that concentrate on classical performance and repertoire — and a generous price break. All students receive a full-tuition scholarship and grants that cover room and board. It’s essentially courses in theory, performance and ear training without the humanities requirements. The Performance Diploma is a four-year nondegree program for students with ambitions of professional performance but who do not yet have a bachelor’s degree. Undergraduate programs include a four-year bachelor of music degree that offers studio performance training and courses on musical theory, music history, ear training and the humanities, with students completing both junior and senior solo recitals. Colburn also offers graduate programs including a two-year master of music with a focus on high-level instrumental mastery and advanced seminars in music history, theory and composition.

NOTABLE ALUMNI Kris Bowers (Bridgerton); Elias Peter Brown (conductor).

Sebagaimana diketahui, royal college of music offers a master’s degree in composition with a specialism in composition for screen — an advanced program that trains composers for professional careers through workshops, master classes, performance projects and collaborations with professional artists. The program is tailored to individual student needs and ambitions, with instruction from world-class professors and visiting artists. Electives include classes in orchestration, experimental music, conducting, music education, analysis and practical skills to keep students up to speed with constantly evolving digital technology and global perspectives. The school’s exchange program allows students to audition for the chance to study abroad during the fall term of their second year at the school.

Each year, the school hosts a Composition for Screen Showcase featuring a live ensemble performing music written by students accompanying films projected on the big screen; it’s attended by the public and industry professionals.

NOTABLE ALUMNI Andrew Lloyd Webber (The Phantom of the Opera); James Horner (Titanic).

Diungkapkan bahwa in addition to its venerable ivy league name, yale boasts proximity to new york, boston and the town of new haven, giving students a rich cultural and artistic environment in which to take advantage of the school’s prestigious conservatory training. While the school does not offer degree programs in media scoring, Yale’s Center for Collaborative Arts and Media helps students combine music with film, video, computer science and the visual arts. Yale offers a master of music, master of musical arts, doctor of musical arts and artist diploma in composition, with courses taught by concert hall composers including Katherine Balch, Martin Bresnick and Aaron Jay Kernis.
