Time to start sharpening your bloodaxe.

Time to start sharpening your bloodaxe.

Diungkapkan bahwa a weak king rules over a cobbled-together kingdom that's already coming apart at the seams. Various heroes and villains compete and scheme to claim the throne. A new challenger rises up from across the sea, full of vengeance and bloodlust. If that sounds like the premise of Game of Thrones, well, that's because it is, but it's also the set-up for Prime Video's thrilling new action drama from one of the 21st-century's most successful (and underappreciated) showrunners.

Berdasarkan laporan, back in october, during new york comic con 2026, i attended an early screening of bloodaxe, a new series from vikings creator michael hirst and his son horatio. 20, 2027 on Prime Video, the streamer might just have a new Game of Thrones-level hit on its hands. Based on the show's first episode, which premieres Jan. Or at the very least, an entertaining show for VIkings fans.

Diungkapkan bahwa bloodaxe tells the real-life story of eric haraldsson (aka eric bloodaxe), who lived during the 10th century. When we first meet Eric (Xavier Molyneux), he's already a powerful warrior and a popular figure in Viking society. His father, King Harald (Jesper Christensen), is beginning to lose his grip on the Norwegian kingdom he spent his life uniting. Eric expects to be named successor, but then Harald reveals that his younger son Haakon (Levi Miller), who spent his childhood in England learning the art of diplomacy, will be king instead. Meanwhile, Eric's statuesque wife Gunnhild (Bridgerton's Jessica Madsen) has her own schemes in mind to elevate her husband to the throne, while her exiled brother Egil (Kārlis Arnolds Avots) plots his own ascension to power from nearby Iceland.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, that might sound like a lot of plot to pack into one hour of television, and… it is. Like Game of Thrones, Bloodaxe pulls out all the stops in its opening act to win over its audience. But Michael and Horatio Hirst deftly plunge us into this world headfirst like a Viking warrior sprinting into the frigid Norwegian Sea. That means plenty of political intrigue, shocking deaths, stunning scenery, meticulous production design, beautiful actors, and gratuitous sex scenes.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the landscapes are particularly stunning. Life-sized boats and massive sprawling sets complete the experience. The cast ain't bad to look at either. Molyneux resembles a lost Hemsworth brother (his breakout role was as a contestant on Australian Big Brother), while Miller bears a striking resemblance to Kit Harington's Jon Snow. While much of what's meant to be Norway was filmed in Ireland, with rugged Scandinavian mountains added in digitally, Egil's scenes were shot on location in Iceland — you just can't fake those scorchingly beautiful geothermal pools and glaciers. It all makes Bloodaxe very easy on the eyes.

Sebagaimana diketahui, that helps when the plot quickly gets down into the muck. (An interesting wrinkle: Of the two, the Vikings were arguably more progressive for their time, with an egalitarian society that treated men and women equally. There's even a few prophecies and witchy rituals thrown in for good measure, all playing out against the backdrop of a larger theological battle between Viking paganism with its pantheon of Norse gods and the rising tide of Catholic monotheism. While Bloodaxe technically hinges on palace intrigue, this is a gritty and grimy world with its own morals and ethics that feel alien by 21st-century standards. The core story of multiple factions vying for power and bracing for all-out civil war also feels particularly Game of Thrones-esque. ).

Berdasarkan laporan, perhaps most interesting of all, bloodaxe is based on a true story. The writers are pulling directly from history (as recorded by Icelandic clerics and scholars several hundred years later). This also means that, like with Game of Thrones, if you're curious about what ultimately happens to Eric and the rest of the gang, you can always read ahead and find out. But why ruin the fun?.

Berdasarkan laporan, all eight episodes of bloodaxe will make landfall on jan. 20, 2027, with season 2 already in production. So while you could head to Wikipedia right now to find out whether Eric Bloodaxe becomes king or not, you may have a lot more fun watching his journey play out onscreen.

Berdasarkan laporan, and assuming the showrunners get to tell a complete story, bloodaxe has one big advantage over game of thrones. This story has been set in stone for over one thousand years, which means it will be very hard for Michael and Horatio Hirst to bungle the ending.

Diungkapkan bahwa bloodaxe premieres jan. 20, 2027 on Prime Video.

#1054. 8 Most Universally Loved Cult Classic Movies Of All Time

📅 15 Nov 2026

8 Most Universally Loved Cult Classic Movies Of All Time

Tanggal: 15 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://screenrant.com/most-universally-loved-cult-movies-all-time/

There are plenty of movies that have gained cult classic reputation as a result of the nature of their reception, their long-term appeal, and their fandoms - and plenty of the most universally loved cult movies are still common talking points today, despite having often released many years ago.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, a contrast of sorts to the likes of big blockbusters or movies mainly focused on for their major box office results, cult movies have a more comparatively low-key reputation. They tend to fall under the radar upon their initial release in one way or another, and then are either rediscovered years later, or experience a progressively more positive or popular response from viewers in the time after their debut. This process happens more often than not because some core aspects of these films go against mainstream cinema conventions in one way or another, making them underdogs in this regard.

Diungkapkan bahwa the most universally loved cult movies generally have a lasting impact on pop culture to this day due to the long-term significance of their story and what it means to people, even if said impact also is often subtler overall due to this status. While the landscape of the movie world may ebb and flow with the years, these films have maintained ardent fanbases throughout their time, which makes them each notable in their own right and way.

Donnie Darko goes from strength to strength with its casting, its story, and its overall ambience, which has a striking gothic kind of surrealism that has played a major role in it being a lasting cult classic with a wide range of audiences.

The story of the titular Donnie narrowly escaping death only to be told by a mysterious rabbit-costumed figure that the world will end in 28 days is one that's hard to not be invested in from the first moment onward.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, donnie darko has all the big set pieces and memorable moments you could possibly want in a film - with said terrifying rabbit costume being a prime example. Despite this, its narrative is inherently focused on its protagonist and the personal challenges Donnie faces, rather than the grander sci-fi-leaning nature of the predicament he finds himself in, giving it a more universal sense of appeal as you fear for and root for the unfortunate troubled teen.

The famous Spinal Tap quote "these go up to eleven" is a perfect example of why the 1984 mockumentary has lived on as a beloved cult hit for decades after its release, thanks to the film's ability to playfully mock the world of rock bands and the documentaries that oftentimes attempt to idealize their legacies.

The scene wherein fictional band Spinal Tap reveal they have amps that go up to eleven despite the maximum for amps generally being ten - with guitarist Nigel reacting in confusion when asked why they didn't simply make the ten setting be louder instead - plays with the idea of rock bands often being over the top, and also satirizes the idea of the musical prodigy, as it's clear that in Nigel's mind, bigger always means better, no matter what the reality is.

Diungkapkan bahwa this is spinal tap's affectionate approach to being a satire means it's loved by many die-hard music fans and music documentary fans, and is often equally appreciated by those who have less glowing perspectives on such matters at the same time. Perhaps more importantly, the lasting impact of This Is Spinal Tap influenced the real-life world of music considerably, as many famous artists enjoyed the film, and sought out amps that go up to eleven as a playful nod to the movie and the influence it had on the music sphere.

A classic cult action thriller movie, The Warriors saw notably negative reviews upon its initial release, which later gave way to a far more positive reception as more and more people found it, and welcomed its over-the-top nature.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the warriors is not a particularly subtle story, and this arguably works to its benefit. Indeed, the plot of a gang trying to escape home to Coney Island after being framed for the death of the most powerful gang leader in New York at a gang meeting arguably needs to lean into the larger-than-life premise of its story, which forgoes realism in order to provide as grand a plot as it wants to deliver.

This decision has proved worth its weight in gold for the film over the course of time, as the style and sensibilities of The Warriors has lastingly engaged viewers, with its visuals still remaining striking even as they've naturally aged.

Sebagaimana diketahui, one of the most beloved movie cases of mistaken identity in history is that of the big lebowski, which focuses around two very different characters who both happen to be named jeffrey lebowski. This classic comedy premise is played off into a neo-noir crime movie setting, with Jeffrey "The Dude" Lebowski finding himself involved in a complex world of crime, ransoms, and kidnappings, which deliver increasingly surreal scenarios.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the legacy of the big lebowski makes a lot of sense given the exaggerated characters that comprise the film's entire cast, and ensures the movie feels almost like a live-action cartoon for portions of its run. This is further supported by the dialogue, which ricochets from being about potentially life-threatening matters to being banter about bowling or the Eagles instead, with plenty of lines that are still being quoted to this day.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, adapting one of the most cult classic musical plays of all time was a move that carried with it plenty of risk alongside plenty of potential reward. A huge part of what makes the theater show such a hit with fans is that it's a very interactive one, with the audience often being encouraged to speak up at certain points in the performance to do things like sing along. Without this, then, the movie rendition had the potential to fall flat, unless it was able to replicate the lively experience in some other way.

Diungkapkan bahwa as it stands, a mixture of the rocky horror picture show's cast and the way in which the movie is able to set up a full on-screen world with expansive sets makes the film a version of the story that audiences find just as fun in its own right. Add Tim Curry playing central character Dr. Frank-N-Furter with visible glee, and the surreal yet engrossing appeal of the film is evident on several levels.

The Thing is a sci-fi horror movie like no other, even though many other films have also followed the storyline of a bloodthirsty entity able to replicate the appearances of others.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the desolate setting of the antarctic tundra with only a team of researchers in it makes things feel far more stressful than many of the things' peers from the outset, however. Similarly, the compelling ways in which the protagonists try to deal with their increasingly dire circumstances leave you rooting for them all the more ardent the more bleak things become, as they're believable, lived-in-feeling characters, who avoid falling into the stereotype of horror victims who only suffer because of their own mistakes.

Berdasarkan laporan, the thing's ending remains one of the most lastingly fascinating and unforgettable in moviedom even with the luxury of decades of time having passed since then. In the same vein, its monster also has a distinctive setup and skillset that's made it one that audiences love to fear still in an age where many other 80s horror figures are regarded as distinctly more cheesy than scary, too.

The Breakfast Club combines every coming-of-age high school movie archetype into one film, and then dissects each of them, showing how everyone has deeper layers, and that understanding others is the only way to grow true bonds with those around you.

Sebagaimana diketahui, because of its emotionally resonant character work and straightforward premise of a range of very different students finding themselves in the same detention - where they are then tasked with making an essay about who they are - the breakfast club is easily a film that can become a comfort watch of sorts. It's also commonly recommended en masse as a feel-good film that encourages people to try and understand themselves and others, which has no doubt helped its longevity as a cult classic.

Diungkapkan bahwa the immensely quotable nature of the princess bride means that it's still pretty common to hear another show, movie, or real-life person recite lines like "my name is inigo montoya. You killed my father - prepare to die. " or "You keep using that word. I do not think it means what you think it means. " almost 40 years after the movie's release.

Sebagaimana diketahui, this is a testament to the strength of the princess bride's script. Almost every line within the movie is a witticism or character-defining moment, which are all carefully balanced to ensure the film seems like a cohesive and engaging movie that isn't simply written for the sake of delivering a slew of one-liners, which is impressive in its own right.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the fantastical, evolved fairy tale narrative of westley attempting to save princess buttercup - which is justified via being delivered through a book a grandfather is reading to his grandchild - gives much of the story a timeless kind of nature and appeal. This is strengthened further by the endearing roster of unforgettable characters The Princess Bride fleshes out along the course of its runtime, resulting in its beloved cult classic reputation, and ensuring that viewers find themselves as entertained as the grandchild the story is being told to by its end.

Diungkapkan bahwa we want to hear from you. Share your perspective in the comments below, and please keep the conversation respectful.

#1056. Robert Christgau and Carola Dibbell Talk New Documentary ‘The Last Critic’ and Staying Crazy in Love

Robert Christgau and Carola Dibbell Talk New Documentary ‘The Last Critic’ and Staying Crazy in Love

Tanggal: 15 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.rollingstone.com/music/music-features/robert-christgau-carola-dibbell-interview-last-critic-1235657436/

Berdasarkan laporan, the last critic is one of the year’s most fascinating rock documentaries — even though it’s not about a musician. ” He was one of the pioneers who invented pop-music criticism in the Sixties — but six decades later, at 83, he’s still at the top of the game. He began his Consumer Guide column in the Village Voice in 1969, and has kept cranking it out ever since, now on Substack. It’s a portrait of the legendary writer Robert Christgau, the self-proclaimed “Dean of American Rock Critics. For generations of music fanatics, Christgau’s voice hits like Bob Dylan or Neil Young — two artists his age who are still doing it with the same fiercely independent spirit he brings to his writing.

Berdasarkan laporan, the debut feature from director matty wishnow, the last critic won the jury prize at the south by southwest and oak cliff film festivals, as well as the 2026 screen dallas grand prize. Christgau and his wife, novelist Carola Dibbell, have been together more than 50 years. The film, which is co-produced by longtime Rolling Stone contributor and editor Joe Levy, goes beyond music, because it’s also the portrait of a marriage. It gets its New York premiere tomorrow. Over the decades, they’ve shared an intellectual life, raised their daughter, collected way too much vinyl, and — the weirdest part — remained crazy in love.

Sebagaimana diketahui, christgau has a fearsome rep for never pulling his punches, with his own savage wit. Lou Reed spent a chunk of his live album Take No Prisoners complaining about getting a B+ grade for Street Hassle; when U2 won the Grammy Award for Album of the Year in 1988 for The Joshua Tree, Bono jokily groused in his speech about his band’s reviews in the Village Voice. Christgau’s inspired more songs attacking him than any other journalist, from Sonic Youth (“Kill Yr Idols”) to Public Enemy (“Bring the Noise”).

Sebagaimana diketahui, but there’s something obsessive about his lifelong quest to chronicle the music, still going strong after 60 years — he’s heard more albums than anyone on the planet. When he reviewed Prince’s Dirty Mind in 1980, he dropped one of the most-quoted one-liners in critical history: “Mick Jagger can fold up his penis and go home. ” Editor’s picks The 250 Greatest Albums of the 21st Century So Far The 100 Best TV Episodes of All Time The 500 Greatest Albums of All Time 100 Best Movies of the 21st Century.

Berdasarkan laporan, the last critic features artists christgau has reviewed, as well as writers he’s inspired, from sonic youth’s thurston moore to pulitzer-winning novelist colson whitehead. ) There’s a touching interlude with his lifelong friend Greil Marcus, the only other OG rock critic who’s kept doing it this long (or this well). In one of the most surprising moments, the legendary songwriter Randy Newman recalls their friendship, and admits he wrote a song about Christgau and Dibbell, “Lost Without You,” inspired by the closeness of their marriage. (I make an appearance as well. It’s the kind of movie where you come for the rock, stay for the romance.

Sebagaimana diketahui, rolling stone met up with the couple at the same east village pad they’ve called home for 50 years. The place is packed with albums, books, art — the first thing that greets you at the door is a painting of the Shirelles. They talked about the doc, seeing their marriage up on the big screen, the art of arguing, playing hoops with Randy Newman, and the strange college semester when Christgau was Gene Simmons’ professor.

Diungkapkan bahwa congratulations on the movie. When [director] Matty [Wishlow] called me up and asked if I would do it, the first thing I said was, “Yes, if you include my marriage,” which at the time I think took him aback. Robert Christgau: It came out really well. However, he came to feel that it was the marriage that made the movie, which is what I believe.

Berdasarkan laporan, it is the marriage that makes the movie. I’m a co-star. Charm’.

Berdasarkan laporan, when i first saw it, i told the director, “this is a love story. The relationship really has a kind of vitality to it that you can see. A very strange love story. And it’s really nice that it actually comes through in the imagery of the film. I think that’s the best thing about the movie. ”Christgau: Well, I agree. And that’s exactly how I feel about Carola, and that’s the most important thing in my life. I think that’s the reason people like the movie, too.

Berdasarkan laporan, when did you two get together?dibbell: the summer of 1972. I knew that he was a rock critic, but I really was not like a groupie. He was my friend Dominique’s boyfriend. I met him in the summer of 1970 — we were all having breakfast at Ratner’s Deli. Bob and I had known each other. Bob had had his eye on me all this time, but I was just so delighted to have him as a friend. But I then got into an argument with you about Godard.

Christgau: She knew more about film than I did.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, dibbell: bob and i had a big argument about it, but then we became friends anyway, and then he began to date dominique, and so we just knew each other. But eventually, everything changed for me.

Diungkapkan bahwa christgau: i’m so glad it did, carola. She was an incredibly cute woman with a Radcliffe degree.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, dibbell: the thing is we were both english majors. One night we were playing a party game called “Celebrity,” and we needed to come up with a celebrity whose initials were an M and a C. And we both came up with Martin Chuzzlewit [the title character in an 1844 Dickens novel].

Berdasarkan laporan, now that’s two people destined to be together. I think that’s why people respond seeing such an unusual couple onscreen. Christgau: What makes it so unusual?.

Berdasarkan laporan, two people, very extreme personalities, who stay madly in love for 50 years of marriage, but remain individuals in a totally unfiltered way. Christgau: I don’t know how extreme I think we are, but—.

Dibbell: Really? I really don’t know that, but I believe you.

Sebagaimana diketahui, you both make a strong impression. People were asking, “Oh, is it OK to be a feminist and get married?” Bob was a feminist too, and he always liked smart women. Dibbell: Well, at the time that we got together, it was … I’m not going to say “turning point,” but it was sort of a point where one chapter in the counterculture and the movement was easing into another. Let me put it that way. And so we both were trying to figure out, how do you do this? A marriage of equals?.

Diungkapkan bahwa something i love about the documentary is how it captures your enthusiasm for the art of a good argument. Dibbell: I used to say that if I told him “I agree with you,” he’d say, “That’s where you’re wrong. ” He just couldn’t stop arguing.

Berdasarkan laporan, dibbell: yeah, you. Who do you think we’re talking about? But it just comes very easily to both of us.

Would it be fair to say that you both have argumentative personalities?Christgau: I don’t think Carola has an argumentative personality.

Dibbell: There’s where I disagree with you.

Diungkapkan bahwa i guess i mean a “debate” more than an “argument. ”Dibbell: I think I argue more than I debate, actually. But it definitely improves our thought to be arguing together.

Diungkapkan bahwa christgau: i got carola to start writing rock criticism, not because she was my wife and i wanted to give her the work — although, obviously, that was part of it. But because A, I knew she could really write, and B, she had knowledge of the subject.

Berdasarkan laporan, dibbell: i found rock criticism so interesting as a form, being a writer, and i was very interested in the unreliable narrator and all that kind of thing. Then when I read Lester Bangs, I said, “Oh, yeah! Why not be literally ambitious while writing about this declassé music stuff?”.

Christgau: He could also write a paragraph in about a minute and a half.

Diungkapkan bahwa when you began writing in the sixties, there wasn’t a lot of serious attention paid to pop music. Rolling Stone was a crucial part of why all of that happened. Christgau: But Rolling Stone was doing that a lot. Jann Wenner had a head for finding the most interesting writers, many from the Boston college scene, and that was a really important factor in why I got to do what I did. No question about it.

Berdasarkan laporan, and also the fact that i was already friends with greil marcus. He was at Rolling Stone, and frankly, I think he had Jann Wenner around his little finger. That was a crucial part of it as well. Because Jann was smart enough to know that this guy was really something else.

Diungkapkan bahwa early on, you wrote that your biggest influences were thelonius monk and alan freed. I still play a lot of Thelonious Monk. Christgau: Let me tell you, Monk has lasted. Carola gets a little tired of it.

Dibbell: I finally say, “Can we listen to The Clash?”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, but you always had an appreciation for am radio. You were open to tawdry pop trash. Christgau: It wasn’t “tawdry. ” Come on.

Diungkapkan bahwa you were writing in the seventies about how great kc and the sunshine band were. That proves my point. Christgau: It’s all well-made, that’s the thing. Extremely well-made. In the Village Voice. Dibbell: It proves your point.

Sebagaimana diketahui, determined as you are to undermine the entire premise of my point, i’m going to make it anyway. When I first read your Consumer Guide as a kid in the Eighties, I couldn’t believe there was an adult writing about Funkadelic and the Go-Go’s and Donna Summer and A Flock of Seagulls and taking it seriously, as art.

Diungkapkan bahwa christgau: four hours a day listening to am radio had something to do with that. But I wanted to write about pop art as an important phenomenon.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, there’s a great story in your memoir about when you were teaching the rock criticism class at cuny on staten island in 1970, and one of your students was a kid named gene klein. Christgau: Who later became Gene Simmons.

I always wonder what the dragon from Kiss learned from you about music critics.

Christgau: He just sat in the back and kept his mouth shut.

Sebagaimana diketahui, something the last critic documents is your insanely obsessive online following, around the world. Christgau: One thing that happens with this movie is people in Sweden and Norway coming up with their dog-eared copies of my books.

Dibbell: It was so funny hearing about Europeans with tattered versions of the first Consumer Guide book.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, christgau: so i had this fanbase all over the world, and i had no idea it was there, really. But when that ended, I kept writing. I was writing for the Village Voice, and they paid me decently, and I had a lot of autonomy, and I really valued it. I managed to have a whole life as a critic, and it’s not like I’m working for Variety or the Times. I feel not just fortunate, I feel like I built something.

Diungkapkan bahwa dibbell: but there was a point when you were having conversations about whether you should stick with the consumer guide or whether you should write more essays. Also, I remember I had to argue Bob into writing the memoir, Going Into the City. You felt, “Why would anybody want to read my story?”.

Christgau: Which came out pretty well, I think.

Diungkapkan bahwa dibbell: yeah, it did. But you resisted that. And I also understood that you had a fanbase based on that. Editors thought you should write more essays, but I felt that the Consumer Guide was such a great form that you shouldn’t stop doing it. I wasn’t even thinking so you can make a living — but just with me, my constant struggle to get a book published, I just felt this is a great thing, that fanbase. Sebagaimana diketahui, how did you become friends with randy newman? he plays such a surprising role in the movie. Dibbell: He was lovely.

Sebagaimana diketahui, randy newman talks about writing a beautiful love song about you two, “lost without you. ”Christgau: I will say I was very proud. I was early on it. This was a long time ago — I don’t play basketball anymore. And then we went out to the ballpark and played basketball. Berdasarkan laporan, it started with basketball, but how did that turn into a long-running friendship?dibbell: he wrote you a fan letter in the nineties, saying that he admired your perseverance, the way you kept up with new music, that it was something he did not actually understand, your enthusiasm for it. Christgau: I’ve always had a high opinion of him.

Sebagaimana diketahui, dibbell: we had lunch with him — this was in the old days when we had an answering machine. Berdasarkan laporan, christgau: we went to lunch. Then he came back to our place, even though he could hardly walk.

Sebagaimana diketahui, dibbell: he had some bad knee problem, but you wanted to play him some new music. He climbed the stairs. Then he looked around our apartment, and he said, “If you wanted to fix this place up, I could loan you some money. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa he’s so sincere in this movie — we’ve never seen this side of him before. It’s probably the only Randy Newman song anyone would want to be about them. Christgau: Yeah, it’s a great compliment. I liked that song before I knew it was about us.

Diungkapkan bahwa were you surprised by the last critic, when you finally saw it?christgau: i think a better way of putting it is that i was more pleased by it than i anticipated being. Matty hadn’t made a movie before. And I was especially happy about how important a role Carola played in it. This was not his area of expertise. But he ended up making a really good movie.

It just seemed like, “OK, you want to do this? What do you see in a documentary about a critic?”.

Diungkapkan bahwa but it goes beyond that. If it had been about [the legendary New Yorker and Village Voice journalist] Ellen Willis [his Sixties ex] and me, it wouldn’t have been this good. It’s the love story, in a collaborative life of the mind. Ellen’s as smart as anybody I’ve ever met. Obviously, I’m very happy who it was a love story with. But Ellen didn’t like music as much as Carola ended up doing. Christgau: That is the thing that I like best about it, and I’m proud of it. [Dibbell comes in from the next room. ] I was just saying you were a better rock critic than Ellen Willis.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, dibbell: i respect her tremendously. Her work was foundational.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, you were on the scene for so many pivotal rock moments, like the monterey pop festival and woodstock. A fan on your Substack recently found a photo of you in the crowd at Monterey. Nobody at that time understood how important Monterey was going to turn out to be historically, as this event that really just pretended something was happening — but then it really happened. Christgau: About the third row, yeah. Woodstock itself was a strange and interesting experience, which involved a lot of lying around the grass, among other things.

Berdasarkan laporan, the way you wrote about women musicians in the 1970s was very ahead of the curve culturally. It was really important to me to be a feminist critic. Christgau: Let it be said that Ellen Willis was not without her presence in that fact, because Ellen Willis really made me a much more fervent and conscience-driven and militant feminist. I’ve been writing about women making rock & roll since the beginning. There’s a really moving moment in the doc when the writer Jessica Hopper discusses reading your words on Joni Mitchell. You were engaging with feminist ideas at a time when it was rare in music journalism. I mean, I had those impulses anyway, but Willis obviously solidified them, without any question. Joy of Cooking and Fanny are bands that 90 percent of people have never heard of.

Berdasarkan laporan, you were taking dolly parton seriously as a writer in the 1970s, when most of the media treated her as a joke. Christgau: But Patti Smith was out there covering “Jolene,” right? Glad she’s still around. How old is Patti?.

Diungkapkan bahwa dibbell: she’s a little younger than us, but not that much younger than us. So, what, she’s in her seventies?.

Sebagaimana diketahui, she turns 80 in december. Dibbell: And Debbie Harry? I think she’s older than me.

Diungkapkan bahwa you had a great line about a billy joel album in the eighties: “sexual-politics rads like me were fretting about a decade ago come home to haunt guys who thought they were a crock. ”Christgau: I said that? That’s pretty good. But as far as my marriage with Carola is concerned, one thing that’s really significant about how it happened is that I went out with one of her best friends, for close to a year before. And so Carola was someone I really knew fairly well, but it wasn’t like we were dating.

#1068. 17 Years Ago, the Longest Running Sci-Fi Show Flipped Its Core Concept On Its Head

📅 15 Nov 2026

17 Years Ago, the Longest Running Sci-Fi Show Flipped Its Core Concept On Its Head

Tanggal: 15 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.polygon.com/doctor-who-the-waters-of-mars-17th-anniversary-retrospective/

Berdasarkan laporan, david tennant has long been recognized as one of the greatest actors alive. He’s played scoundrels, cops, serial killers, and even a demon — an actual one, not a member of the Conservative Party, though he’s played one of those too.

Sebagaimana diketahui, if there’s one thing you can’t say about tennant, it’s that he lacks range. He can play a lover, a fighter, or the scummiest person you know. But his most iconic role as the time-traveling alien known as the Doctor in the sci-fi family show Doctor Who brings all three together.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, that might be a shocking statement to process. One of the Doctor’s core moral philosophies, articulated as early as Classic Who in 1963, is that the Time Lord is ultimately a peaceful person. During the Twelfth Doctor’s (Peter Capaldi) regeneration in 2017, one of his very last statements was that the future Doctor should “never be cruel, never be cowardly, and never ever eat pears! Remember, hate is always foolish, but love is always wise. Always try to be nice, but never fail to be kind. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa and yet, tennant’s tenth doctor was the opposite of all those things during the 2009 autumnal doctor who special, "the waters of mars. ".

There have always been moments when the Doctor has shown that, for every person he has saved over the centuries, there have been just as many whom he has condemned.

Berdasarkan laporan, however, the most memorable episode in which whovians see the doctor at his lowest point morally comes when the time lord lands on mars in 2059 and encounters humanity’s first colony there: bowie base one. Unfortunately, once the Doctor realizes who they are, another realization follows: it’s a fixed point in history in which everyone on Bowie Base One will die in an unknown cataclysm. Led by Captain Adelaide Brooke (Lindsay Duncan), the colonists seem to be doing quite well for themselves, and there is hope that more of humanity will be able to join them in the future. Worse, it’s set to happen on the day the Doctor arrives.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the reason is revealed with the arrival of the flood — an incredibly intelligent, waterborne alien virus. A single drop of the virus infects humans, turning them into zombie-like creatures with one sole aim: to keep spreading. One by one, the personnel of Bowie Base One perish, though one member cleverly destroys all the ships so the Flood cannot spread to Earth.

Diungkapkan bahwa throughout it all, the doctor is racked with indecision. Messing with fixed points in history is usually seen as a big no-no, but he had done so before with his previous companion Donna Noble (Catherine Tate) when they saved a single family during “The Fires of Pompeii. ” However, if he saves Adelaide, her granddaughter Susie won’t be inspired to become the first human captain to pilot a lightspeed ship to Proxima Centauri, a major historical event.

Sebagaimana diketahui, it’s a conundrum that arises while the doctor is traveling alone, still reeling from the loss of his companion, donna. In several previous episodes, the alien race known as the Ood has also warned him that his time is running out — regeneration is on the way.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, this knowledge leaves the doctor furious. No matter how many he saves, it seems all he does lately is lose. Now that he’s on his own, the fact that time and circumstance take so much away has driven him to the brink. He’s tired of losing; he wants to win.

After revealing to Adelaide her impending doom and her granddaughter’s achievement, the Doctor, in a moment of profound, unbridled hubris, delivers a speech that must be read in full to appreciate just how villainous it sounds:.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “there are laws of time. They all died. Once upon a time there were people in charge of those laws, but they died. Do you know who that leaves? Me! It's taken me all these years to realize that the laws of time are mine and they will obey me!”.

Berdasarkan laporan, it’s a quote that feels exactly like it would come from the doctor’s worst enemy, fellow time lord, the master. Unlike the Doctor, the Master has always wanted to dominate others, making the Doctor’s subsequent rescue of Adelaide in the TARDIS feel even worse.

Diungkapkan bahwa unfortunately for the doctor, his victory in giving time itself a big ‘f u’ is short-lived. Back on Earth, Adelaide is shaken by the Doctor’s self-perception as a god over time and berates the Time Lord for thinking he gets to live and choose who lives and who dies. She walks away and kills herself, righting history once more.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the doctor's overwhelming pride has always been part of him. As much as he loves exploring the universe and often falls in love with humanity, he undoubtedly thinks himself better than most. There have been too many episodes to count in which a character has called the Doctor out for thinking others are stupid.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the time lord’s arrogance often leaves it to his companions to reel him back from the brink of destruction by reminding him of his humanity. In “The Waters of Mars,” it is easy to see why: If they don’t, the Doctor can easily become the very monster he so often fights.

#1070. 'Indiana Jones Meets Agatha Christie' Series With 39 Episodes Beats Spielberg At His Own Game

'Indiana Jones Meets Agatha Christie' Series With 39 Episodes Beats Spielberg At His Own Game

Tanggal: 15 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://screenrant.com/adventures-of-tintin-animated-series-better-than-movie/

Berdasarkan laporan, steven spielberg brought hergé’s beloved tintin character to the attention of a much wider, younger audience when he directed a dazzling blockbuster movie adaptation in 2011. Jamie Bell starred as Tintin, Andy Serkis provided strong support as his grizzled sidekick Captain Haddock, and a crack filmmaking team brought Hergé’s cartoons to life in a gorgeous, lived-in 3D animated world. But Tintin was an icon in Europe long before Spielberg introduced him to American audiences.

Berdasarkan laporan, decades before spielberg would bring tintin to the big screen in an animated movie, he appeared in live-action movies, stop-motion movies, and a couple of animated tv shows. The first TV adaptation ran in the ‘60s, but its four-minute episodes barely had room to tell a story. In the early ‘90s, during HBO’s brief push into original animated programming, a French studio and a Canadian studio co-produced three seasons of The Adventures of Tintin, comprised of half-hour episodes with plenty of room to breathe.

Berdasarkan laporan, spielberg’s movie is great; it’s a dazzling visual feast, a rollicking buddy comedy, and it came a lot closer to recapturing the pulpy magic of the original indiana jones trilogy than spielberg’s own kingdom of the crystal skull or james mangold’s dial of destiny. But the source material gave him a leg up — Hergé’s comics combine the globetrotting action of an Indiana Jones movie with the twisty intrigue of an Agatha Christie mystery — and the animated show from the ‘90s is even better.

Diungkapkan bahwa spielberg’s tintin movie made hergé’s characters and storylines accessible to a wider audience through the explosive spectacle and white-knuckle pacing of an action blockbuster, but the animated series was a much closer adaptation. The titular Tintin is a boy detective, chasing criminals with his trusty canine sidekick. The heart and soul of the Tintin stories is the characters. He has a handful of trusted associates, like Captain Haddock (the Victor Sullivan to Tintin’s Nathan Drake) and the hilarious double act of Thomson and Thompson, and he encounters a delightfully eccentric villain in each story.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the movie certainly has that heart — spielberg takes every opportunity to slow down for a little character moment — but the tv show had a lot more opportunities. I love the Spielberg movie, but the source material was better-suited to episodic television. The charm of Hergé’s comics is getting to see Tintin’s day-to-day life, as he and Snowy search for clues, ruffle feathers with the locals, and hang out with their fellow crimefighters, and the animated series could spend half of every episode indulging in those quieter “hangout” moments.

Berdasarkan laporan, 15 years after the adventures of tintin arrived in theaters, the sequel is finally moving forward. In mid-2026, he confirmed it would be his next project. Last month, he confirmed that the script was finished. We’ve been hearing talk of a second movie since the first one came out, but it seems to finally be happening. In early 2026, Peter Jackson said he was developing a Tintin sequel script with Fran Walsh for himself to direct. Tintin 2 is closer to happening than ever before.

Diungkapkan bahwa we’ve been burned in the past, so don’t get your hopes up. But even if Jackson does make an Adventures of Tintin sequel as his next movie, it’ll still be at least a couple of years before we see it. The good news is that the technology used to make the Tintin films will allow Bell and Serkis to pick up where they left off, no matter how much older than their characters they get, so this is one of the few sequels that can handle a decade-and-a-half’s worth of delays. In the meantime, check out the old animated series.

Berdasarkan laporan, "[i]t had cost me eighteen months work, my peace of mind, and almost all of my remaining hair. Nevertheless, when I saw the 'rough cut' of the picture, it seems to have been worth it. ".

Berdasarkan laporan, heinlein wrote his masterpiece, "stranger in a strange land," several years after his experiences working on "moonbase" and "moon," so hollywood started looking at him again. A producer named Howie Horowitz called Heinlein about making a TV pilot, and the result was a script called "XXII Century" (also called "Century XXII" various places online). Diungkapkan bahwa the basics behind the pilot of "xxii century" can be found on the libertarian futurist society website. "XXII Century" was to take place in the year 2163, and followed the plight of a secret society of powerful superhumans who had the ability to think rationally at all times, even if it pained them. Heinlein's 1949 novella "Gulf. " In the pilot episode, called "The Man Who Wasn't There," it was explained that the United States, Russia, and China engaged in a devastating war in the year 1984. Thereafter, the former two affected authoritarian governments founded moon colonies, and eventually began sending criminals and undesirables there. #1079. 10 Books With Talking Animal Companions Almost as Charming as Princess Donut

10 Books With Talking Animal Companions Almost as Charming as Princess Donut

Tanggal: 15 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://screenrant.com/best-books-talking-animal-companions-similar-princess-donut/

Diungkapkan bahwa obviously, there's no talking animal more charming than princess donut, and it would be an outrage to suggest otherwise. But while Dungeon Crawler Carl's ​​​​​​reigning princess might have claim to Best in Show, there are other lovable animal companions out there.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, for many readers, princess donut is the best thing about dungeon crawler carl. No doubt she'll deliver more unforgettable moments in the next installment, but in the meantime, what's a reader to do? There's always another DCC reread to fill the Princess Donut-shaped hole in your heart while we wait for a Book 9 release date. But you could also spend some time in the pages of another story with a charming animal companion character for a change of pace.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, whether you're after a talking dog, cat, or something a little less conventional like, say, a rat, bat, or animated plant, chatty animal sidekicks abound in books. They're often adorable and frequently charming, and some of them are even almost as delightful as Princess Donut. Almost.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, naturally, there can only be one princess donut the queen anne chonk. But when it comes to books featuring down-on-their-luck men with a cat sidekick that's almost definitely smarter than them? Well, as it turns out, there are at least two books like that. And oh, the conversations Donut and Hera would have if they ever met.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, starter villain follows charlie, a divorced substitute teacher who suddenly inherits his uncle's supervillain business. Thankfully, hyper-intelligent spy cat Hera has been keeping an eye on Charlie for a while, and she's ready to help him learn the ropes. She takes her job as his protector quite seriously, even if she also thinks he's a bit of an idiot.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, it's hard to beat a talking dog, but have you considered a talking corgi that also happens to be an all-powerful magical being? because that's precisely what readers get in the blue moon cafe & 24-hour occult emporium. And it is, frankly, delightful.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, when talula's mother steps away on urgent magical business, she recruits a powerful magical being to take over magic lessons. For starters, he's a corgi. Though he starts out a bit overly self-assured and aloof, Simon is an absolute delight who truly cares for Talula. He will win you over not only with cuteness, but with his willingness to grow and learn. But Simon is far from what Talula expected. And his true identity is a fun little surprise, too.

You can purchase The Blue Moon Cafe & 24-Hour Occult Emporium here.

Berdasarkan laporan, druids and talking to animals often go hand-in-hand, especially in games like dungeons & dragons. So it's not too surprising that a series called The Iron Druid Chronicles features at least one prominent talking animal companion. Loyal Irish wolfhound Oberon may not be able to talk out loud, but his telepathic connection with Atticus lets him voice his opinion plenty well, thank you very much.

Berdasarkan laporan, this 10-book urban fantasy series starts with hounded. Like you might expect from a dog, Oberon really loves food, especially bacon, and really hates squirrels. It follows Atticus, the last of the druids, who has been on the run along with his dog Oberon for two thousand years. No word on how he feels about cocker spaniels, but we won't hold that against this otherwise charming and hilarious talking animal companion.

You can purchase book 1 in The Iron Druid Chronicles here.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, okay, yes, caz is technically a spider plant, not an animal. Though the spell that created him was a crime, Caz was allowed to remain at the Great Library where he was born. But he is sentient, talkative, and charming, which earns him a place among some of the best chatty companions fantasy books can offer. But when political upheaval forces librarian Kiela to flee the city, Caz goes with her.

Diungkapkan bahwa kiela and caz wind up living on the island she once called home. But soon, they find themselves running an illicit spell shop and experimenting with magic. Their goal? Stay out of trouble and avoid attention until they and their quite-possibly-illegal hoard of books can return to the city. Despite his anxious tendencies, Caz is often the voice of reason in Kiela's plans, making him both charming and relatable. Their friendship is absolutely heartwarming, and it's easily one of the best things about this cozy fantasy.

Berdasarkan laporan, the farseer trilogy is a prime example of the chosen one trope done well. But this series doesn't just deliver the start of an unforgettable epic fantasy with a dubious chosen one. The second book, Royal Assassin, also introduces readers to Nighteyes, the wolf companion who accompanies Fitz.

Berdasarkan laporan, like many animal companions in fantasy, nighteyes doesn't talk out loud. Nighteyes is fiercely loyal, but also very much a wolf who isn't afraid to point out the all-too-human worries that plague Fitz throughout the series. But thanks to the Wit, the wolf can communicate telepathically with his human friend and companion. And much like in DCC, the bond between human and animal companion has plenty of time to grow and develop over the course of several books, giving readers plenty of time to fall in love with Nighteyes.

Sebagaimana diketahui, cats, dogs, and wolves are pretty common animal companions in fantasy novels. And Rachel Gillig delivers a new charming bat-like companion in the form of Bartholomew. Technically, he's a stone grotesque, aka a gargoyle, in the shape of a giant bat. But bats? That's a good bit less common, but as Anastasia proved, it works. And he's so popular that you can buy a talking mini of him for your desk.

Berdasarkan laporan, bartholomew quickly became the most beloved character in gillig's duology thanks to his role as sybil's helpful companion and one of the main sources of comic relief. Like Princess Donut, his quippy nature has earned Bartholomew entire Reddit threads devoted to his best quotes. But his tragic backstory also lends him a serious, emotionally resonant role in the story that makes us all love him even more.

Berdasarkan laporan, yes, we have another animal-like sentient plant in the mix. And brandishing said knives at people, especially ones who threaten to hurt Violet or her friends.

Diungkapkan bahwa the song of the lioness quartet is an iconic ya fantasy series for so many reasons. Introduced early in In the Hand of the Goddess, the mysterious black cat with purple eyes quickly becomes a steadfast companion of Alanna's.

Much like Donut and her Magic Missiles, The Cat is more than just a cat and has the magical abilities to prove it.

You can purchase In the Hand of the Goddess here.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, assistant to the villain kicked off a beloved cozy fantasy series when it released in 2023. The premise of a young woman working for a surprisingly charming villain is, obviously, a huge part of the appeal. But so is the talking frog, Kingsley. He captivated readers so much that readers left book 1 desperate for more of his backstory, which gets slowly revealed as the series progresses.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, to this day, "god loves, man kills" is one of the few books in marvel's library that reaches true literary prestige, and which can compare to the great works of their rival publisher dc, like frank miller's "the dark knight returns" or alan moore and dave gibbons' "watchmen. " It runs over 60 pages, three times as long as a typical "X-Men" issue. Reverend Stryker would fit right in with the Moral Majority. (It's worth noting that one of the evangelical movement's casus belli in those days was opposition to school desegregation. ) While "God Loves, Man Kills" remains a clear product of the 1980s, its themes are timeless; you would only have to change the allegory's specifics to set it today. Diungkapkan bahwa chris claremont more elegantly tied mutants' oppression to reality a year earlier in 1981 when, in "x-men" #150, he revealed magneto as a holocaust survivor. If You Liked Colleen Hoover's Verity, Watch Dakota Johnson's Acclaimed 2025 Movie Next

Berdasarkan laporan, if you liked seeing dakota johnson starring in a twisted psychosexual drama like "verity," which is based on the novel by colleen hoover, you might want to check out the more adult romantic drama "materialists," celine song's acidic essay on modern dating from 2025. /Film's Bill Bria said in his review of "Materialists" that it was structured like a typical rom-com, but more heartfelt, full of yearning and depth.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, more than anything, though, "materialists" deals with a deeply cynical approach to romance, just as the title would lead you to believe. The movie itself seems to wince whenever one of Lucy's clients says they desire a woman who is "fit"; those characters might as well be yelling "no fat chicks. It's about how modern matchmaking has become a painfully specialized industry because modern adults have become all too fixated on the superficial qualities — and the earning power — of their potential mates. Johnson plays a cold-hearted matchmaker-for-the-rich named Lucy who has trouble weaning her male clients off of the idea of dating younger women exclusively. ".

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, over the course of the film, lucy finds herself torn between two potential boyfriends who have both appeared — or reappeared — in her life. On the one hand, she can pursue Harry (Pedro Pascal), an unbearably handsome, unfathomably rich, and suitably tall man who ticks all the boxes on the average dating profile requirement list. On the other hand, she has reconnected with her ex-boyfriend John (Chris Evans), a struggling actor who was always disorganized and never wealthy, but who loved her deeply. Does Lucy choose a life of poverty undergirded by true love, or does she follow her more cutthroat, materialistic instincts, and pursue the wealthy man who can give her a life of luxury?.

Diungkapkan bahwa for long portions of "materialists," lucy's choice seems obvious. Harry may not have the same kind of passion as John, but he is definitely interested in Lucy, and he is happy to share his wealth. She also becomes startled when she learns a secret about Harry that we won't spoil here. There is a coldness, however, to his well-moneyed lifestyle, and something vaguely transactional about his love affair. She begins to question if her attraction to him is genuine, or if it just checks the right boxes on a typical dating profile.

Diungkapkan bahwa as "materialists" unspools, however, it begins to skew away from the acidic nature of its opening act and begins strolling toward a drama about romantic truthfulness. Lucy is also thrown for a loop when she unwittingly matches one of her long-single clients Sophie (Zoë Winters) with a man who sexually assaults Sophie. Lucy subsequently doubts her every romantic instinct, and a portion of "Materialists" becomes about Lucy trying to reach out to Sophie to make amends. Perhaps she can mitigate her bad romantic instincts by being a genuine friend to this woman.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the ultimate answer is perhaps a little treacly, but lucy finds herself drawn back to john. The pair had previously broken up over his incapacity for amassing wealth and her frustrations with the boring everyday financial struggles they went through. Now, however, she is beginning to appreciate the nature of human connection, and John looks more and more romantically alluring.

Diungkapkan bahwa of course, one could argue that dakota johnson, in being torn between chris evans and pedro pascal, is hardly in an unenviable place. We should all be so lucky to have two devastatingly handsome movie stars equally eager to court us.

Sebagaimana diketahui, "materialists" was a pretty big hit, making almost $108 million worldwide on a relatively small budget of only $20 million. The film isn't terribly deep in its commentary on the foibles of modern romance and the shallowness therein, but it's at least about something, and it features multiple beautiful people alternately romancing one another. When the movie hit streaming, "Materialists" became a hit for HBO Max. It also, according to our exclusive interview with writer/director Celine Song, was modeled on a film noir, giving the film an alluring, mysterious quality. All those elements put together seemingly were what drew people out in such numbers.

Sebagaimana diketahui, critics largely liked "materialists," as evidenced by its 77% approval rating on rotten tomatoes, based on 307 reviews. Angelica Jade Bastién, writing for Vulture, felt that the movie didn't delve deeply enough into its own thesis that modern romance is directly tied to capitalism. Indeed, she wrote that, in its last act, the film "pivots to a more conventional romantic narrative of the kind it had promised to upend, if not outright critique. ".

Berdasarkan laporan, stephanie zacharek, writing for time magazine, was more generous, writing that celine song is speaking very much to the moment, analyzing what romance means in an ego-driven and money-driven world of instagram and an easily reduced sense of personal value. "That's the world 'Materialists' takes place in," Zacharek writes, "and Song sees what's funny and what's terrible about it at once—even as she acknowledges that it's human to yearn for beautiful things, and for comfort. She's chosen the perfect actors for this enterprise. ".

Sebagaimana diketahui, if you want a romance that mixes acid with some thoughtfulness, check out "materialists. ".

#1087. Stephen King Named This Alfred Hitchcock Thriller As One Of His Favorite Scary Movies

📅 15 Nov 2026

Stephen King Named This Alfred Hitchcock Thriller As One Of His Favorite Scary Movies

Tanggal: 15 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.slashfilm.com/2311493/stephen-king-alfred-hitchcock-thriller-favorite-scary-movies-frenzy/

Berdasarkan laporan, back in 2017, indiewire amassed a list of stephen king's favorite scary movies based on the titles he had either previously recommended on social media or written about in his 1981 non-fiction book "danse macabre. " Among the many, many films included were Ridley Scott's "Alien," Mario Bava's "Black Sunday," Brian De Palma's "Carrie" (itself based on King's own litany of feminine rage), and George A. Romero's "Dawn of the Dead. ".

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, somewhat surprisingly, alfred hitchcock's 1972 serial killer "frenzy" made the cut as well. "Frenzy" was Hitchcock's penultimate film and is famously the only one of Hitchcock's movies to receive an R rating in the United States. Indeed, one might be startled to see actual on-screen nudity in a film from The Master of Suspense. The murders in "Frenzy" are notably brutal, too, and the movie, quite shockingly, contains scenes of sexual assault. This was clearly an attempt by Hitchcock to push the envelope, and one can only speculate if he was drawn to the film's twisted serial killer mentality, the sweatiness of the overall picture, or its sheer amount of on-screen violence.

Sebagaimana diketahui, "frenzy" tells the story of richard blaney (john finch), a sad-sack and impoverished london-based former military man who is accused of sexually assaulting his ex-wife, brenda (barbara leigh-hunt), and using a necktie to strangle her to death. However, the necktie is connected to a string of other murders that have been committed all over the city, as the real killer is Richard's creepy friend Bob Rusk (Barry Foster).

Diungkapkan bahwa as with so many other alfred hitchcock movies, the main character in "frenzy" becomes a falsely accused man on the run (see also: "the wrong man," "stage fright," "the 39 steps," "young and innocent," "north by northwest," "saboteur," "i confess"), and he has to elude capture to clear his name. Along the way, Richard ends up finding an ally and lover in his former co-worker Babs (Anna Massey). although, with Rusk still engaged in his murderous shenanigans, that doesn't bode well for her.

Sebagaimana diketahui, hitchcock films excel at making audiences unwittingly root for the bad guy (see "dial m for murder" and "psycho" for two better-known examples), and "frenzy" includes a sequence where rusk has to retrieve a personal item of his from a victim whose body he has already disposed of. Because of this, viewers are forced to watch as he struggles with the tension of having to retrieve the incriminating evidence, and while we might not feel sympathy for Rusk, we do become involved in his plight. (It's one of the most noteworthy scenes in Hitchcock's filmography. ) You can see, then, why Richard turns to Rusk for help at one point, not knowing that his friend is the murderer.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the final act of "frenzy" gets a little involved and maybe spins a little too far off with its trials and prison sentences, but know that the ultimate conclusion is very satisfying. It's a tonally unique movie as well, feeling very loose and 1970s-y. And where many of Hitchcock's previous films felt mannered and polite despite involving murder and fetishes, "Frenzy" is comparatively casual, focusing more on Rusk's overcooked murderous mindset and the sexual element of his killing spree.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, what many cineastes saw as the sexual subtext of alfred hitchcock's previous movies becomes text in "frenzy. " By the 1970s, the filmmaker could afford to be a little more frank. There's even one particularly memorable shot in "Frenzy" of one of Rusk's victims, freshly dead, with her eyes wide and her tongue lolling out, that will remain in your nightmares for quite some time. This is not the balletic, aesthetic, obfuscated violence of Hitchcock's earlier movies. The murder scenes, more so than in any other Hitchcock movie, "Psycho" included, are brutal and unsettling. This is disturbing.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, many critics responded very positively to "frenzy" at the time. Roger Ebert gave the film four stars (out of four), writing that it was both a departure for Hitchcock and a return to form. As he put it:.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "this is the kind of thriller hitchcock was making in the 1940s, filled with macabre details, incongruous humor, and the desperation of a man convicted of a crime he didn't commit. It's almost as if Hitchcock, at seventy-three, was consciously attempting to do once again what he did better than anyone else. The only 1970s details are the violence and the nudity (both approached with a certain grisly abandon that has us imagining 'Psycho' without the shower curtain). ".

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, ebert added that "frenzy" possesses a nice macabre sense of humor, another feature hitchcock's fans appreciate from the master. (There's a reason we here at /Film once listed it as one of Hitchcock's 20 best movies. Vincent Canby, writing for the New York Times, listed "Frenzy" as one of the 10 best films of its year, and it was a hit at the box office to boot. ) Clearly, Hitchcock hadn't lost his talent for snagging audiences.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, cupertino is already doing well in the ratings, ensuring that the era of network television is far from over. The Kings are continuing to demonstrate their genius when it comes to crafting stories that feel inherently captivating, and we can't wait to see what else Cupertino tackles in the courtroom.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, but chekov knowing khan is the kind of detail that evidently slipped by bennett. I chose survival as opposed to ethics. Altman: "I was faced with the ethical dilemma of mentioning it to Bennett or letting it go. As Koenig put it when interviewed in "The Fifty-Year Mission: The First 25 Years" by Edward Gross and Mark A. Koenig, who was asked to read the script and give it a "Trekkie read," had a vested interest in not pointing out the mistake. ".

Diungkapkan bahwa chekov is the only member of the "star trek" main cast who shares physical screentime with khan in the movie. ) It's also Khan's first appearance in the movie, as well as the scene from "Wrath of Khan" that I rewatch the most in isolation. Diungkapkan bahwa for koenig's part, his cheeky theory to explain away this inconsistency was that chekov once made khan wait an uncomfortable amount of time to use the enterprise's restroom. "Chekov was on the Enterprise, just offscreen" has become the go-to fanon answer. The novel "To Reign in Hell: The Exile of Khan Noonien Singh" by Greg Cox legitimizes that; Chekov is said to have led a failed effort to retake the Enterprise from Khan, and is part of the detachment that helps Khan and his people get settled on Ceti Alpha V.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, despite the continuity gap with "space seed," chekov was the best pick among the main characters as the one captured by khan. The Enterprise can function without him in a way it wouldn't without Spock (Leonard Nimoy) or Dr. Amusingly, this is precisely because he's the most ancillary one. McCoy (DeForest Kelley).

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, while koenig evidently feared that they would swap chekov's part out in the script, the only other main character who could work would be uhura (nichelle nichols), which would add some icky subtext to khan violating her body with the ceti eels, or sulu (george takei). With Sulu, you run into the same problem because he wasn't in "Space Seed" either! While Sulu/Takei was part of the show in Season 1, he was absent for that particular episode. Walter Koenig may have created a small problem in "Wrath of Khan" by staying silent here, but he helped fix a much bigger one, too, by suggesting moving Spock's death to the end of the film.

We’ve already begun receiving offers of help today, and that support will continue. It’s hard to even believe what has happened,” Felipe Minambres told reporters after de Miguel died. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “we are deeply affected by what has happened and we share the pain that the club is experiencing,” a statement read. “From the very beginning we have maintained contact with them and we are at their disposal for anything they may need. Kate Middleton Announces First Major Trip Since Her Cancer Diagnosis

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, in unexpected news, kensington palace has just announced that kate middleton will accompany prince william on his upcoming three-day official visit to mumbai, india. The trip, which commences on Monday, will mark their first joint tour outside the United Kingdom in the past four years and represents a new milestone in Kate Middleton’s gradual return to public duties since she was diagnosed with cancer in early 2024 and began scaling back her official engagements.

Last May, the princess made a brief solo trip to Italy to learn about early childhood development, but this trip to India (a nine-hour flight from London) represents her first long-distance journey and her highest-profile diplomatic engagement since the Caribbean tour she undertook in 2022 and the Earthshot Awards gala she attended in Boston that same year.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "so proud, i'm very, very proud. She's been amazing. She's been through so much in the last couple of years, particularly," William shared on UK radio show Heart Breakfast in May, pleased to see that Kate was “gradually resuming” her travels. "Away trips like that take a lot out of you," he explained. "So we have to balance that, make sure she's, she's OK and rested, but she's in good form. Still, the heir to the throne wanted to be cautious and warned that these visits are very taxing. ".

The royal couple at the 2022 Earthshot Prize ceremony in Boston, their most recent joint trip abroad to date.

The reason for the visit is the sixth edition of the Earthshot Prize, an initiative spearheaded by the heir to the British throne that each year awards one million pounds (about $1,323,249) to five innovative environmental projects and which, after making stops in other cities abroad such as Singapore, Cape Town, and Rio de Janeiro, is now taking place in the country that has produced the most finalists and winners in the competition’s history.

Berdasarkan laporan, standout finalists this year include mahindra last mile mobility, for its fleet of electric motorcycle taxis designed to reduce urban pollution, and mahila housing trust, which installs reflective roofs capable of lowering the temperature inside homes by up to five degrees during extreme heat. The awards ceremony will be held this Tuesday evening at the Jio World Centre in Mumbai and will feature a performance by the band Take That and be attended by celebrities such as actor Rami Malek.

William and Kate during their 2016 visit to the Taj Mahal.

Diungkapkan bahwa hours before the main event, the prince and princess of wales will also preside over the first edition of the earthshot children’s awards, a competition in which 15,000 schools from 24 indian states have participated with environmental proposals designed by young people aged 9 to 17. The itinerary also includes a solo appearance by Kate Middleton, meetings with the Bollywood film industry, cricket-related celebrations, and a possible meeting with Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi.

Diungkapkan bahwa in addition to being a positive sign regarding the princess’s health, this return to india holds strong symbolic significance for the couple, who last visited the country in april 2016. On that occasion, the then-Duke and Duchess of Cambridge visited the Taj Mahal and posed on the same white marble bench where Princess Diana was photographed alone in 1992—an image that has gone down in history as a reflection of the breakdown of her marriage to the now-King Charles III.

#1098. 8 Must-Play Open-World RPGs for People With Real-Life Schedules

8 Must-Play Open-World RPGs for People With Real-Life Schedules

Tanggal: 15 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.polygon.com/open-world-rpgs-real-life-schedules/

These maps will be there for you when you’re ready.

Berdasarkan laporan, raise your hand if this has ever happened to you: a friend texts you a screenshot of a map with 400 icons on it and the message “you’re going to love this game. Until you check your calendar and remember that you’ve got a dentist appointment, three work deadlines, and a birthday dinner to prepare for, so that map is going to have to stay unexplored for a minute. ” You’re excited — the map is detailed, the game looks great, and you do love it…for about 10 seconds. (My hand is raised. ).

Sebagaimana diketahui, if you’re looking for open-world rpgs you can actually play with a busy schedule, start here. These eight games range from true open-world adventures you can finish in a few weekends to RPG giants like Mass Effect that can be made manageable if you play them one mission at a time. Remember this: Keep it to just one quest tonight. The rest of the map will still be there when you get back.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, two kings walk into a war. One has whiskers. One has a wagging tail. Neither wants to be there. Cat Quest 2 is a 2D open-world action RPG set in a fantasy realm of cats and dogs where those kings are brought together against their will during a war between the cats of Felingard and the advancing dogs of the Lupus Empire, and both of them want their thrones back. The humor — as you might expect — leans on delightfully pun-heavy wordplay.

Berdasarkan laporan, you can play solo by swapping between the canine and feline heroes whenever you like, or play in local co-op, where each player takes one animal. Fast travel keeps the map from eating your entire night, so you can chain a few quests and stop when dinner is ready. Grab nearby quests before you enter a dungeon, since many dungeons have quests attached and nobody wants to make the trip twice.

Berdasarkan laporan, let’s say you have half an hour, a fishing boat, and you’ve just noticed there’s something odd in the water. Dredge is a sinister fishing adventure that casts you as a down-on-their-luck fisherman exploring an eerie archipelago. After your boat wrecks near the island town of Greater Marrow, you get a replacement vessel…and a debt to pay off. Days are for fishing and selling, but at night, strange things start to happen on the water. The day-night cycle gives you a built-in stopping point: Head back to port when the light fades, sleep, sell your catch, and spend the money on upgrades to your vessel, skills, and knowledge. Think of this as an open-world game that’s made mostly of ocean: There’s always an island in the distance hiding a secret, and you get to pick which one to sail to next.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, a calm british narrator tells you the whole story of biomutant. It is an open-world, post-apocalyptic Kung-Fu RPG where you create a gene-spliced hero in a world with a Tree of Life at its center. Your task: Pick a faction, and then do something about those World Eaters. This can be deceptive, since Biomutant is not a calm story. Four World Eaters are killing that all-important tree. There’s also a war brewing among the tribes dotting this world, and they disagree about what to do with the dying tree. The Myriad want to unite the tribes and save it, while the Jagni want to crush their rivals and bring it down. New Game+ unlocks after the credits and lets you ally with any of the six tribes from the start, which makes a second run a good excuse to try the path you skipped.

Sebagaimana diketahui, you awake on a beach on an island called new wirral. You’ve been transported from Earth, and all you’ve got on you is a cassette player that grants you the ability to turn into various monsters. Cassette Beasts is a monster-fusing open-world RPG with turn-based battles. Your goal is to get back home with help from the other stranded people on the island. Good luck!.

Sebagaimana diketahui, that cassette player will be extremely helpful: in addition to becoming a monster yourself, when that feels appropriate, you can fuse monsters in combat to create whatever the moment needs. (There are over 14,000 possible fusions!) After a short tutorial, you’re free to wander in any direction, choose your fights, and skirt around any that you’d rather skip. Pro tip: Campfires let you rest and serve as a return point after you save, so make one before you quit for the night.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the gods of olympus are in prison. Zelda fans will also appreciate the Vaults of Tartaros, puzzle chambers scattered across the island. Navigating one (or more) gives you a clean goal for a single gaming session. It’s got a flexible gear system with enough complexity to tweak your playstyle without overwhelming you, plus new skill tree paths to unlock. It borrows a lot of its free-feeling vibe from games like Breath of the Wild; there is a lot of climbing in this game. The hero sent to free them — you, but no pressure — is a winged mortal named Fenyx. Immortals Fenyx Rising sets you loose on the Golden Isle, a vast open world of puzzles, cliffs to glide from, and monsters to fight. Fair warning: Every upgrade you get does feed into an “I’ll play for just a bit longer” loop, so determine your goals and decide when you’re going to stop before you start.

Berdasarkan laporan, a weekly cheat sheet to what you’ll eventually love to play. No buying, no commitment — just saving for later.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, sea of stars has a world that feels simultaneously pocket-sized and expansive — and it’s packed with small delights to discover, even if it doesn't start out wide open. You play Valere and Zale, two Children of the Solstice fated to become Solstice Warriors, who fuse solar and lunar powers into Eclipse Magic to stop an evil alchemist called the Fleshmancer. The game takes inspiration from Chrono Trigger and even features music by the same composer, Yasunori Mitsuda.

Sebagaimana diketahui, early on, the overworld does parcel out exploration in set routes, but as your characters grow and gain powers, you’ll get a boat, faster ways to travel, and more freedom to roam the world. The story is a heartfelt tale of friendship, which keeps the mood approachable even when the world is in danger. That’s a good thing, because there’s so much to poke at: a card game called Wheels, fishing, cooking, a crypt honoring the game’s backers, and hidden chests. Dungeon puzzles rarely ask you to stop and think for more than a few seconds, side quests are sparse, and a friendly character usually tells you where to go next, so you can return after a week away and still know your next move.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, there are 120 shrines nestled into the rolling green hills and treacherous fire pits of hyrule. They’re all self-contained, with a little reward at the end. Each usually takes between ten minutes and an hour (if you’re dealing with a trickier puzzle). This is the trick to playing Breath of the Wild, an admittedly gigantic and overwhelming game, on a schedule: Pick a shrine, clear it, do one or two things nearby that seem fun, and call it a day.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, in this game, link wakes up after 100 years with no memories, and a spirit tells him that princess zelda has been holding back calamity ganon the whole time. On paper it’s an open-world action-adventure, but its systems have a lot in common with an RPG. Each shrine you clear earns a Spirit Orb, and you can trade four orbs for an extra heart or a boost to your stamina, so every shrine works like a small level-up. Try not to get distracted as you get stronger and do more things, though. You cook meals and elixirs that grant bonuses such as extra strength or weather resistance, and your weapons and shields wear out, which keeps your loadout changing as you go. One shrine, one quick sidequest, that’s it — Hyrule will be there waiting for you next time.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, think of mass effect as a tv series with a great cast: every mission is an episode, every crewmate gets a loyalty mission of their own, and the story stays easy to leave and come back to at the end of any one of them. Mass Effect: Andromeda is the series’ open-world chapter. Each explorable planet is open-world, with its own hazards such as radiation, heat, and cold. If you’re looking for a galaxy to roam at your own pace, this one does reward patience. After a 600-year journey to the Heleus Cluster, you play Ryder, who inherits the role of Pathfinder. Stay the course on your first planet, Eos, since radiation will kill you if you wander off it, and skip the repetitive “tasks,” like mineral scanning, until you’re in the mood.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, if you’d rather have tighter, mission-by-mission storytelling, start with the first three mass effect games instead. The original trilogy isn’t open-world in the strictest sense, but its missions are episodic, and the first game even lets you explore planets in the Mako when you have time and skip them when you don’t. Or two. Whatever you have time for. Play one mission per night. The Normandy will wait.

Fans and developers remain confident that Mass Effect will return.

Sebagaimana diketahui, we want to hear from you. Share your perspective in the comments below, and please keep the conversation respectful.

Berdasarkan laporan, interesting list. Very interesting. Is this someone's personal favorite list? Because there are some seriously questionable picks on it.

Dredge is awesome! An excellent take on the "cosmic horror drowned in the ocean" trope.

Did they ever patch Immortals Fenyx Rising to remove the Ubisoft account requirement on consoles? Seriously stupid requirement for a single player game.
